title: Formalizing the Hindley–Milner Type Inference Algorithm in Coq with a Completeness Proof
abstract: Hindley–Milner type inference is the basis of type systems in languages such as ML and Haskell. While the soundness of the algorithm is discussed in most textbooks, completeness—the fact that the algorithm finds the most general type—is harder to prove and is often omitted from mechanized treatments. This paper presents a full Coq formalization of Algorithm W including both soundness and completeness. The formalization uses a constraint-based presentation in which unification is factored out and verified separately as a rewriting system on finite trees. Completeness is stated as: if a term has any type in the Damas–Milner type system, then Algorithm W returns a substitution that is at least as general. The proof involves a detailed induction over the derivation structure and requires 38 auxiliary lemmas. The total proof is 5 100 lines of Coq 8.9. A worked example traces type inference for a small polymorphic program through every step of the formalization.
venue: Journal of Automated Reasoning

title: Dependent Types as a Specification Language for Numeric Algorithms: A Case Study in Matrix Multiplication
abstract: Dependent type systems can express fine-grained correctness conditions directly in types, making it possible to state and prove algorithmic properties without writing separate logical specifications. We use this capability to specify and verify a straightforward matrix-multiplication algorithm in Agda, where matrix dimensions are carried as type indices and the result type statically enforces dimensional compatibility. Beyond dimensional correctness, we encode the algebraic property that the result equals the mathematical matrix product over a commutative ring, and prove this property for both a naive cubic algorithm and a block-decomposed variant. The block-decomposed proof reuses the naive algorithm's correctness lemma recursively. We measure proof effort in terms of lines and proof steps and compare the approach with a standalone Coq proof using a separate specification predicate. The Agda intrinsic approach requires 22 % fewer lines for the equivalent theorems at the cost of more constrained type signatures.
venue: Electronic Notes in Theoretical Informatics and Computer Science

title: Towards a Certified Compiler for a Subset of Rust: Ownership Types in Coq
abstract: Rust's ownership and borrowing model prevents data races and use-after-free errors by construction but is complex enough that certified-compilation work has largely avoided it. This paper reports on an initial formalization of a small Rust-like language, called MicroRust, in Coq 8.13. MicroRust supports mutable and immutable borrows, move semantics, and basic lifetimes but excludes closures and traits. We define a type system for MicroRust that enforces single ownership and borrow exclusivity, prove type soundness via progress and preservation, and define a translation to a low-level language without ownership annotations. The translation is proved to be a backward simulation: every behavior of the target is a behavior of the source. The current formalization is 7 800 lines and covers programs up to 200 lines of MicroRust. We discuss the main obstacles encountered when encoding lifetime constraints as de Bruijn-indexed region variables.
venue: Proceedings of the European Symposium on Programming (ESOP 2022)

title: A Survey of Mechanized Semantics for Intermediate Representations Used in Production Compilers
abstract: Several production compilers—including GCC, LLVM, and CompCert—rely on one or more intermediate representations (IRs) as the backbone of their optimization pipelines. Formalizing the semantics of these IRs in a proof assistant is a prerequisite for certified compilation work, but the landscape of existing formalizations is fragmented and difficult to navigate. This chapter surveys mechanized semantics for six IRs drawn from the literature: three register-transfer-level IRs, an SSA-form IR, a continuation-passing-style IR, and a typed bytecode IR. For each, we summarize the semantic model used (operational, denotational, or axiomatic), the proof assistant and its version, the scope of verified properties, and the known limitations. We identify five recurring technical challenges and discuss how different formalizations address or sidestep them. The survey covers 24 papers published between 2005 and 2023 and is intended as an entry point for researchers beginning work on certified compilation.

title: Certifying Dataflow Analyses for a Static Analyzer: From Coq Proofs to Extracted C Code
abstract: Static analyzers that detect runtime errors in C programs rely on dataflow analyses whose correctness is critical but rarely formally verified. This paper describes the verification of three dataflow analyses—reaching definitions, live variables, and interval analysis—for a small but realistic subset of C, including pointers and loops. All three analyses are formalized as instances of a generic Galois-connection-based abstract interpretation framework in Coq 8.18. The generic framework is proved sound once; each analysis instantiates it and proves that its transfer functions are monotone with respect to the relevant abstract lattice. The verified analyses are then extracted to OCaml and linked against a hand-written parser to form a prototype analyzer. On a benchmark of 80 programs drawn from embedded-systems code, the extracted analyzer reproduces all 214 warnings produced by a reference implementation and raises no false negatives relative to the reference. Extraction and compilation take under 3 seconds.
venue: Proceedings of the International Symposium on Static Analysis (SAS 2026)

title: Sensitivity Bounds for Linear Queries on Partitioned Statistical Databases
abstract: This paper examines global and local sensitivity of linear aggregate queries executed over horizontally partitioned relational databases. We derive closed-form upper bounds for query sensitivity as a function of partition cardinality and attribute domain width, and show that these bounds are tight for a class of sum and count queries. The analysis uses elementary combinatorial arguments and applies to both exact and approximate differential privacy formulations. We validate the bounds empirically using a synthetic population dataset of 500,000 records partitioned across eight virtual nodes. Results show that our bounds reduce required Laplace noise by 12–18% compared to the standard global sensitivity baseline in all tested query families. The work provides a foundation for calibrating noise mechanisms in distributed query systems without requiring full database access at a central point.
venue: Journal of Mathematical Foundations of Computing

title: Fleet Assignment Under Stochastic Travel Times: A Chance-Constrained Formulation for the Multi-Depot Case
abstract: The paper formulates the multi-depot fleet assignment problem under stochastic travel times as a chance-constrained mixed-integer programme. Travel time distributions on each arc are estimated from six months of GPS data and approximated as log-normal. The chance constraint requires that the probability of a vehicle violating its depot return time does not exceed 5 %. Two solution strategies are compared: sample average approximation with 200 scenarios and a deterministic equivalent obtained by replacing stochastic arcs with their 95th-percentile values. On a test bed of 48 instances derived from a regional food distribution network with three depots and 12 to 24 vehicles, sample average approximation yields solutions 4.1 % less conservative in total fleet cost than the deterministic equivalent, at the expense of roughly four times longer computation. The model is implemented in Python using an open-source MILP solver.
venue: Transportation Research Record: Journal of the Transportation Research Board

title: Time-of-Day Variation in Public Transport Accessibility: Evidence from Continuous Isochrone Sampling
abstract: Most accessibility studies use one or two representative departure times, potentially masking large intra-day variation. This paper samples 30-minute isochrone areas from a fixed set of 50 residential origin points in Novi Sad at every 10-minute interval between 05:00 and 23:00 on weekdays, Saturdays, and Sundays, using a GTFS feed validated against on-board passenger counts from autumn 2017. The resulting dataset contains 8,280 isochrone polygons. Results show that the coefficient of variation in reachable area across departure times exceeds 0.45 for origins in outer districts, compared with 0.18 for origins near the main corridor. Sunday midday accessibility in peripheral zones is on average 41% lower than weekday peak accessibility. The paper provides a methodological template and openly releases the sampling scripts and aggregated isochrone dataset under a CC-BY licence.
venue: Journal of Transport Geography

title: Systematic Identification of Human Action Initiating Events in HAZOP Studies for Automated Process Plants
abstract: Automated process plants retain a significant number of manual operations — sampling, bypass switching, filter cleaning — that can initiate hazardous process deviations not captured by standard HAZOP guide words applied to piping and instrumentation diagrams. This book chapter reviews procedures for supplementing conventional HAZOP with human reliability analysis (HRA) to ensure completeness of the initiating event inventory. The chapter draws on three case studies from Serbian and Hungarian process industries covering a solvent recovery unit, a gas compression station, and a polymer blending facility. For each case, task analysis was used to enumerate manual operations, and the THERP method was used to estimate human error probabilities, which were then incorporated as additional initiating events in the HAZOP worksheets. The integrated approach increased the number of identified initiating events by 18 to 27% across the three cases and led to additional independent protection layer requirements in two of the three LOPA studies that followed.

title: Functional Safety Assessment of a Retrofit PLC-Based Safety Instrumented System Replacing a Relay Logic Panel
abstract: Relay logic panels in older process plants are increasingly being replaced by programmable logic controller-based safety instrumented systems to reduce maintenance burden and extend plant life. This paper documents the full IEC 61511 safety lifecycle assessment for such a retrofit at a Vojvodina sugar production facility, where a 42-relay panel controlling steam drum protection was replaced by a two-channel IEC 61508-compliant safety PLC. The assessment covers hazard identification, SIL determination by risk graph, SIL verification by simplified equations, functional logic review, and factory acceptance testing. PFD for the final SIS configuration was calculated at 4.3 × 10⁻³, confirming SIL 1 compliance with margin. The paper also documents lessons learned regarding the management of change process, specifically the challenge of re-validating cause-and-effect logic when the original relay panel documentation was incomplete. A structured documentation recovery procedure involving loop testing and tracing is described.

title: Automated HAZOP Node Decomposition from P&ID Graph Representations Using a Rule-Based Parser
abstract: Manual HAZOP preparation — extracting nodes, process parameters, and design intentions from piping and instrumentation diagrams — is time-consuming and depends on facilitator experience. This paper describes a rule-based parser that ingests vectorised P&ID data in ISO 10628-2 symbol format and automatically decomposes the diagram into HAZOP nodes together with candidate process parameters and control loop references. The parser was implemented in Python and tested against four P&IDs from an ammonia refrigeration system, ranging in complexity from 18 to 61 instrument tags. Automatic node proposals agreed with expert-defined nodes in 83% of cases; disagreements arose primarily at interfaces between heat exchanger circuits and their associated control loops. The tool also generates a preliminary cause-consequence seed list derived from propagation rules encoded from IEC 61882 Annex D. Integration with a commercial HAZOP worksheet software package is described. The paper does not claim to replace experienced HAZOP facilitators but characterises the workload reduction achievable in the preparation phase.

title: Diagnostic Coverage Estimation for Smart Positioners on Pneumatic Rotary Valves: Field Data from Five Years of Operation
abstract: Smart positioners equipped with valve signature diagnostics are marketed as providing diagnostic coverage sufficient to support SIL 2 claims for pneumatic rotary valve assemblies, but independent field assessments of the actual diagnostic coverage achieved in service are scarce. This paper analyses five years of diagnostic alarm and maintenance records from 67 butterfly and ball valves fitted with smart positioners at two process plants in the Pannonian region. Maintenance records were cross-referenced with positioner diagnostic outputs to classify each corrective maintenance event as detected or undetected by the positioner diagnostics prior to the maintenance trigger. Observed diagnostic coverage ranged from 0.61 to 0.88 across valve types and service conditions, with lower values associated with high-cycle services and abrasive media. For seven valves in high-pressure gas service, the positioner failed to detect developing seat leakage until process measurements indicated a deviation. The paper provides a disaggregated coverage dataset by failure mode category that can be used directly in IEC 61511 PFD calculations.

title: Aerodynamic Disturbance Compensation in Multirotor UAVs: Methods, Limitations, and Open Problems
abstract: This chapter reviews approaches for compensating aerodynamic disturbances in multirotor UAV control systems, covering the period from the emergence of commercial autopilots around 2010 to the early 2020s. The chapter is organised around four disturbance categories: steady crosswind, low-frequency gusts, high-frequency turbulence, and rotor-induced aerodynamic coupling. For each category, representative compensation strategies are described—feedforward from onboard anemometry, model-based disturbance observers, adaptive and robust controllers, and learning-based methods—with attention to the implementation constraints imposed by onboard computational resources. A recurring theme is the conflict between disturbance rejection bandwidth and actuator authority limits, especially in payload-carrying UAVs. The chapter closes with a discussion of open problems, including the absence of standardised outdoor wind disturbance test protocols, the difficulty of validating rotor wake models above 12 m/s, and the gap between laboratory controller performance and in-field reliability. Approximately 140 references are synthesised.

title: Embedded implementation of a kinematic recalibration algorithm on a real-time robot controller platform
abstract: Moving kinematic recalibration algorithms from an external PC to the embedded controller of an industrial robot reduces latency, eliminates communication overhead, and simplifies integration into existing cells. This paper describes the porting of a previously published extended Kalman filter recalibration algorithm to a real-time Linux platform running on the controller hardware of a six-axis robot. The implementation uses fixed-point arithmetic for the filter prediction step and floating-point only for the infrequent update step triggered by laser tracker measurements. Execution time per filter cycle was reduced from 18 ms on a desktop PC to 6 ms on the embedded platform, comfortably within the 10 ms control loop period. Numerical equivalence between the embedded and desktop implementations was verified to within 1×10⁻⁵ mm over 10,000 test epochs. Integration into the robot's existing joint offset update mechanism required modification of 340 lines of controller firmware. Field validation over 30 eight-hour shifts confirmed that embedded and external implementations produced statistically indistinguishable TCP error distributions.

title: Gear diagnostics in planetary drives: signal processing and simulation methods
abstract: This book chapter reviews the signal processing and computational simulation approaches used for diagnostics in planetary gearboxes, covering synchronous averaging, cepstrum analysis, time-frequency methods, and multi-body torsional dynamics modelling. The chapter discusses the practical challenges of sensor placement on rotating carriers, reference signal acquisition for order tracking, and the selection of appropriate diagnostic indices for different failure modes including pitting, spalling, and tooth fracture. Example results from laboratory gearbox experiments at two test facilities are used to illustrate each method. The chapter concludes with a discussion of current limitations, including the difficulty of separating overlapping mesh harmonics when the number of planet gears changes the sideband spacing, and directions for combining physics-based models with data-driven approaches.

title: Polypyrrole–MnO₂ composite electrodes deposited on laser-perforated stainless-steel mesh: capacitance and rate performance
abstract: Laser perforation was used to introduce a regular array of 120 µm diameter holes in type-316 stainless-steel mesh current collectors, increasing the geometric surface area by 34% as verified by profilometry. Polypyrrole–MnO₂ composites were then deposited on both perforated and unperforated meshes under identical potentiostatic conditions. Mass loading was controlled gravimetrically and held constant at 1.8 mg cm⁻² for all samples. Cyclic voltammetry in 0.5 M Na₂SO₄ at scan rates from 2 to 100 mV s⁻¹ showed that perforated-mesh electrodes retained 71% of their 5 mV s⁻¹ capacitance (440 F g⁻¹) at 100 mV s⁻¹, compared with 52% retention for unperforated counterparts. EIS-derived ion diffusion coefficients were 1.8× higher for perforated electrodes, consistent with improved electrolyte access through the holes. After 3000 charge–discharge cycles at 3 A g⁻¹, the perforated electrodes retained 83% of initial capacitance versus 74% for the reference. The laser-perforation approach is simple, scalable, and compatible with existing roll-to-roll processing.

title: Co-crystal formation between furosemide and three pyridine derivatives: structural inference from PXRD and Raman spectroscopy in the absence of single-crystal data
abstract: Three co-crystals of furosemide (a poorly soluble loop diuretic) with 2-aminopyridine, 3-hydroxypyridine, and 4,4′-bipyridine were prepared by LAG with acetonitrile and characterised entirely in polycrystalline form. Single crystals suitable for X-ray diffraction could not be grown from any of the nine solvent systems attempted. Structural inference relied on indexing of PXRD patterns (DICVOL06 and TREOR90 algorithms), lattice parameter comparison with Cambridge Structural Database entries, and Raman band shifts. The carbonyl stretch of furosemide at 1678 cm⁻¹ shifted to 1663 cm⁻¹ in the 2-aminopyridine co-crystal, consistent with N–H···O hydrogen bonding. Quantitative phase analysis of DSC data confirmed 1:1 stoichiometry for all three co-crystals by molar enthalpy comparison. Dissolution experiments in simulated intestinal fluid (FaSSIF) at 37 °C showed 1.5-, 1.9-, and 1.3-fold increases in maximum dissolved concentration for the three co-crystals, respectively. The 3-hydroxypyridine co-crystal showed a spring-and-parachute effect with maximum concentration maintained for 120 minutes.

title: Predicting cumulative estrogenic burden in dairy cow diets: a scoring model validated against urinary biomarkers in Vojvodina farms
abstract: No practical on-farm tool currently integrates multiple estrogenic feed inputs into a unified risk score. Using data collected from 22 farms over two years, we developed a cumulative estrogenic burden (CEB) score that combines standardised contributions from dietary ZEN, formononetin, daidzein, coumestrol, and cypermethrin, weighted by their relative binding affinities to the bovine estrogen receptor-α derived from published Ki values. The CEB score was validated against urinary α-ZOL and estradiol-17β in 220 cows. Linear regression of urinary α-ZOL on CEB score yielded R² = 0.54 (p < 0.001); inclusion of herd random effects improved fit (marginal R² = 0.49, conditional R² = 0.68). CEB score quartile membership was significantly associated with FSCR in a secondary analysis (Q4 vs. Q1: OR 0.44; p = 0.003). A simplified spreadsheet implementation of the model, requiring only routine feed analysis data, was tested by three Vojvodina veterinary practitioners and rated as feasible in field conditions. The model requires prospective validation in wider farm populations.

title: Floor-level and ceiling-level wayfinding cues: visibility from wheelchair and walking-frame user eye heights
abstract: Standard-height wall-mounted signage is designed for standing adult eye heights (approximately 1.55–1.70 m) and may be partially or fully outside the useful visual field of wheelchair users (eye height approximately 1.20 m) and walking-frame users who adopt a forward-inclined posture (functional eye height approximately 0.95–1.10 m). This study measured detection and identification distances for wall-mounted signs at three installation heights (1.0 m, 1.5 m, 2.1 m) for 22 wheelchair users and 18 walking-frame users recruited at rehabilitation and geriatric wards. Detection distance for signs at 1.0 m was significantly greater for wheelchair users than for walking-frame users (p = 0.008). Floor-applied vinyl wayfinding strips were also tested; identification of the destination label was not possible beyond 2.5 m for any participant group due to perspective distortion. Dual-height mounting at 1.0 m and 1.5 m is recommended for facilities serving high proportions of mobility-impaired users.

title: The Language of Damage: Environmental Metaphor in Niger Delta Poetry and Prose
abstract: This study undertakes a systematic metaphor analysis of environmental language in a corpus of 14 texts—eight poetry collections and six prose works—produced by writers associated with or originating from the Niger Delta between 1995 and 2018. Using conceptual metaphor theory as operationalised by Zoltán Kövecses, the study codes 387 discrete metaphorical expressions relating to ecological harm across the corpus. The analysis identifies three dominant source domains: the human body, kinship structures, and legal-juridical discourse. The body metaphor cluster is quantitatively most frequent, appearing in 44 percent of coded instances, and is distributed equally across poetry and prose genres. The legal-juridical cluster increases markedly in texts produced after 2005, which the study correlates with the rise of international environmental-rights litigation involving multinational oil companies and Delta communities. The paper argues that metaphor analysis provides a complement to thematic ecocriticism by making visible patterns of conceptualisation that close reading alone may not surface systematically.

title: Climate Precarity and the Realist Novel: Form and Ecology in Three West African Texts of the 2000s
abstract: This article examines how three West African realist novels published in the 2000s manage the representational challenge of depicting slow-onset climate impacts—seasonal irregularity, coastal erosion, and aquifer depletion—within narrative forms developed primarily to depict social relations between persons. The theoretical framework draws on Fredric Jameson's account of realism as the formal articulation of social contradiction, adapted here to argue that the ecological subject matter introduces a contradiction between the realist novel's anthropocentric focalization conventions and the nonhuman temporal scales required to narrate climate change. The article performs detailed structural analyses of three novels, tracking chapter-by-chapter shifts in narrative time, setting, and perspectival distance. It identifies a recurring technique—brief shifts to an omniscient, deep-time perspective embedded within otherwise close third-person narration—as a formal response to the temporal mismatch. The study positions these texts within current debates on the 'climate novel' without treating that category as a fixed generic label.

title: Postcolonial Ecocriticism in the Classroom: Approaches to Teaching West African Environmental Fiction at Central and East European Universities
abstract: This article reports on a curriculum development initiative carried out between 2020 and 2022 at three universities in Serbia, Hungary, and Poland, in which postcolonial environmental fiction from West Africa was introduced into existing English literature survey courses. The paper describes the design rationale, the selection of primary texts, and the pedagogical problems encountered. Structured student feedback was collected through written reflections and two focus-group sessions totalling 34 participants across the three institutions. Analysis of student responses reveals consistent patterns: students found environmental themes more accessible entry points than political or historical contexts, but struggled to situate the texts within West African geographical and social specifics they had limited prior knowledge of. The article proposes a set of contextualisation strategies—including the use of documentary film excerpts and edited maps—that proved effective in pilot implementation. It also reflects on the challenge of teaching texts whose environmental referents (mangrove ecosystems, savanna agriculture) are largely unfamiliar to Central and East European students.
venue: Teaching Postcolonial Literatures: An International Journal

title: Coastal Futures: Sea-Level Narratives in Recent Nigerian and Ghanaian Fiction
abstract: This article examines six novels published between 2014 and 2023 that represent communities on the Nigerian and Ghanaian coasts confronting erosion, saltwater intrusion into farmland, and the gradual inundation of low-lying settlements. The study reads these texts against IPCC regional projections for the Gulf of Guinea coast and published reports from the West African Science Service Centre on Climate Change and Adapted Land Use (WASCAL), not to judge the novels' scientific accuracy but to understand what the texts select and emphasise from available environmental knowledge. Close reading is supported by a spatial analysis of the texts using hand-coded mental map reconstructions of each novel's fictional geography. The article identifies a consistent formal feature: the use of a child narrator or child focalizer to represent coastal futures, a choice that encodes uncertainty and vulnerability in the narrative voice itself rather than in explicit commentary. The article contributes to ongoing discussions of African climate fiction and its relationship to global anglophone climate-writing.

title: Extraction, Silence, and Narrative Authority in the Fiction of the Postcolonial Resource Frontier
abstract: This book chapter contributes to an edited volume on resource extraction and narrative form across postcolonial literatures. The chapter focuses on Anglophone West African fiction but situates it comparatively within a broader argument the volume makes about how resource extraction generates particular silences and evasions in literary representation. The chapter examines five novels from Nigeria, Liberia, and Sierra Leone in which diamond, gold, or oil extraction functions as a structuring economic condition but is rarely described directly. Using Mieke Bal's narratological framework, the chapter analyses what is narrated versus what is shown versus what is withheld, mapping the distribution of narrative authority among character voices, implied author, and reader inference. The chapter argues that the indirection of these novels—their reluctance to name extractive processes directly—is not a formal weakness but a historically conditioned rhetorical choice shaped by censorship histories and the dependence of some authors on state cultural institutions.

title: Textbook Representations of European Integration in Serbian Secondary Education
abstract: This book chapter examines how EU accession is portrayed in Serbian social studies and English-language textbooks approved by the Ministry of Education between 2006 and 2012. The corpus consists of 14 textbook chapters drawn from eight titles across three publishers. Critical discourse analysis informed by Fairclough's three-dimensional framework is applied to identify ideological assumptions embedded in definitions, timelines, and exercises. Findings show that accession is consistently presented as a teleological process with a predetermined positive outcome, while alternative political trajectories receive no textual space. Exercises foreground civic compliance rather than critical evaluation of EU institutions. The chapter argues that textbook discourse functions as a secondary socialisation instrument aligning youth identity with a pro-integration orientation, and discusses this in relation to broader state communication strategies during the candidate period.

title: Pragmatic Failure in Written Academic English: A Case Study of Vojvodina Graduate Students
abstract: This study analyses pragmatic failure in academic emails written in English by 98 graduate students enrolled at the University of Novi Sad. Participants were asked to compose emails to a fictional foreign professor requesting an extension of a submission deadline. Texts were evaluated for appropriateness along four dimensions: directness calibration, face-work, conventionally indirect request forms, and closing rituals. A panel of three expert raters scored each email using a rubric developed for the study; inter-rater reliability reached κ = 0.81. Results indicate that 61% of participants produced at least one instance of pragmatic failure, most frequently through omission of pre-request grounders and absence of softening modals. Sociolinguistic background variables, including home language and prior residence abroad, were significant predictors of pragmatic accuracy. Practical recommendations for academic writing courses are discussed.

title: Disagreement Management in L2 English Online Discussion Boards: Vojvodina Student Interactions During Remote Learning
abstract: This study examines how multilingual Vojvodina students manage disagreement in asynchronous English-language discussion boards during the 2020–2021 academic year, a period of enforced remote instruction. A total of 1,842 posts from six online courses across three faculties were collected and coded for disagreement markers, hedging devices, and mitigation sequences. Results show that explicit disagreement openings ('I don't agree that…') occurred in 34% of disagreement turns, a rate higher than comparable online corpora from British and Irish universities. Hedged disagreements using epistemic modal expressions were less frequent than in native-speaker reference data. Negative affect expressions and face-attack sequences increased in posts appearing later in thread chains, suggesting accumulating interactional pressure. The paper discusses implications for moderating academic online discourse in EFL-medium institutions.

title: Warm-Starting ALNS with Machine-Learning Initialisation for Real-Time Rescheduling
abstract: In real-time vehicle rescheduling, the quality of the initial solution fed to a metaheuristic strongly affects final solution quality when computation time is capped at 30–60 seconds. This paper investigates whether a graph neural network (GNN) trained on historical rescheduling instances can produce initial assignments that reduce the number of ALNS iterations needed to reach a target solution quality. The GNN is trained on 4 200 solved instances derived from a regional transport operator's incident log spanning three years. Experiments on a held-out test set of 600 instances show that GNN-initialised ALNS reaches solutions within 1% of a 5-minute ALNS run using only 18 seconds of computation on average, compared to 41 seconds when initialised with a greedy heuristic. The approach is sensitive to distribution shift: performance degrades when incident types in the test set differ substantially from those in training data, which limits transferability without retraining.

title: Experimental validation of a CO₂ transcritical refrigeration test rig at the University of Novi Sad: instrumentation, steady-state protocol, and uncertainty analysis
abstract: This paper documents the small-scale CO₂ transcritical test rig commissioned at the Thermal Systems Laboratory, Faculty of Technical Sciences, Novi Sad. The rig has a nominal cooling capacity of 3.2 kW (MT circuit) with adjustable high-side pressure between 70 bar and 120 bar, controlled via an electronic expansion valve and a back-pressure regulator. Instrumentation consists of eight T-type thermocouples (±0.3 K), four pressure transducers (±0.15 % FS), and a Coriolis mass-flow meter (±0.1 % reading). A GUM-compliant uncertainty analysis gives expanded COP uncertainty of ±4.2 % at a 95 % confidence level. Steady-state validation runs were conducted at ambient temperatures of 25 °C, 30 °C, 35 °C, and 38 °C, with measured COP values of 3.41, 3.08, 2.71, and 2.44 respectively. Simulated values from the EES model deviate by no more than 3.8 % across all conditions. The dataset is made available as supplementary material to support further validation work in the region.

title: Finite Element Limit Analysis of Rainfall-Triggered Slope Failures: Coupling Transient Seepage with Bound Theorems
abstract: Coupling transient seepage analysis with limit analysis allows time-varying safety factors to be computed during a rainfall event without iterative strength-reduction procedures. This paper describes an implementation in which pore pressure fields from a Richards-equation seepage model are passed at successive time steps into upper- and lower-bound FELA, using linear programming with 6-noded triangular elements and discontinuous stress and velocity fields. The procedure is applied to a 12 m cut slope in Fruška Gora marl subjected to a 72-hour design storm derived from frequency analysis of Novi Sad meteorological records (1961–2019). Factors of safety drop from 1.63 (dry antecedent conditions) to 1.08 at 61 hours, with the lower bound trailing the upper bound by less than 6 % throughout the event. The time to critical safety factor is sensitive to initial suction distribution; a 20 % reduction in initial suction advances the critical time by 9 hours. The method is computationally tractable on a standard workstation, completing a 72-step analysis in under 40 minutes.

title: Phenotypic plasticity in metabolic rate of juvenile common carp under chronic moderate hypoxia: acclimation dynamics and reversibility
abstract: Juvenile common carp (mean body mass 12.4 g) originating from a single normoxic-site population were exposed to chronic moderate hypoxia (3 mg O₂/L) or normoxia (8 mg O₂/L) for 10 weeks in flow-through tanks, followed by a six-week recovery period at normoxia. Standard metabolic rate was measured every two weeks using intermittent respirometry. Hypoxia-exposed fish reduced standard metabolic rate by 31% relative to controls by week four, with rates stabilising thereafter. Haematocrit and gill lamellar surface area increased significantly in hypoxia fish by week six. Upon return to normoxia, metabolic rate recovered to control levels within three weeks, but gill morphology showed only partial reversal by week six of recovery. Growth rate was reduced in hypoxia-exposed fish by 18% over the treatment period. Results indicate that gill structural changes are more persistent plastic responses than metabolic rate adjustments, which has implications for interpreting field population data.
venue: Fish Physiology and Biochemistry

title: Transfer factors between substrate bark, epiphytic lichen thallus, and ambient particulate matter for selected trace elements: a comparative field study in Serbia and Hungary
abstract: Transfer factors (TFs) between bark substrate, lichen thallus, and colocated PM10 filter samples were determined for Zn, Cu, Ni, Cd, Pb, and Fe at 18 paired sites across a cross-border transect spanning southern Hungary and northern Serbia. Lichen species sampled included Hypogymnia physodes and Parmelia sulcata. PM10 filters were collected over 30-day passive exposure periods using standard diffusion samplers. ICP-MS was used for trace element quantification in all matrices following microwave-assisted acid digestion. TFs from bark to thallus ranged from 0.8 to 4.6 depending on element and species, with Cd consistently showing the highest values. Correlation analysis indicated that lichen Pb and Cd concentrations were more strongly associated with PM10 loadings than with bark substrate concentrations (r² = 0.71 and 0.68 respectively), reinforcing the aerial uptake pathway as dominant. Inter-species differences in TF were statistically significant for Ni and Fe but not for Cd or Pb.

title: Effects of simulated nitrogen deposition on desiccation tolerance and pigment content in Syntrichia ruralis
abstract: Nitrogen deposition is increasing in Central European steppe systems. To test its effect on moss stress physiology, Syntrichia ruralis turfs were irrigated weekly with NH4NO3 solutions at 0, 10, 25, and 50 kg N ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹ equivalent concentrations for 12 weeks in outdoor mesocosms. Desiccation tolerance (Fv/Fm recovery after 72 h at 20 % RH) declined significantly at the 50 kg N treatment (recovery to 0.58 vs. 0.74 in controls, p = 0.003, n = 8 per treatment). Chlorophyll a/b ratio increased at high N, suggesting impaired xanthophyll cycle activity. SOD activity was significantly lower in high-N plants during rehydration. Total nitrogen content of moss tissue confirmed uptake. No significant growth response was detected over the experiment duration. These results suggest that even moderate increases in atmospheric N deposition may reduce the stress resilience of steppe moss species without producing visible morphological changes.

title: Bryophyte and biological soil crust diversity as indicators of loess habitat integrity: methods and preliminary assessment
abstract: This book chapter reviews methodological approaches for using BSC and bryophyte communities as integrity indicators for loess bank and steppe habitats in the Pannonian region. We discuss species composition surveys, remote sensing of crust cover, and ecophysiological benchmarks (including Fv/Fm thresholds and chlorophyll content indices) as complementary assessment tools. A case study from 22 loess wall sites in Vojvodina illustrates how a combined score based on species richness, crust continuity, and mean summer Fv/Fm correlates with independently assessed habitat quality scores (Spearman r = 0.71, p < 0.001). We argue that rapid ecophysiological screening with portable fluorometers can substitute partial laboratory assays for routine monitoring. Practical recommendations for conservation managers are provided, including protocols adaptable to non-specialist field teams. Limitations of current methods related to seasonal variation and observer calibration are discussed.

title: Seasonal dynamics of antioxidant capacity in biological soil crusts on south-facing steppe slopes in Vojvodina
abstract: Biological soil crusts were sampled monthly from March to October at a permanent plot on a south-facing steppe slope at Stara Pazova over two consecutive years (2019–2020). Total antioxidant capacity (DPPH and FRAP assays), ascorbate peroxidase activity, and malondialdehyde content were measured in crust material separated into phototrophic crust (upper 1 mm) and bulk crust (1–5 mm) fractions. DPPH-radical scavenging capacity in the phototrophic fraction peaked in July (mean 142 µmol TE g⁻¹ DW) and was lowest in March (61 µmol TE g⁻¹ DW). MDA content followed the same pattern, peaking in July–August. APX activity was highest in April–May, coinciding with the period of rapid rehydration–desiccation cycling after spring rainfall. Interannual variability was pronounced: the drier year 2020 produced 28 % higher peak DPPH values. Depth fractionation revealed consistently lower antioxidant capacity in the bulk crust layer.

title: Transcriptomic response to desiccation in Syntrichia ruralis from a continental steppe population: comparison with an Atlantic reference dataset
abstract: RNA was extracted from Syntrichia ruralis plants collected at a Vojvodina loess steppe site and subjected to controlled desiccation (48 h at 25 % RH, 25 °C) and 2 h rehydration. Transcriptome libraries were prepared using TruSeq and sequenced on an Illumina NextSeq 550 (paired-end, 2 × 75 bp). De novo assembly produced 38,412 unigenes. Differential expression analysis (DESeq2) identified 2,104 significantly upregulated and 1,387 downregulated unigenes during desiccation (FDR < 0.05, |log2FC| > 1.5). Comparison with a published Atlantic-climate S. ruralis transcriptome dataset showed 71 % overlap in desiccation-upregulated gene clusters, but the continental population showed stronger upregulation of late embryogenesis abundant (LEA) protein transcripts and lower induction of aquaporin-related transcripts. GO enrichment analysis highlighted protein folding, ROS detoxification, and membrane stabilisation as primary biological processes. These differences may reflect population-level adaptation to more severe desiccation regimes.

title: Drought frequency modulates recovery capacity of cyanobacterial crusts: evidence from a multi-year rewetting experiment
abstract: We conducted a three-year outdoor mesocosm experiment at the University of Novi Sad experimental garden, exposing intact BSC cores (n = 60, 15 cm diameter) from the Deliblato Sands to three rewetting frequency treatments: ambient rainfall, reduced frequency (50 % of ambient events), and increased frequency (150 % via supplemental irrigation). After each growing season, crust photosynthetic recovery rates (Fv/Fm after 2 h rehydration), biomass, and community composition were assessed. By year 3, reduced-frequency treatment crusts showed significantly slower initial Fv/Fm recovery (0.42 at 30 min vs. 0.61 in controls, p = 0.01) and 23 % lower total crust biomass. Moss component richness declined in reduced-frequency treatments (from mean 4.2 to 2.7 species per core), while cyanobacterial dominance increased. Increased-frequency treatment produced modest biomass gains but no significant change in recovery rates. Results suggest that projected drying trends in the Pannonian region may gradually shift BSC communities toward cyanobacterial dominance.

title: Mapping biological soil crust cover on Vojvodina loess banks using UAV multispectral imagery and field spectroradiometry
abstract: We evaluated whether UAV-mounted multispectral sensors can reliably detect and map BSC cover on loess bank habitats at eight sites in Vojvodina. A DJI Matrice 300 drone carrying a MicaSense RedEdge-MX sensor was flown at 30 m altitude. Ground truth was provided by field spectroradiometry (ASD FieldSpec 4) and 128 quadrat-based BSC cover estimates. A random forest classifier trained on five spectral bands plus NDVI and NDWI indices achieved an overall accuracy of 79 % and a kappa coefficient of 0.71 for distinguishing crust-covered, bare, and vascular-plant-covered surfaces. Confusion was highest between sparse BSC and bare loess (17 % misclassification rate). Crust cover mapped at one intensively managed agricultural border site was 4 % compared with 38 % at a protected steppe reference site. The method provides a scalable tool for monitoring crust recovery after disturbance and is discussed in the context of habitat restoration assessment.

title: Pseudotime Ordering of Hematopoietic Progenitor Cells Using Elastic Principal Graphs
abstract: Trajectory inference from single-cell RNA-seq data requires assigning each cell a pseudotime coordinate reflecting its position along a differentiation path. We apply the elastic principal graph framework, which fits a branching curve skeleton to data in PCA-reduced space by minimising a sum of data-to-graph distances and a smoothness penalty on graph topology. Using a dataset of 2 730 bone-marrow progenitor cells profiled across six developmental stages, we infer a trajectory with three branches corresponding to myeloid, erythroid, and lymphoid lineages. Branch assignment accuracy, evaluated against known surface-marker labels, reaches 89 percent. Comparison with three competing trajectory methods on the same data shows that elastic graphs recover the known branching topology more consistently when the branching point occurs late in pseudotime. We discuss sensitivity to PCA dimensionality choices and propose a cross-validation heuristic for selecting the number of principal components.

title: Benchmarking Nonlinear Dimensionality Reduction Methods on Simulated Single-Cell RNA-Seq Datasets
abstract: We present a systematic evaluation of six nonlinear dimensionality reduction methods — diffusion maps, UMAP, t-SNE, LLE, PHATE, and a graph-autoencoder baseline — on single-cell RNA-seq data generated with the Splatter simulation framework under twelve parameter settings. Evaluation metrics include preservation of global structure (Spearman correlation of pairwise distances), cluster separability (Davies–Bouldin index), and trajectory recovery (Kendall tau between inferred and ground-truth pseudotime). Across 144 simulation conditions, PHATE and diffusion maps score highest on trajectory recovery, while UMAP excels at cluster separability. No single method dominates across all metrics. We also examine how the choice of highly variable gene selection affects results: restricting to the top 500 versus top 2 000 variable genes changes method rankings for trajectory recovery in 31 of 144 conditions. The benchmark suite is released as a reproducible Snakemake workflow.

title: Skin Conductance Response as a Scenographic Element: Technical Constraints and Performer Perspectives
abstract: Electrodermal activity (EDA), often measured as skin conductance response (SCR), is frequently discussed in affective computing literature but rarely deployed in live performance contexts. This paper documents a performance research process in which SCR signals from two performers were used to modulate the density and colour temperature of programmable LED lighting rigs across a 22-minute piece. Technical challenges included the 1–3 second response latency inherent to EDA, high sensitivity to electrode pressure artefacts caused by movement, and the difficulty of distinguishing thermoregulatory from emotionally driven responses during physically demanding performance. Two electrode placements (fingertip and volar forearm) were compared across 14 rehearsal sessions; the volar forearm placement produced 34% fewer movement artefacts. Performers were interviewed using a phenomenological approach adapted from Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis. Both reported that lighting changes felt most connected to experienced emotional states in slower, more stationary passages of the work, and disconnected during high-movement sequences. The paper concludes with revised signal-processing recommendations for EDA in movement-rich performance.

title: Towards Standardised Reporting for Biosensor-Based Performance Research: A Methodological Proposal
abstract: The field of biosensor-driven performance research lacks shared reporting conventions, making it difficult to compare results across studies. This preprint proposes a minimum reporting standard comprising nine items: sensor type and placement, sampling rate, signal processing pipeline (with version numbers of software used), calibration procedure, number and experience level of performers, number and duration of sessions, data logging method, method of evaluating the perceptual or expressive outcome, and a description of system failure events. The proposal is grounded in a review of 41 published studies from 2008 to 2024 that the authors identified through database searches of performance studies, HCI, and biomedical engineering literature. Of these, only 7 reported all nine items. The preprint invites community response and provides an example reporting template formatted for both journal articles and conference proceedings. A companion spreadsheet of the 41 reviewed studies is included as supplementary material.

title: Breath-Driven Generative Visual Systems in Mindfulness-Based Performance: A Cross-Cultural Study
abstract: This paper examines the use of respiratory signals—captured via a custom elastic chest-band sensor with a resistive stretch element—as the primary driver of generative visual output in two parallel mindfulness-based performance works created independently in Novi Sad, Serbia, and Ljubljana, Slovenia, using an agreed common technical framework. Each work involved six performers, eight rehearsal sessions, and two public performances. Breath rate, inhalation-to-exhalation ratio, and breath depth were extracted and mapped to visual parameters (cloud particle count, opacity, and drift velocity) in a shared TouchDesigner template. Post-performance audience surveys (n=47 Novi Sad, n=51 Ljubljana) used a 7-point Likert scale to assess perceived calm, perceived connection between performer and image, and aesthetic satisfaction. Mean scores for perceived calm were 5.6 (Novi Sad) and 5.3 (Ljubljana); perceived connection scores were 4.9 and 5.1 respectively. The paper discusses minor mapping-parameter differences introduced by each creative team and their measurable effects on audience perception scores.

title: Spectral Layering as a Compositional Strategy in Interactive Audio Installations
abstract: This study documents the design and audience reception of an interactive sound installation, Sediment, exhibited at the Novi Sad Cultural Centre in 2012. The piece used real-time spectral layering controlled by visitor movement tracked through a grid of 16 infrared proximity sensors. Spectral layers were generated procedurally using SuperCollider, with each sensor zone mapped to a distinct frequency band between 80 Hz and 8 kHz. Visitor trajectories were logged over a four-week exhibition period totalling approximately 1,200 individual visits. Qualitative post-visit interviews with 38 visitors and structured observation sessions with 12 recruited participants informed the analysis. Findings indicate that visitors consistently modulated their movement speed in response to sonic feedback, suggesting bidirectional behavioural influence between body movement and sound output. The paper discusses implications for designing participatory installations that foreground sonic agency without requiring prior musical knowledge.

title: Algorithmic Accompaniment for Oral Storytelling Performances: A Field Study
abstract: This paper reports on a two-year collaboration with three professional oral storytellers in the Vojvodina region to develop and evaluate an algorithmic accompaniment system that responds to speech prosody in real time. The system used pitch detection and speech energy envelope analysis to select and crossfade between procedurally generated textural layers in SuperCollider. Performers wore a Bluetooth headset microphone feeding a latency-compensated audio interface; end-to-end system latency was measured at 22 ms, which performers described as imperceptible in post-session debriefs. Three public performances were documented through audio-visual recording and followed by audience questionnaires (n = 67, 74, and 52 per event). Audiences rated the perceived integration of voice and accompaniment at 4.1 out of 5 on average. Challenges included prosodic variability across languages (Serbian and Hungarian were both used) and performer adaptation to the system's response curve, which required a rehearsal period of roughly six hours per performer.

title: Tactical Media
abstract: This book chapter provides an overview of the tactical media concept from its emergence at the Next Five Minutes festivals (Amsterdam, 1993–2003) through to its dispersal into social media-era practice. The chapter traces the intellectual genealogy of the term through contributions by David Garcia, Geert Lovink, and Critical Art Ensemble, then maps how Eastern European practitioners adopted, translated, and contested the concept within their specific post-socialist contexts. The chapter draws on archival research in three institutional collections in the Netherlands, Hungary, and Serbia, and on secondary literature across media studies, art history, and political theory. A section on legacy considers how tactical media's insistence on temporality and ephemerality complicates retrospective canonisation, a process now underway in several European contemporary art museums. The chapter is addressed to advanced undergraduates and postgraduate researchers entering the field.

title: Participatory Web Projects as Collective Memory Practice: Three Cases from Serbia, 2005–2015
abstract: This article examines three long-duration participatory web projects initiated by Serbian artists and collectives between 2005 and 2015, each of which solicited user-contributed materials—photographs, personal testimonies, audio recordings—to construct crowd-sourced archives of recent traumatic history. The projects are analysed through the frameworks of collective memory studies (Assmann, Halbwachs) and participatory art theory (Bishop, Kester). The study draws on semi-structured interviews with the three project initiators, download statistics and contributor metadata from project servers, and ethnographic observation of two offline events connected to the projects. Contributor analysis shows that all three projects attracted predominantly urban, university-educated users under forty, raising questions about whose memories are assembled and whose are absent. The article also addresses how platform migration and link rot have affected the projects' ongoing accessibility and reflects on the implications for memory studies of ephemeral digital archives.

title: Teaching Tactical Media: Curriculum Challenges in a Post-Yugoslav Art Academy
abstract: This paper reports on a five-year curriculum development process at the Department of Digital Arts, Academy of Arts, University of Novi Sad, where an undergraduate module on tactical media and net.art was introduced in 2014 and revised in 2016 and 2019. The paper describes the pedagogical rationale, the selection of historical case studies, and the structure of practical assignments in which students produced their own tactical media interventions under live conditions. It reflects on tensions between the anti-institutional ethos of tactical media and the institutional setting of a state university, and on challenges posed by students' unfamiliarity with pre-smartphone internet culture. Data are drawn from module evaluation surveys (n=287 students across five years), assessment outcomes, and the author's reflective teaching journal. The paper identifies three recurring difficulties: contextualising historical works for students with no lived memory of the 1990s, managing ethical risks in live interventions, and assessing ephemeral or deliberately undocumented work.

title: Comparative Numerical Study of Shed Profile Modifications for Reducing Electric Field Peaks on Medium-Voltage Composite Insulators
abstract: Several shed profile variants — standard alternate-shed, deep-rib, and aerodynamic-taper designs — were evaluated numerically to identify geometric features that reduce electric field peaks under contaminated conditions. A parametric 2D FEM model was constructed for each profile with identical overall leakage distance of 560 mm and the same pollution conductivity of 0.1 S/m. Peak tangential field values, integrated field non-uniformity indices, and dry-band formation risk scores derived from field gradients were computed for 21 geometric configurations obtained by varying shed pitch, shed diameter ratio, and rib depth. The aerodynamic-taper profile with a shed diameter ratio of 1.35 and a pitch of 38 mm produced the lowest field peak (0.72 kV/mm) and the most uniform field distribution. Results are presented as response surfaces to guide future insulator design within standard dimensional constraints.

title: Calibration of a Simplified Freeze-Thaw Deterioration Index for Use in Network-Level Pavement Management Systems in Serbia
abstract: A freeze-thaw deterioration index (FTDI) was developed to support network-level pavement management without requiring full mechanistic-empirical analysis at each section. The index combines annual freeze-thaw cycle count derived from daily minimum and maximum air temperatures, mean annual precipitation, subgrade soil type category, and pavement age into a single weighted score. Weights were calibrated against 12 years of pavement condition index (PCI) monitoring data from 340 sections in the Serbian state road network, using multiple linear regression with cross-validation. The FTDI explained 62 percent of the variance in PCI decline rates on flexible pavement sections with unbound granular bases. Sections with FTDI above 65 showed median PCI deterioration rates 2.3 times higher than sections below 35. The index is implemented as a spreadsheet tool supplied to regional road management offices and was piloted during 2024 network condition surveys.

title: Effect of row-structure proximity on achievable calibration accuracy: a simulation study
abstract: Orchard row structures restrict manipulator configuration diversity during in-situ calibration because the arm must avoid collisions with trellis wires and tree canopy. This paper examines, through simulation, how configuration-space restrictions imposed by a standardised apple-row geometry affect the identifiability of geometric and compliance parameters. A Monte Carlo study over 5000 random row geometries (inter-row spacing 2.8–4.2 m, trellis height 1.8–3.4 m) generated constrained configuration sets of varying size. Calibration was simulated by adding Gaussian measurement noise (σ = 0.3 mm) to synthetic pose data and solving the identification problem. Parameter estimation error increased by a median factor of 2.4 compared to unconstrained full-workspace calibration. A minimum of 48 reachable configurations yielded position accuracy below 0.6 mm in 90% of row geometries tested. Strategies for selecting maximally informative configurations within the constrained space are discussed. The simulation code is available under a BSD-2 licence.

title: Post-Pandemic Demand Recovery Trajectories and Repricing Strategies in Urban Hotels: Evidence from Four Serbian Cities
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic produced an unprecedented and heterogeneous demand shock in urban hotel markets. Using daily administrative revenue data from 31 hotels in Belgrade, Novi Sad, Kragujevac, and Niš for the period January 2019 to December 2022, this paper estimates city-specific demand recovery curves and evaluates whether hotels that adopted aggressive repricing during the trough phase recovered faster than those that maintained pre-pandemic rate levels. A synthetic control method is applied to construct counterfactual recovery paths for each property. Results show that hotels that cut average daily rates by more than 20% during the trough recovered to 90% of pre-pandemic RevPAR roughly 4.2 months earlier on average, but at a cost of sustained brand dilution measurable in online review scores 18 months later. The trade-off between short-run occupancy gains and longer-run reputation effects is quantified and discussed.

title: Effect of DC Bias on Resonant Inductance and Quality Factor in LLC Converters for Supercapacitor Interfaces
abstract: Supercapacitor terminal voltage varies continuously from near 0 V to full rated voltage during charge and discharge cycles. When an LLC converter is used at the supercapacitor interface, the secondary-side current can introduce a DC bias component into the resonant inductance under partial-resonance operating modes, shifting the resonant frequency by up to 9 % and degrading the quality factor. This study characterises this effect on three inductors wound on different core materials (N87 ferrite, amorphous ribbon, and nanocrystalline) using a combination of impedance analyser measurements and LTspice simulations incorporating a Jiles–Atherton permeability model. Measurements were taken at DC bias currents from 0 A to 12 A and small-signal AC frequencies from 80 kHz to 300 kHz. The nanocrystalline core showed the smallest resonant frequency shift (1.8 %) and the best retention of quality factor under bias. Practical guidelines for air-gap selection to limit frequency deviation below 3 % across the supercapacitor voltage range are provided.

title: Parameterisation of an Extended Describing Function Model for CLLC Converters Using Impedance Analyser Measurements
abstract: The extended describing function (EDF) is a widely used small-signal model for resonant converters, but its accuracy depends critically on the accuracy of the resonant tank parameters. This paper demonstrates a measurement-based parameterisation procedure in which the resonant capacitance, resonant inductance, and transformer magnetising inductance are extracted from impedance analyser scans performed on the fully assembled converter board, rather than relying on component datasheet values or separate bench measurements of individual components. Measurements were made on a 5 kW CLLC converter operating between 90 kHz and 180 kHz. The procedure accounts for PCB trace inductances, interconnect capacitances, and winding inter-winding capacitance, all of which become significant above 100 kHz. Using the measured parameters reduced the error in the predicted control-to-output frequency response from 9.6 dB to 1.8 dB at the gain crossover frequency. A step-by-step measurement protocol is presented that can be applied without circuit disassembly.

title: Loss Partitioning in a 7 kW Bidirectional CLLC Stage for a Second-Life Battery Pack
abstract: Second-life lithium-ion battery packs repurposed from electric vehicles exhibit a wider terminal voltage range and higher internal resistance spread than new cells, placing additional demands on the DC-DC interface converter. This paper reports a detailed loss partitioning study on a 7 kW bidirectional CLLC stage designed for a second-life pack with a nominal voltage of 72 V and an operating range of 55–88 V. Losses were separated into switching losses (measured via double-pulse test), conduction losses (derived from on-state resistance measurements at operating temperature), and magnetic losses (calorimetric method). At full load in forward mode, total converter loss was 218 W, with magnetic losses contributing 38 %, primary switching losses 29 %, secondary conduction losses 21 %, and gate drive and auxiliary supply 12 %. Across the battery voltage range, total loss varied by ±19 % relative to the nominal operating point. Frequency schedules that minimise total loss as a function of instantaneous battery voltage are computed and compared against constant-frequency and fixed-frequency-with-phase-shift strategies.

title: Sensitivity of LLC Converter Efficiency to Resonant Tank Component Tolerances: A Monte Carlo Study
abstract: Resonant tank components—capacitors and inductors—carry manufacturing tolerances that shift the resonant frequency and quality factor away from their designed values. This paper presents a Monte Carlo analysis of the impact of ±5 % and ±10 % tolerance bands on resonant capacitance and inductance on the efficiency and ZVS coverage of a 3 kW LLC converter operating at a nominal resonant frequency of 130 kHz. The FHA gain model was solved for 10,000 randomly sampled component combinations under three load conditions (20 %, 60 %, 100 % of rated power). The probability of losing ZVS on the primary switches at 20 % load exceeded 14 % when both components carried ±10 % tolerances simultaneously, compared to 3.1 % with ±5 % tolerances. Efficiency at rated load was degraded by more than 0.5 percentage points in 8 % of Monte Carlo draws for ±10 % tolerances. Component sorting and post-assembly impedance measurement are evaluated as mitigation strategies, with their cost–benefit trade-off discussed for a small-series production context.

title: Frequency-Domain Loss Budgeting for Isolated DC-DC Converters in Stationary Energy Storage: A Unified Methodology
abstract: This paper proposes a unified methodology for constructing a frequency-domain loss budget for isolated resonant DC-DC converters used in stationary energy storage applications. The methodology integrates harmonic decomposition of converter waveforms with component-level loss models: an extended Steinmetz approach for magnetic cores, a frequency-weighted resistance model for windings, a charge-based switching loss model for semiconductors, and a dielectric loss model for film resonant capacitors. Each sub-model is calibrated independently using standardised bench measurements before being assembled into a full converter loss prediction. The methodology is validated against calorimetric measurements on a 10 kW CLLC prototype at nine operating points spanning the converter's frequency and load range. Total loss prediction error remained below 4.8 % at all tested operating points. The paper discusses how the methodology can be used during the design phase to allocate loss budgets between subsystems and to identify the component most sensitive to operating point deviations.

title: Adaptive Impedance Matching for Wearable UHF RFID Reader Antennas Subject to Body Loading
abstract: Body loading significantly alters the input impedance of antennas integrated into wearable devices, degrading read range and increasing power reflected back to the transmitter. This study characterises impedance variation of a 915 MHz RFID reader patch antenna mounted on five tissue-simulating phantom configurations representing different body locations. Measured impedance loci at each location were mapped on the Smith chart, with reactance shifts up to 35 Ω and resistance shifts up to 22 Ω recorded compared to free-space values. A switched-capacitor tuning network with four binary-weighted capacitors was designed and integrated, enabling 16 discrete matching states. An iterative hill-climbing algorithm operating from reflected power measurements selected the optimum state in under 80 ms. Field tests with five human subjects showed that adaptive matching recovered a mean 2.1 dB improvement in effective isotropic radiated power compared to a fixed matching network optimised for free-space conditions. Current consumption of the tuning circuit remained below 3 mA during active tuning.

title: Bootstrapped high-side gate driver for 650 V GaN: bootstrap diode selection and charge budget under variable duty cycle
abstract: Bootstrap-supplied high-side gate drivers for 650 V GaN half-bridges require careful diode selection and charge budget analysis because the bootstrap voltage must not fall below the gate-driver under-voltage lockout threshold across the full duty-cycle range. This paper analyses three bootstrap diode types—silicon fast-recovery, SiC Schottky, and GaN-based—in terms of reverse leakage current, forward voltage, and dynamic charge loss. A charge budget model including gate charge, quiescent current, and bootstrap capacitor leakage was validated experimentally in a 400 V, 300 W converter sweeping duty cycles from 5 % to 95 % at frequencies from 100 kHz to 1 MHz. The silicon fast-recovery diode caused bootstrap dropout at duty cycles above 85 % and above 500 kHz due to reverse recovery charge injected back into the bootstrap node. The SiC Schottky diode maintained stable high-side supply voltage across the full range. Minimum bootstrap capacitance requirements are tabulated as a function of frequency and duty cycle.

title: Uticaj artefakata retiminga na formalnu verifikaciju pipeline DSP jezgara: analiza i smernice
abstract: Automatski retiming, dostupan u sintetizatorima kao što su Vivado i Quartus, premešta registre između kombinacionih stepena radi poboljšanja timinga, ali može da izmeni posmatrljive latencije i da pokvari prethodno napisana formalna svojstva. Predložen je metodološki vodič u četiri koraka koji obuhvata: (1) automatsku ekstrakciju latencije iz post-implementacionog netlista, (2) parametrizaciju SVA iskaza latencijom, (3) resintez netlistem kao novim referentnim modelom i (4) automatsku reanalizaciju. title: Residual Distortion Analysis After National Datum Modernisation: Vojvodina as a Test Area
abstract: Serbia completed a phased renewal of its national geodetic datum between 2005 and 2015. Despite this effort, residual distortions inherited from the former Gauss–Krüger coordinate system and from inconsistencies in the analogue cadastral archive remain detectable. This study analyses the spatial distribution of such residuals across Vojvodina using 489 benchmark coordinates from both the new D96 adjustment and historical D48 records, cross-checked against GNSS-derived positions. Semivariogram fitting reveals two dominant distortion scales: a regional trend with a range of approximately 40 km accounting for 58 % of total distortion variance, and a local component with a range near 4 km. The regional component correlates with administrative boundaries of former cadastral municipalities, suggesting that piecemeal digitisation of municipal cadastral plans introduced block-wise offsets. Kriging interpolation of the local component is shown to reduce RMS residuals from 12.3 cm to 4.1 cm in a cross-validation experiment.

title: Raman mapping of spatial co-former distribution in spray-dried co-crystal intermediates as a function of drying inlet temperature
abstract: Spray drying is increasingly considered for continuous manufacturing of pharmaceutical co-crystals, yet the effect of inlet temperature on intra-particle co-former distribution remains poorly understood. Naproxen–picolinamide co-crystal solutions in ethanol (5 wt% total solids, 1:1 molar ratio) were spray-dried at four inlet temperatures (80, 110, 140, and 170 °C) with a fixed outlet temperature range of 58–65 °C. Particles collected on filters were embedded in epoxy resin, sectioned to approximately 1 μm thickness, and mapped by confocal Raman microscopy (256 × 256 pixels, step 0.5 μm). At 80 °C, 94% of map pixels showed co-crystal phase; at 170 °C, this dropped to 71%, with naproxen-rich segregated domains appearing at the particle surface. PXRD quantification confirmed partial amorphisation (up to 18%) at 170 °C. Residual ethanol content measured by headspace GC decreased monotonically from 0.43 wt% at 80 °C to below the ICH Q3C limit at 140 °C. The findings indicate that an inlet temperature of 110–130 °C provides acceptable phase purity and solvent removal simultaneously.

title: Solid-state characterisation of a ternary co-crystal: indomethacin, saccharin, and l-tartaric acid
abstract: Ternary pharmaceutical co-crystals remain rare and their preparation is empirically guided. An indomethacin–saccharin–l-tartaric acid (1:1:1) ternary phase was obtained by LAG with acetonitrile and confirmed by PXRD (new diffraction peaks at 6.2°, 11.8°, and 17.4° 2θ not present in any binary sub-system), DSC (single eutectic-like endotherm at 148 °C), TGA, and solid-state ¹³C CP-MAS NMR collected at a national facility. Raman mapping of tablet cross-sections confirmed homogeneous co-crystal distribution. The ternary co-crystal dissolved 2.3× faster than crystalline γ-indomethacin in pH 6.8 phosphate buffer (USP Apparatus II, 37 °C, 75 rpm, n = 6), compared with 1.9× for the binary indomethacin–saccharin co-crystal prepared and tested under identical conditions. Physical stability testing at 40 °C / 75% RH for 12 weeks showed no detectable phase change by PXRD. The work demonstrates that controlled introduction of a third co-former can measurably improve dissolution performance beyond the binary co-crystal.

title: Crystal engineering of aceclofenac co-crystals for improved aqueous solubility: systematic co-former selection and scale-up by twin-screw extrusion
abstract: Aceclofenac is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug with low aqueous solubility (0.011 mg mL⁻¹ at 25 °C). Twenty-two co-formers listed on the GRAS list were screened by LAG; five yielded new crystalline phases by PXRD. The three most stable candidates—nicotinamide, caffeine, and theophylline—were selected for full characterisation. DSC, TGA, PXRD, and Raman mapping confirmed co-crystal identity and purity. Aqueous solubility measured by the miniaturised shake-flask method (n = 3) increased to 0.034, 0.029, and 0.021 mg mL⁻¹ respectively for the three co-crystals. All three were prepared at 50 g scale by twin-screw extrusion (temperature 65 °C, screw speed 80 rpm, feed ratio adjusted to 1:1 molar), yielding phase-pure product as confirmed by PXRD with Rwp < 5.0%. Flowability (Hausner ratio) improved from 1.41 for pure aceclofenac to 1.22, 1.18, and 1.25 for the three co-crystals. A 24-month open-dish stability study at 25 °C / 60% RH showed no polymorphic conversion for nicotinamide and caffeine co-crystals; the theophylline co-crystal showed partial conversion to theophylline monohydrate after 6 months.

title: Crystal engineering approaches to active pharmaceutical ingredients: from polymorph screening to co-crystal scale-up
abstract: This book chapter provides a methodological overview of solid-state screening workflows for active pharmaceutical ingredients, intended for graduate students and early-career researchers entering the field. The chapter covers the logical sequence from initial polymorph screening through co-former selection, crystallisation method optimisation, and scale-up considerations. Specific sections address PXRD data collection and interpretation, DSC experimental design (mass, scan rate, atmosphere), Raman mapping data acquisition parameters and chemometric processing, and the use of crystallographic databases in co-former selection. Case studies drawn from the authors' own laboratory data on ibuprofen, carbamazepine, and aceclofenac co-crystals are used throughout. Quantitative benchmarks are provided for typical experimental outcomes: for example, the success rate of LAG screening from a random 20-member co-former set is reported from several published studies as 15–30%. The chapter concludes with a discussion of regulatory expectations for co-crystal characterisation, referencing the EMA reflection paper and FDA guidance.

title: Fast-dissolving co-crystal pellets of piroxicam–malonic acid prepared by hot-melt extrusion: effect of polymer matrix on phase purity and in vitro release
abstract: Piroxicam–malonic acid co-crystal (PMC, 1:1) was incorporated into pellets by hot-melt extrusion (HME) using three hydrophilic polymers: polyvinyl caprolactam–polyvinyl acetate–polyethylene glycol graft copolymer (Soluplus equivalent), hydroxypropyl methylcellulose acetate succinate (HPMCAS-MF grade), and polyvinylpyrrolidone–vinyl acetate 64 (PVP-VA64) at 20 wt% drug loading. Extrusion was carried out at 100–130 °C depending on polymer; torque and melt temperature were logged for all runs. Post-extrusion PXRD analysis showed that the PVP-VA64 matrix caused complete co-crystal-to-amorphous conversion, while HPMCAS-MF and Soluplus matrices retained 88% and 79% crystalline co-crystal, respectively (Rietveld quantification). Raman mapping of pellet cross-sections (64 × 64 pixels, step 3 μm) confirmed the co-crystal distribution correlated with PXRD results. In vitro dissolution in FaSSIF-V2 at pH 6.5 showed that all three pellet formulations exceeded the intrinsic dissolution rate of crystalline piroxicam by at least 2.1×, with the HPMCAS-MF pellets showing the most sustained supersaturation profile over 240 minutes. Six-month stability testing at 25 °C / 60% RH showed no further amorphisation in HPMCAS-MF pellets.

title: Distribution of dissolved iron species in the Tisa River tributaries of Vojvodina during seasonal low-flow periods
abstract: Iron speciation was investigated in twelve surface water sampling points along three tributaries of the Tisa River in northern Serbia during summer and early autumn low-flow conditions over two consecutive years. Total dissolved iron, Fe(II), and Fe(III) concentrations were determined by ferrozine spectrophotometry combined with 0.45 µm membrane filtration. Fe(II) fractions ranged from 18 to 64 % of total dissolved iron depending on sampling site and season, with the highest Fe(II) proportions observed in hyporheic exchange zones downstream of drainage channels. Dissolved oxygen, pH (6.8–8.1), and temperature (14–24 °C) were recorded in situ. A positive correlation between Fe(II)/Fe(total) ratio and turbidity was noted at two sites, indicating particle-associated reductive dissolution. The dataset provides a seasonal baseline for redox-driven iron cycling in lowland river systems receiving agricultural drainage. Implications for drinking water treatment intakes drawing from these tributaries are discussed.

title: Redox speciation of iron in constructed wetland outflows treating acid mine drainage
abstract: Iron speciation was characterised at the inflow, mid-zone, and outflow of two pilot-scale constructed wetlands built to treat low-pH drainage (pH 3.2–4.5) from an abandoned pyrite extraction site in eastern Serbia. Total Fe, Fe(II), and Fe(III) were determined at 48-hour intervals over six weeks by ferrozine photometry and ICP-OES. Fe(II) at the inflow averaged 48 mg/L and decreased to 3.1 mg/L at the outflow, while pH rose to 6.1–6.8 through bacterial sulfate reduction and alkalinity generation. Fe(III) accumulated transiently as schwertmannite-type precipitates in the mid-zone as confirmed by XRD analysis. Fe removal efficiency averaged 93.5 % across the six-week period but dropped to 81 % during a cold spell (air temperature below −3 °C) in week four, coinciding with reduced microbial activity. The dataset supports mechanistic modelling of coupled iron oxidation–precipitation–reduction in passive treatment systems.
