title: Calibration Transfer of NIR Protein Models Between Two Benchtop Instruments Using Direct Standardisation and Piecewise Direct Standardisation
abstract: Spectral differences between instruments of the same nominal model from different production lots complicate the deployment of a master calibration on a secondary instrument. A calibration model for total protein in wheat–rye blend samples, originally developed on a first-generation instrument at the University of Novi Sad, was transferred to a second instrument at the University of Osijek using a set of 12 standardisation samples. Direct standardisation and piecewise direct standardisation were compared using a transfer set that included samples spanning the full protein range of 9.5–16.8 g per 100 g. Without transfer correction, the secondary instrument yielded a mean bias of 1.2 g per 100 g and RMSEP of 1.4 g per 100 g. Piecewise direct standardisation with a segment width of 20 nm reduced bias to 0.08 g per 100 g and RMSEP to 0.38 g per 100 g, achieving performance close to the master model. Selection of informative standardisation samples by Kennard–Stone sampling is described.

title: Assessment of Domain Shift in NIR Protein Calibrations Transferred Across Harvest Years Using a Small Annual Update Set
abstract: Calibration models for protein in wheat flour tend to lose accuracy across harvest years because of systematic differences in variety composition, growth conditions and moisture history of grain. This study followed the predictive performance of a master PLS protein model over three consecutive harvest years (2021, 2022 and 2023) using a fixed set of 155 flour samples from the 2020 harvest as calibration and fresh sets of 40–55 samples per year as independent test sets. Without any update, RMSEP increased from 0.29 g per 100 g in 2021 to 0.58 g per 100 g in 2023. Annual slope-bias corrections based on 8 selected update samples brought RMSEP back to below 0.35 g per 100 g in all years. The optimal size of the annual update set was investigated by random subsampling, showing diminishing returns above 6 samples. Recommendations are given for a low-cost annual recalibration workflow compatible with laboratory routine.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Predicting Judgment Outcomes: A Feasibility Study on Serbian Case Law
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems combine a retrieval component with a generative model and have been applied to question answering in several legal jurisdictions, but their use for outcome prediction on small corpora remains unexplored. This preprint describes a feasibility study in which a dense retrieval index is built from 1,840 Serbian civil court decisions and used to condition a fine-tuned sequence-to-sequence model on retrieved precedents at inference time. Three retrieval configurations—BM25, dense passage retrieval with a multilingual encoder, and a hybrid combination—are compared on a 200-instance test set. The hybrid configuration achieves the highest accuracy (0.71) and macro F1 (0.63), compared to 0.65 and 0.57 for the no-retrieval baseline. Analysis of retrieved documents shows that recency and jurisdictional tier of retrieved cases are positively associated with prediction correctness. The study flags limitations arising from incomplete metadata and inconsistent anonymisation in the source corpus.

title: Pelletisation of Hemp Shive Biosorbent for Packed-Bed Applications: Mechanical Stability, Hydraulic Performance, and Dye Removal Efficiency
abstract: Powdered hemp shive biosorbent, identified in earlier work as a high-capacity material, was pelletised using carboxymethyl cellulose as a binder (5 and 10 wt%) and evaluated for column applications. Pellets of 3 and 5 mm diameter were tested for mechanical crush strength, water stability over 72 h, and methylene blue removal in fixed-bed columns (bed height 15 cm, flow rates 3–12 mL/min, inlet concentration 100 mg/L). The 5 mm pellets with 10 wt% binder showed adequate crush strength (>4.2 N) and maintained structural integrity over 72 h. Pressure drop across the bed was 30–65% lower compared to equivalent packed powder beds. Thomas model fits gave column capacities of 85–101 mg/g, representing a 15–20% reduction relative to unpelletised material, attributed to restricted intraparticle diffusion within pellets. Scanning electron microscopy of pellet cross-sections confirmed partial pore occlusion by the binder at 10 wt%. An optimised binder content of 7 wt% is proposed for future scale-up studies.

title: Machine Learning-Assisted Prediction of Langmuir Isotherm Parameters for Cationic Dye Biosorption: A Dataset-Driven Approach
abstract: A dataset of 310 biosorption experiments from published and in-house studies was assembled, covering 14 cationic dyes, 11 lignocellulosic by-products, and pH values of 4–10. Input features included dye molecular weight, charge, log P, biosorbent carboxylate density (mmol/g), BET surface area (m²/g), pH, and temperature. Random forest (RF) and gradient boosting (GB) regression models were trained to predict Langmuir q_max and K_L parameters using 5-fold cross-validation. GB outperformed RF for q_max prediction (RMSE 8.4 vs. 12.1 mg/g) while both models performed similarly for K_L (RMSE ~0.006 L/mg). Feature importance analysis confirmed carboxylate density and pH as the two dominant predictors of q_max, consistent with mechanistic understanding. The model was validated against 22 independent experiments not used in training, achieving a mean absolute percentage error of 14.2% for q_max. The trained model and dataset are made available as supplementary material to support rapid pre-screening of candidate biosorbents.

title: Continuous Flow Biosorption of Safranin O and Basic Red 46 in a Two-Stage Fixed-Bed System Using Hemp Shive Pellets
abstract: A two-stage fixed-bed configuration was designed and tested for continuous treatment of synthetic textile wastewater containing safranin O (SO) and Basic Red 46 (BR46) at inlet concentrations of 80 and 60 mg/L, respectively. Hemp shive pellets (7 wt% CMC binder, 5 mm diameter) were packed into two serially connected glass columns (15 cm bed height each). Flow rates of 5 and 8 mL/min were tested over 72-hour runs. Effluent was monitored by UV-Vis spectrophotometry at 520 and 498 nm for SO and BR46, respectively. The two-stage setup extended time to 10% breakthrough by 2.7-fold (5 mL/min) compared to a single-stage column of equal total volume, confirming better utilisation of sorption capacity. BDST (bed depth service time) model parameters were determined for both stages and both dyes. After exhaustion, regeneration with 0.1 M citric acid restored 88% of capacity for SO and 79% for BR46 over three cycles. Effluent quality met the Serbian national limit for colour discharge in 94% of the operational period tested.

title: Characterisation of ajvar off-flavour: identification of key odorants by GC-olfactometry and aroma extract dilution analysis
abstract: Ajvar, a roasted Capsicum annuum-based condiment widely consumed in the western Balkans, frequently develops off-flavours during storage. GC-olfactometry combined with aroma extract dilution analysis (AEDA) was used to identify the most potent odorants in commercial ajvar samples collected from Serbian producers. Fifteen samples were evaluated by a seven-member trained panel. Compounds with the highest flavour dilution (FD) factors included 2-acetyl-1-pyrroline (FD 512), (E)-2-decenal (FD 256), and guaiacol (FD 256). A paint-like off-note attributed to 1-octen-3-one was detected in four samples showing elevated lipid oxidation indices. The study maps the odorant landscape of both fresh and oxidatively degraded ajvar, providing targets for future quality control work.

title: Enantioselective esterification of (R,S)-ibuprofen with n-propanol catalysed by Burkholderia cepacia lipase on celite in isooctane
abstract: The resolution of racemic ibuprofen was investigated using Burkholderia cepacia lipase physically adsorbed onto Celite 545. Reactions were performed in isooctane at substrate concentrations between 25 and 200 mM, alcohol:acid molar ratios of 1:1 to 5:1, and temperatures of 30–50 °C. Enantiomeric excess of the (S)-ester product (ee_p) reached 94.2% at 40 °C with a 2:1 propanol:ibuprofen ratio and 0.1 g enzyme preparation per mmol substrate. The E value was calculated as 38 ± 3 across three replicate experiments. Conversion was limited to 42% to preserve high ee_p. A substrate inhibition model fitted the kinetic data better than Michaelis–Menten kinetics, with inhibition constant K_i of 98 mM. The work provides practical parameters for a preparative-scale resolution protocol applicable to production of the active pharmaceutical ingredient.

title: Effect of descriptor scaling and normalisation choices on QSAR model stability for antifungal azoles
abstract: Preprocessing decisions—mean centring, autoscaling, range scaling, and Pareto scaling—are rarely reported in detail yet can alter descriptor rankings and model coefficients substantially. This study evaluated four scaling strategies on a fixed dataset of 65 azole antifungals using MLR, PLS, and RF, with all other settings held constant. Autoscaling produced the most stable PLS models across 50 random train–test splits (variance in Q²ext = 0.0041), while range scaling led to the highest instability in MLR (variance = 0.019) due to sensitivity to descriptor outliers. RF was largely insensitive to scaling method (maximum variance in R²ext = 0.0018), consistent with its tree-based structure. For MLR and PLS, autoscaling is recommended as the default; range scaling is inadvisable when descriptors contain structural outliers. These findings have practical implications for QSAR reproducibility and should be reported alongside model statistics in publications.

title: Declarative Data Quality Rules for Tabular Integration Pipelines: Specification and Automated Checking
abstract: Data quality problems in integration pipelines are often detected late, after erroneous records have propagated through multiple transformation steps. This paper proposes a declarative language for expressing data quality rules over tabular sources, covering completeness, domain conformance, referential consistency, and cross-column dependency constraints. Rules are compiled into SQL CHECK expressions and evaluated incrementally as new data batches arrive. The specification language was designed to be accessible to domain analysts without programming expertise, using a controlled natural language surface syntax. A user study with 12 participants from two Serbian public institutions showed that analysts with no SQL background could write correct rules for 78% of test scenarios after a two-hour training session. Automated checking was integrated into a lightweight ETL framework and evaluated on five operational data feeds from a regional land registry, detecting between 3% and 11% of records as quality-violating across the feeds.

title: Moisture ingress risk mapping for outdoor electromechanical enclosures across climatic regions of the Western Balkans
abstract: Meteorological data from 41 weather stations across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia were used to compute three moisture-ingress risk indicators: annual condensation-degree-days, maximum sustained diurnal temperature amplitude, and annual precipitation contact hours estimated from enclosure orientation geometry. A risk score was defined by weighting these indicators using coefficients derived from a previous regression model. Spatial maps were produced at 10 km × 10 km resolution using ordinary kriging interpolation. The Pannonian lowland region, including Vojvodina, was classified as moderate risk, while mountain basins in the Dinaric area showed high risk due to frequent temperature inversions producing prolonged condensation conditions. For each risk zone, minimum gasket specifications in terms of compression-set limit and diffusivity threshold are proposed. The dataset and scoring tool are made available as a freely downloadable spreadsheet to support enclosure procurement decisions by practitioners.

title: Sensitivity of precast concrete LCA results to background database choice: ecoinvent, EF-compliant datasets and a locally adapted Serbian dataset
abstract: Life-cycle assessment results for construction products are sensitive to the background database used, yet most Serbian studies rely on unmodified European or global databases. This paper systematically compares three background datasets – ecoinvent 3.9, the European Commission Environmental Footprint (EF 3.1) dataset, and a locally adapted Serbian dataset compiled from national energy statistics, cement plant emission reports, and aggregates industry data – applied to five representative precast concrete product types. For GWP (climate change, fossil), the Serbian-adapted dataset yields values 9–17% higher than ecoinvent 3.9 for products with a high cement content, primarily due to higher clinker-to-cement ratios in Serbian cement production (average 84% vs. 76% in the European average). For acidification and particulate matter formation, the locally adapted dataset shows differences of up to 31% from ecoinvent values. The paper makes the compiled Serbian background inventory dataset publicly available and recommends its use as a default in future Serbian EPD programmes.

title: Factor structure of a newly constructed verbal reasoning battery in a Serbian undergraduate sample
abstract: This study examined the internal structure of the Verbal Reasoning Battery for Selection (VRBS), a 60-item instrument developed for use in personnel selection in Serbian-speaking contexts. A sample of 412 undergraduate students from three universities in Vojvodina completed the battery under controlled conditions. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA) with oblimin rotation and parallel analysis indicated a two-factor solution distinguishing vocabulary-based items from inferential reasoning items, together accounting for 41% of common variance. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) on a hold-out subsample (n = 198) yielded acceptable fit (CFI = 0.93, RMSEA = 0.057). Internal consistency estimates (Cronbach's α) were 0.81 and 0.78 for the two subscales. Item difficulty indices ranged from 0.31 to 0.72, indicating moderate spread appropriate for selection contexts. The findings support a two-dimensional interpretation of verbal reasoning in this population and provide a basis for subsequent criterion validity studies with the VRBS.

title: Adapting the Hexagonal Personality Inventory for occupational use in Serbia: translation, pilot testing, and preliminary structural validity
abstract: The paper describes the Serbian adaptation of the Hexagonal Personality Inventory (HPI-S), a 180-item instrument covering six broad personality dimensions relevant to work behaviour. Following a committee translation–back-translation procedure with a bilingual panel of five psychologists, cognitive interviews were conducted with 24 working adults to assess item comprehensibility. A pilot sample of 310 employed adults from service and industrial sectors completed the inventory alongside the Eysenck Personality Questionnaire Revised (EPQ-R) as a convergent marker. CFA of the six-factor structure showed marginal fit in the full pilot sample (CFI = 0.88, RMSEA = 0.063), prompting revision of 18 items showing high residual correlations or low factor loadings (< 0.30). Convergent correlations with EPQ-R Extraversion and Neuroticism scales were in the expected direction (r = 0.61 and –0.54, respectively). The revised 162-item version is recommended for further large-scale validation before operational deployment.

title: Construct validity of a brief dark triad measure in Serbian job applicant versus non-applicant samples
abstract: Dark triad traits—narcissism, Machiavellianism, and psychopathy—have attracted interest in personnel psychology, yet most validation evidence derives from student samples in Western European countries. This study examined the factor structure and construct validity of the Serbian adaptation of the Short Dark Triad Scale (SDT-SR, 27 items) in two samples: 298 job applicants undergoing formal selection for supervisory positions and 244 non-applicant adults recruited via workplace contacts. CFA supported a three-factor correlated model in both samples (CFI ≥ 0.91, RMSEA ≤ 0.068). Multi-group tests confirmed metric but not full scalar invariance, with three Machiavellianism items showing elevated intercepts in the applicant sample, consistent with socially desirable responding under evaluation conditions. Correlations with HPI-S Agreeableness and Conscientiousness were in the expected negative direction (–0.41 to –0.52) in the non-applicant group and were attenuated in the applicant group. The findings underscore the importance of context-specific validation for dark triad instruments used operationally.

title: Digital Pre-Distortion for RF Power Amplifiers: Architectures, Models and Practical Constraints
abstract: This chapter surveys the principal approaches to digital pre-distortion for broadband power amplifiers in modern wireless base stations. It covers memoryless polynomial correction, memory polynomial and generalised memory polynomial methods, Volterra series truncations, and machine-learning-based approaches that have appeared since 2015. For each class of model, the trade-off between coefficient count, extraction data volume, numerical conditioning, and achievable ACPR improvement is discussed. Practical implementation topics covered include observation receiver design, IQ imbalance and DC offset compensation, delay alignment, and coefficient update scheduling in time-division and frequency-division duplex systems. A unified notation is used throughout to allow direct comparison between model families. Numerical examples are drawn from published measurements on GaN and LDMOS devices in the 700 MHz–6 GHz range. The chapter concludes with a discussion of challenges introduced by carrier aggregation and 5G NR waveforms, including crest-factor reduction interaction with DPD.

title: Constitutive overexpression of CYP81A-type genes in metabolically resistant Amaranthus retroflexus: transcript abundance and correlation with resistance level
abstract: RNA was extracted from leaf tissue of 18 A. retroflexus plants spanning a range of resistance factors (1.4–18.6) to imazethapyr, with and without confirmed ALS target-site mutations. Quantitative RT-PCR was performed using primers designed for CYP81A-type cytochrome P450 sequences identified by BLAST alignment against publicly available Amaranthus transcriptome assemblies. Normalisation was carried out against three reference genes (EF-1α, GAPDH, UBQ10) using the geometric mean method. Plants with resistance factors above 8 and no target-site mutation showed 4.8- to 11.3-fold higher CYP81A-like transcript levels compared with the susceptible reference, while plants with target-site mutations showed only 1.0- to 2.1-fold differences. A Spearman correlation of 0.71 (p < 0.001) was found between CYP81A-like transcript abundance and resistance factor across mutation-negative plants. These data support constitutive upregulation of CYP81A-type genes as a primary driver of metabolic resistance in this weed.

title: Cross-resistance profiles in PPO inhibitor-treated Amaranthus retroflexus from soybean fields: whole-plant and enzymatic evidence
abstract: Populations of A. retroflexus from soybean fields where lactofen had been applied continuously for at least four seasons were assessed for resistance to PPO inhibitors. Whole-plant bioassays were run with lactofen, fomesafen, and acifluorfen at seven rates per compound. Eight of 16 populations displayed resistance factors above 5 for lactofen. Cross-resistance within the PPO inhibitor class was variable: all lactofen-resistant populations also showed resistance to fomesafen (RF 3.1–9.4), while only four showed elevated tolerance to acifluorfen (RF 2.0–4.1). PPO enzyme activity was extracted from etiolated seedling shoots and measured by spectrophotometric protoporphyrin IX accumulation assay. Km values for the PPO substrate did not differ significantly between resistant and susceptible populations. In contrast, Vmax ratios suggested higher total PPO activity in resistant plants, potentially through target enzyme amplification rather than altered substrate affinity. Sequencing of the PPX2L gene is ongoing.

title: Stacked resistance mechanisms in a multiple-resistant Amaranthus retroflexus biotype: ALS mutation, CYP-mediated metabolism, and reduced leaf uptake
abstract: A single A. retroflexus biotype collected from a long-term sunflower monoculture in Bačka Palanka, showing resistance to both imazethapyr and tribenuron-methyl with resistance factors exceeding 50, was characterised in detail to disentangle the contribution of three putative resistance mechanisms. Sequencing confirmed a Trp574Leu ALS mutation in all 20 plants analysed. PBO co-treatment reduced the GR50 for imazethapyr by a further 6.3-fold beyond the effect of the target-site mutation alone, indicating an additive metabolic component. Foliar uptake and translocation were quantified using 14C-imazethapyr applied to intact leaves enclosed in treatment chambers: resistant plants absorbed 31 ± 5% of applied radioactivity at 48 h versus 54 ± 7% in the susceptible reference, pointing to a reduced uptake component. Cuticle composition analysis by GC-MS showed a higher proportion of long-chain alkanes in resistant plants. Taken together, three mechanisms—target-site mutation, CYP metabolism, and reduced foliar uptake—accumulate in this biotype, with each contributing measurably to the overall resistance phenotype.

title: Herbicide resistance diagnostics for Vojvodina arable weed management: a practical guide for extension services
abstract: This book chapter reviews and synthesises the methods used for routine herbicide resistance diagnostics applicable under the resource constraints typical of extension laboratory settings in Serbia and comparable countries. Covered methods include the petri-dish seedling test, whole-plant dose–response bioassay, chlorophyll fluorescence inhibition screening, ALS enzyme extraction and activity assay, and rapid PCR-based detection of the most prevalent target-site mutations (Pro197, Trp574 in ALS; Ser264 in psbA). For each method, practical guidance is given on sample sizes, adequate controls, and decision thresholds for designating a population as resistant. Case examples from Vojvodina field surveys between 2014 and 2022 are used to illustrate interpretation of ambiguous results and the importance of confirming putative resistance with at least two independent lines of evidence. The chapter is intended for use by certified crop advisors and plant protection inspectors rather than specialist research laboratories, and deliberately avoids techniques requiring radioisotope licensing.

title: Glutathione S-transferase activity profiles across susceptible and resistant Chenopodium album populations under sub-lethal tribenuron-methyl exposure
abstract: Ten C. album populations with varying resistance factors to tribenuron-methyl (RF 1.1–22.4) were used to profile glutathione S-transferase (GST) activity in response to sub-lethal herbicide exposure. Total soluble protein was extracted from shoot tissue at 0, 6, 24, and 72 h after treatment at one-tenth of the field rate. GST activity towards 1-chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene (CDNB) was measured spectrophotometrically. Populations with RF > 10 consistently showed higher constitutive GST activity (1.8- to 3.4-fold over susceptible controls at 0 h) and a more pronounced induction response at 24 h. Populations with confirmed psbA Ser264Gly mutations but susceptible to ALS inhibitors showed constitutive GST activity indistinguishable from the fully susceptible reference, indicating that elevated GST is not a generic stress response to the psbA mutation but is linked to ALS inhibitor tolerance. Native PAGE zymograms revealed additional faint GST isoform bands in the high-resistance populations. Protein identification of these bands by LC-MS/MS is under way.

title: Soil compaction modifies root crown angle in maize but not in sunflower: a two-year field experiment on Chernozem
abstract: Soil compaction is widespread in Vojvodina due to repeated heavy machinery use on fine-textured Chernozem soils. We investigated whether experimentally imposed compaction (target bulk density 1.55 g cm⁻³ vs. 1.30 g cm⁻³ in control plots) altered root crown architecture traits in four maize hybrids and four sunflower inbred-line test-crosses over two growing seasons (2019–2020). Compaction was created by repeated passes of a loaded tractor before planting; soil penetration resistance was verified with a cone penetrometer at 10 cm intervals. Root crowns were excavated by shovelomics at V8 (maize) and R1 (sunflower). In maize, compaction significantly increased mean nodal root angle by 4.8° (P < 0.001) and reduced lateral root density by 19%; effects were consistent across all four hybrids. In sunflower, no significant effect of compaction on any measured trait was observed. Compaction reduced maize grain yield by 14% on average. The divergent response suggests that the tap-rooted architecture of sunflower provides greater mechanical tolerance to high bulk density compared to the fibrous-rooted maize crown.

title: Variogram analysis of topsoil electrical conductivity measured by EM38 in a salt-affected field in northern Vojvodina
abstract: Apparent electrical conductivity (ECa) measured with an EM38 electromagnetic induction sensor was used to characterise spatial variability of topsoil salinity in a 45-hectare salt-affected field near Bačko Gradište, Serbia. A total of 312 georeferenced ECa readings collected along transects at 10-metre intervals were analysed by fitting spherical, exponential, and Gaussian theoretical variogram models. The spherical model provided the best fit (nugget-to-sill ratio 0.18), indicating strong spatial structure with a range of approximately 87 metres. Cross-validation with leave-one-out ordinary kriging yielded a root mean squared error of 1.4 mS/m and a mean error close to zero. Interpolated ECa maps were compared with 42 soil core measurements of electrical conductivity of the saturation extract (ECe). The Pearson correlation between predicted ECa and measured ECe was 0.81, confirming the utility of EM38 data as a surrogate for direct salinity measurements in this landscape. Results suggest that a transect spacing of 15 metres would be sufficient for capturing the dominant spatial patterns without significant loss of mapping accuracy.

title: Isolation frequency and species diversity of Pythium spp. from carrot fields in Vojvodina: a two-season survey
abstract: Damping-off and root dieback of processing carrot (Daucus carota subsp. sativus) have intensified in Vojvodina since the wet spring of 2021, yet species-level attribution of causal agents remains incomplete for the region. Soil and root samples were collected from 38 commercial carrot fields across six municipalities during the 2022 and 2023 growing seasons. Isolation on selective PARP medium yielded 214 oomycete cultures, of which 178 were assigned to Pythium using ITS and cox2 sequencing. Six species were identified: P. ultimum var. ultimum (44 %), P. irregulare (21 %), P. sylvaticum (14 %), P. dissotocum (9 %), P. aphanidermatum (7 %), and P. helicoides (5 %). Pathogenicity was confirmed for all species by seedling inoculation assays at 15 °C and 25 °C under controlled conditions. P. ultimum var. ultimum dominated in fields with heavier soils and later planting dates, while P. aphanidermatum was associated with lighter soils and July sowing. The survey provides a baseline species inventory and preliminary habitat associations needed for subsequent population-genetic work across the Pannonian Plain.

title: Byzantine-Robust Aggregation Under Local Differential Privacy Constraints
abstract: Federated learning systems face two simultaneous threats: privacy leakage toward the aggregator and Byzantine clients that submit corrupted model updates. We study whether standard Byzantine-robust aggregation rules—coordinate-wise median, trimmed mean, and Krum—remain effective when client updates are additionally perturbed for local differential privacy. We show analytically that the coordinate-wise median rule retains its Byzantine tolerance when the fraction of malicious clients is below 1/4, provided the LDP noise scale is below a threshold that we characterise in terms of model dimension and ε. Above this threshold, Byzantine clients can craft updates that are indistinguishable from honest noisy updates, defeating the robust rule. We verify these claims in a simulation with a 32-dimensional linear model, 100 clients, and up to 20 Byzantine clients using a sign-flip attack. Practical guidelines for choosing ε in adversarial deployments are provided.

title: Slow oscillation–spindle coupling in drug-resistant focal epilepsy: relationship to overnight memory consolidation
abstract: Slow oscillation–spindle coupling during NREM sleep is considered a mechanism of hippocampus-dependent memory consolidation. We tested whether this coupling is disrupted in drug-resistant focal epilepsy and whether disruption predicts declarative memory performance. Forty-two patients and 35 controls underwent overnight polysomnography with simultaneous 64-channel EEG. Spindle events were detected automatically and phase-locked to slow oscillations (<1 Hz). Coupling strength was quantified as modulation index. Patients showed reduced modulation index compared with controls (0.038 vs 0.061, p<0.001), with the largest reductions ipsilateral to the seizure onset zone. Coupling reduction was associated with worse next-morning performance on a word-pair recall task (r=0.47, p=0.002) even after controlling for seizure frequency and medication load. IED density during N2 was negatively associated with modulation index (r=−0.39, p=0.011). These findings link electrophysiological sleep disruption to a measurable functional consequence and suggest that improving coupling could be a treatment target.

title: Seasonal variation in baseline antioxidant enzyme activities in Gammarus fossarum from unpolluted streams in the Fruška Gora region
abstract: Establishing seasonal baseline values for antioxidant enzyme activities in reference organisms is a prerequisite for meaningful biomarker studies. This study measured SOD, CAT, glutathione peroxidase (GPx), and glutathione S-transferase (GST) activities in Gammarus fossarum collected monthly over 14 months from three unpolluted headwater streams in Fruška Gora National Park. Metal concentrations in stream water were consistently below detection thresholds for copper, cadmium, and lead throughout the sampling period. SOD and CAT activities showed significant seasonal variation (ANOVA, p < 0.001), peaking in February–March and reaching minima in July–August, likely linked to temperature-driven metabolic changes. GPx and GST activities were less variable seasonally. No significant differences were detected among the three sites for any enzyme. The dataset provides reference ranges for each enzyme and season that can be applied in field ecotoxicology studies using G. fossarum as a sentinel species in the Pannonian region.

title: Point Economies and Learner Motivation in a Pilot Serbian-as-a-Second-Language Module for Hungarian-Speaking Students
abstract: This study examined how a simple point-and-level reward structure affected voluntary usage of a web-based Serbian language module among Hungarian-speaking students at secondary schools near Subotica. The module covered basic conversational Serbian across six thematic units. In a six-week trial, 83 students were randomly assigned to a version with visible point counters, level badges, and a class leaderboard, or to an identical version with all reward displays hidden. Session logs showed that the reward-visible group initiated 2.3 times more voluntary review sessions per student per week. However, performance on graded written assessments did not differ significantly between groups (mean scores 64.1 vs. 62.7 out of 100). Qualitative interviews with 24 participants suggested that students valued the sense of progress more than competitive standing, and several found the leaderboard demotivating when they fell behind peers. The paper discusses the mismatch between engagement metrics and learning outcomes, and recommends separating progress indicators from competitive displays in minority-language learning contexts.

title: An Item Response Theory Approach to Adaptive Exercise Selection in a Grammar Drill Platform
abstract: This paper reports the integration of a one-parameter logistic IRT model into an online grammar drill platform to drive real-time exercise selection. Item difficulty parameters were estimated offline from a corpus of 18,400 completed exercises collected from 312 students over two academic years. At runtime, the platform selected the next exercise whose estimated difficulty was closest to the current ability estimate for each student, updating the estimate after each response using a maximum likelihood step. A prospective study with 94 students in introductory university Serbian courses compared the adaptive version against a version using random selection within difficulty bands. Over ten weeks, the adaptive group required 17 percent fewer exercises to reach an 80 percent accuracy criterion on a standardised grammar test. The paper provides a detailed account of item bank construction, calibration procedures, and the practical constraints of running IRT estimation on server hardware available in 2005. Limitations include item exposure imbalance and the absence of guessing-parameter estimation.

title: Designing Feedback Timing in Computer-Based Language Exercises: Immediate, Delayed, and Summary Conditions
abstract: Feedback timing is a persistent variable in drill-and-practice research, yet most deployed platforms default to immediate error correction without empirical justification. This experiment assigned 174 first-year students across three faculties in Novi Sad to one of three feedback conditions in an online English reading comprehension module: immediate sentence-level feedback after each answer, delayed feedback at the end of each ten-item block, or summary feedback at the end of the session only. Students completed eight sessions over four weeks. Comprehension scores on matched transfer texts were highest in the delayed condition (mean 72.1 out of 100) compared to immediate (67.4) and summary (65.8), with a significant main effect (F(2,171)=4.83, p=0.009). Time-on-task was shortest in the immediate condition. Think-aloud data from a sub-sample of 18 students indicated that immediate feedback disrupted inference-building for longer texts. The paper recommends configurable feedback windows rather than fixed platform defaults, and provides a decision rubric based on exercise type and target skill.

title: Learner-Facing Difficulty Labels and Their Effect on Task Persistence in an Online Language Platform
abstract: Most adaptive systems adjust difficulty silently, without informing the learner of the system's current assessment of their level. This study investigated whether displaying explicit difficulty labels ('beginner', 'intermediate', 'advanced') on exercise cards affected persistence and performance among adult learners using a free online Croatian-language module. A between-subjects design with 220 registered users compared labeled and unlabeled interface versions over a self-paced four-week period. Users in the labeled condition completed on average 34 more exercises per person (p=0.03) and were less likely to abandon a session mid-exercise (abandonment rate 9.1% vs. 14.6%). Performance differences on a post-use proficiency task were not significant. Open-ended survey responses suggested that the labels helped users set expectations and reduced frustration when an exercise proved harder than anticipated. The paper discusses implications for transparent learner modeling and cautions that label granularity matters: a five-point scale piloted in a smaller sample produced higher anxiety than the three-point scale reported here.

title: A Comparative Review of Difficulty Adaptation Algorithms in Open-Source Language Learning Platforms, 2005–2012
abstract: This book chapter surveys the adaptation mechanisms present in seven open-source or publicly documented language learning platforms released between 2005 and 2012. For each platform, the authors describe the student model used (if any), the exercise selection or sequencing algorithm, the granularity of the difficulty dimension, and the evidence base cited in the platform documentation. Platforms examined include systems built on Moodle plugins, standalone Java applications, and two early browser-based environments. The analysis finds that five of the seven systems relied on threshold rules rather than probabilistic models, that only two systems updated difficulty estimates within a session rather than only between sessions, and that none provided a documented calibration procedure for item difficulty values. The chapter identifies four recurring design gaps: absence of item exposure controls, conflation of speed and accuracy into a single performance signal, lack of support for multi-skill learning objectives, and missing fallback behaviour when the item bank is exhausted at a given difficulty tier. Each gap is illustrated with interaction log excerpts from published studies.

title: Badge Design Parameters and Their Differential Effects on Low- and High-Performing Learners in a Grammar Tutoring System
abstract: Badge-based reward systems are widely adopted in educational software, but empirical guidance on design parameters such as badge frequency, visual salience, and social visibility remains sparse. This study systematically varied three badge design parameters in a within-subjects factorial experiment using a Latin square design with 96 university students using an online German grammar tutor over six weeks. Dependent variables included voluntary session count, exercise completion rate, and grammar post-test scores. Main effects were found for badge frequency (F(2,93)=6.12, p=0.003) and social visibility (F(1,94)=4.47, p=0.037) on session count, but not on post-test scores. Stratified analysis showed that low-performing students (bottom quartile on pre-test) responded more positively to frequent, low-threshold badges, while high-performing students showed slight negative effects of high-frequency badges on engagement. Visual salience had no significant main effect. The paper provides concrete parameter recommendations for practitioners and discusses floor and ceiling effects in badge-based motivation designs.

title: Longitudinal Decay of Gamification Effects in a University Language Learning Platform: A Four-Year Follow-Up
abstract: Much gamification research measures effects over weeks rather than semesters. This paper reports a four-year observational follow-up of a cohort of 211 students who were initially exposed to a gamified English for Academic Purposes platform during the 2010–2011 academic year. Annual voluntary usage logs were collected for each subsequent year, supplemented by annual 12-item motivation surveys. Median voluntary session counts declined from 14.3 in year one to 3.1 in year four, with the steepest drop between years one and two. Students who had scored in the upper half on initial engagement measures retained above-median usage longer, but the effect attenuated by year three. Survey data indicated that novelty was cited as the primary initial motivator by 68 percent of respondents, and only 21 percent reported the reward mechanics as a continued reason for use in year three or four. The paper argues that gamification in formal educational platforms functions as an onboarding mechanism rather than a sustained engagement driver, and recommends phased reward designs that evolve with learner familiarity.

title: Revisiting Adaptive Difficulty in Language Apps: What Has Changed Since 2010 and What Has Not
abstract: This co-authored position paper, written with colleagues active in current research, revisits the state of adaptive difficulty in mobile and web language learning applications a decade after an earlier survey. The paper examines ten widely used application categories documented in the research literature between 2017 and 2024, assessing changes in the underlying adaptation mechanisms against the baseline gaps identified in a 2013 review. Key findings are that probabilistic student modeling has become more common, driven largely by the availability of machine learning libraries, but that item calibration practices remain poorly documented in most systems. Social comparison features have proliferated, often without evidence-based design rationale. The paper identifies new concerns absent from earlier work, including the use of streaks as a retention mechanism and the privacy implications of granular learner data collection by commercial platform operators. Recommendations are oriented toward platform evaluators and procurement decision-makers in educational institutions rather than platform developers.

title: Batched Low-Rank Updates for Domain Decomposition Preconditioners in Repeated Assembly–Solve Cycles
abstract: In manufacturing simulation workflows, the geometry and material distribution of a component remain fixed while boundary conditions or load cases change across dozens of solves. Each change in loading alters the global stiffness matrix only locally—near applied forces and contacts—making a full preconditioner rebuild wasteful. This paper proposes a batched low-rank update strategy for BDDC and one-level additive Schwarz preconditioners, where only the affected subdomain factors are refactored and the coarse problem is updated via a bordered system solve. The update cost is proportional to the number of altered subdomains rather than total problem size. Tests on a stamping-die simulation with 2.3 million degrees of freedom and 80 load cases show that the update strategy reduces total preconditioner build time by 61% while increasing solve-phase iteration counts by no more than 8% compared to fresh builds. An error indicator based on the local residual is proposed to trigger full rebuilds when updates accumulate.

title: Explainability Methods for Time-Series Classification: Adapting SHAP to Temporal Feature Structures
abstract: SHAP values are well understood for tabular data, but their application to time-series classification raises questions about how to define meaningful coalitions of temporal features. This paper examines three strategies for grouping time steps into coalitions — contiguous windows, wavelet-band grouping, and learned segment boundaries — and compares their effect on explanation quality when applied to a univariate industrial sensor dataset (vibration readings from a compressor, 8,400 samples, 120 time steps each) used to classify fault types. A convolutional neural network trained on this data achieves 91.4% classification accuracy. Explanation quality is assessed via a deletion metric: progressively masking features identified as important and measuring accuracy drop. Window-based grouping with an adaptive overlap procedure produces the steepest accuracy-deletion curve, suggesting higher explanation relevance. Computational cost remains manageable; full SHAP estimation takes under 4 minutes per batch on a mid-range GPU.

title: Explainable AI in Regulated Industries: A Practitioner's Guide to Selecting Post-Hoc Methods
abstract: This book chapter surveys the landscape of post-hoc explainability methods from the perspective of practitioners working under regulatory constraints, including the EU General Data Protection Regulation and forthcoming AI Act provisions. The chapter organises methods along two axes: the level of explanation (local versus global) and the type of model assumption (model-agnostic versus model-specific). For each category, the chapter discusses what the method can and cannot guarantee about faithfulness to the underlying model, what documentation artefacts can be derived from it, and what computational resources are typically required. Case studies drawn from credit risk, insurance underwriting, and automated triage are used to illustrate trade-offs. The chapter concludes with a decision flowchart intended to help compliance teams select a suitable explanation approach given their model class, data type, and regulatory reporting requirements. No new empirical results are presented.

title: Evaluating Consistency of SHAP Explanations Across Model Retraining Cycles in Production Systems
abstract: Machine learning models deployed in production are periodically retrained on new data. Each retraining cycle may produce a model with similar predictive performance but different internal structure, potentially yielding different SHAP explanations for the same input. This paper quantifies explanation drift — the change in SHAP value vectors for a fixed set of 1,000 held-out test instances across 12 monthly retraining cycles — for a gradient-boosted tree model used in a fictional financial services context. Explanation drift is measured as the cosine distance between SHAP vectors before and after retraining and as rank-order correlation of feature attributions. Over 12 cycles, mean cosine distance accumulates to 0.18, and the top-three feature set changes for 31% of instances. The paper proposes a monitoring statistic based on median cosine distance that can trigger a fairness and explainability re-audit when it exceeds a threshold calibrated on a held-out validation window.

title: Fairness Auditing of a Municipal Social Benefit Allocation Algorithm: Methodology and Findings
abstract: This paper reports an external fairness audit of an automated scoring system used by a mid-sized Serbian municipality to prioritise applicants for a means-tested housing assistance programme. The audit was conducted under a data access agreement and covered 6,800 applications submitted over three years. The system's scoring formula is partially transparent; audit access included the scoring code but not training data. Demographic data were obtained by linking application records with census microdata using approximate matching. Four fairness criteria are evaluated: demographic parity, equalised odds, calibration, and individual fairness via a similarity metric defined over observable financial features. The system satisfies demographic parity at the aggregate level but exhibits an equalised odds gap of 0.11 between applicants of Roma and non-Roma ethnicity, driven largely by differential error rates in the income imputation sub-module. Remediation options including re-calibrating the imputation model and adding an ethnicity-blind income proxy are discussed with their legal and operational implications.

title: Comparing Global Surrogate Model Complexity and Accuracy Trade-offs for Regulatory Reporting
abstract: Global surrogate models fit a simple interpretable model (typically a shallow decision tree or linear model) to the input-output behaviour of a complex black box. Regulatory frameworks increasingly require that institutions provide comprehensible model documentation, making surrogate depth and fidelity a practical engineering choice. This paper systematically varies surrogate tree depth from 2 to 12 and measures fidelity (R² and area under the ROC curve relative to the black-box labels) and comprehensibility (number of leaves, depth, and a human-rated clarity score from a panel of 20 domain experts) across five datasets. A Pareto frontier analysis identifies depth-4 and depth-5 trees as consistently near-optimal across both dimensions. The paper further tests whether fidelity improvements from increasing depth beyond 6 are statistically significant using a permutation test, finding that they rarely are for datasets under 50,000 instances. Recommendations for regulatory documentation templates are included.

title: Uncertainty Quantification for SHAP Values: A Bootstrap Confidence Interval Framework
abstract: SHAP values are typically reported as point estimates, but any estimate derived from a finite sample carries uncertainty that is rarely communicated to end users or auditors. This paper develops a bootstrap-based confidence interval framework for KernelSHAP and TreeSHAP, estimating interval width as a function of background dataset size, model complexity, and input point location in feature space. Experiments on four tabular datasets (ranging from 3,000 to 120,000 instances) show that 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for individual feature attributions are wide enough to include zero for the second and third ranked features in 44% of cases with background sets of 100 samples, dropping to 18% with 1,000 samples. The paper provides guidelines for minimum background set size under different desired interval widths and discusses implications for audit reports that rely on single-run SHAP estimates. An accompanying Python library implements the interval estimation.

title: Embedded Wavelet Lifting for ECG Compression on Wearable Cortex-M0 Nodes
abstract: Electrocardiogram data transmitted from chest-patch wearables place a disproportionate load on BLE bandwidth. We ported a fixed-point integer lifting-scheme wavelet transform (5/3 Le Gall filter) to an ARM Cortex-M0 running at 48 MHz and paired it with a simple threshold quantiser and arithmetic coder. The implementation stores all intermediate coefficients in 12 kB of SRAM, fitting within the budget of low-cost microcontrollers. Compression was evaluated on 30-minute, two-lead recordings from 18 subjects sampled at 500 Hz. The scheme achieved a mean compression ratio of 9.4:1 at a percent root-mean-square difference (PRD) of 2.7%, which is within the clinically acceptable range for rhythm monitoring. QRS peak locations in reconstructed signals deviated by a mean of 1.2 ms from reference annotations. Runtime was 1.8 ms per 500-sample frame, leaving the processor idle for 64% of each sampling period. Power consumption during active compression was 3.1 mW.

title: Equity Implications of a Proposed Bus Network Restructuring in Novi Sad: A Before–After Isochrone Analysis
abstract: In 2016 the City of Novi Sad prepared a draft bus network restructuring plan that would consolidate 22 lines into 18 higher-frequency routes. This paper evaluates the accessibility equity implications of that plan by comparing 30-minute isochrones from every residential building polygon before and after the proposed change. Routing was performed in OpenTripPlanner using peak-hour (07:30–09:00) departure windows with 60-second resolution. A Gini coefficient of transit accessibility was computed for both scenarios, disaggregated by income quintile estimated from 2011 census housing quality indicators. The restructuring would improve median accessibility by 8.4% but increase the Gini coefficient from 0.31 to 0.34, disproportionately disadvantaging low-income tracts in the northern industrial periphery. The paper recommends three targeted line modifications to reduce this equity gap without increasing operating costs by more than 4%.

title: Reactive distillation for ethyl propanoate synthesis: column design, steady-state multiplicity, and experimental validation
abstract: A reactive distillation column (RDC) for acid-catalysed synthesis of ethyl propanoate was designed, simulated, and tested at pilot scale (column diameter 50 mm, 12 reactive stages, Amberlyst-15 catalyst packing, 200 g per stage). Steady-state simulations using a non-equilibrium stage model predicted the existence of three steady states at certain feed compositions; experimental operation confirmed bistable behaviour with switching hysteresis between high-conversion (ethyl propanoate 97.2 mol%) and low-conversion (34.8 mol%) states depending on reboiler duty trajectory. Total acid conversion under stable high-conversion operation was 99.1% at a feed flow rate of 0.8 L/h (equimolar propionic acid and ethanol). Catalyst mechanical stability was assessed by sieve analysis before and after 200 h operation, showing less than 3% fines generation. Column energy demand was 2.7 kW per kg/h of ester produced, approximately 15% lower than a conventional reactor-separator sequence modelled under the same throughput.

title: Measurement invariance of observational executive function tasks across age groups from 36 to 84 months
abstract: Three observational EF tasks developed by the Novi Sad group were administered to 328 children distributed across five 12-month age bands from 36 to 84 months to test measurement invariance across the preschool period. Multigroup confirmatory factor models were estimated for configural, metric, and scalar invariance. Results indicated configural and metric invariance across all age bands but only partial scalar invariance: two item intercepts showed significant non-invariance at the youngest band (36–48 months). Practical implications of partial invariance are quantified using latent mean difference estimates with and without constraining non-invariant intercepts. The pattern suggests that the tasks measure the same constructs across the preschool period but that direct score comparisons at the youngest ages should be interpreted cautiously. Suggestions for item revision to achieve full scalar invariance are discussed, along with considerations for longitudinal tracking studies that span a wide age range.

title: Topology optimization with self-supporting constraints
abstract: This paper presents a topology optimization framework that incorporates self-supporting geometric constraints, enabling the direct manufacture of optimized components via selective laser melting without the need for additional support structures. Traditional topology optimization methods generate geometries that frequently include overhanging features below a critical angle, necessitating supports that increase material consumption, post-processing effort, and surface roughness. The proposed method integrates a continuous overhang constraint formulated in the density field, penalizing the formation of unsupported material during the optimization iteration. The constraint is implemented within a SIMP-based (Solid Isotropic Material with Penalization) optimization algorithm and applied to benchmark mechanical loading cases. Comparative studies show that self-supporting designs achieve structural performance within 8–15% of unconstrained optima while completely eliminating critical overhangs. The computational overhead introduced by the constraint evaluation is analyzed and shown to be acceptable for practical part sizes. Experimental validation is carried out by printing selected optimized geometries in Ti-6Al-4V and assessing support-free printability. The framework demonstrates a viable path toward fully automated, support-free design-to-manufacture workflows in metal additive manufacturing.

title: Effect of scanning strategy on microstructure and mechanical anisotropy in SLM-produced AlSi10Mg parts
abstract: Selective laser melting of AlSi10Mg aluminum alloy is gaining traction for lightweight structural applications, yet the influence of scanning strategy on resulting microstructure and mechanical anisotropy remains incompletely understood. This study systematically evaluates four scanning strategies—unidirectional, bidirectional, island, and rotating stripe—applied to identical part geometries under otherwise fixed process parameters. Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) and optical microscopy are used to characterize grain morphology, texture, and melt pool geometry. Tensile specimens extracted in three orientations are tested to quantify anisotropy in ultimate tensile strength, yield strength, and elongation at break. Results demonstrate that the rotating stripe strategy produces the most isotropic mechanical response and the finest average grain size, attributed to more uniform thermal gradient distribution. Island scanning yields the highest porosity among the tested strategies under the selected parameters. A correlation between melt pool aspect ratio and degree of columnar grain growth is established. These findings provide actionable guidance for selecting scanning strategies in applications where directional mechanical performance must be controlled, and form the basis for a process-structure-property linkage model applicable to powder-bed fusion of aluminum alloys.

title: Gradient lattice infill generation for metal additive manufacturing using topology-driven density maps
abstract: This work presents a computational methodology for generating functionally graded lattice infill structures for metal additive manufacturing components, driven by stress-based density maps derived from topology optimization. Rather than applying uniform lattice patterns, the proposed approach maps local von Mises stress distributions onto a library of strut-based unit cells—including body-centered cubic, face-centered cubic, and octet-truss variants—scaling cell size and strut diameter continuously according to normalized stress intensity. The resulting gradient lattice geometries are evaluated for printability in selective laser melting by analyzing strut inclination angles and minimum feature sizes relative to machine capabilities. Finite element simulations of the gradient lattice components are compared against both solid and uniform lattice counterparts, showing up to 34% mass reduction while maintaining structural compliance within a 5% margin. Physical specimens in 316L stainless steel are produced and subjected to compressive and three-point bending tests, confirming the simulation predictions with deviations below 7%. The methodology is implemented as a parametric design pipeline compatible with standard CAD and slicing software environments, making it accessible for industrial application. This contribution bridges topology optimization and lattice design in a unified workflow targeting the metal additive manufacturing context.

title: Thermal residual stress prediction in SLM components using layer-by-layer finite element simulation
abstract: Residual stresses arising from the rapid thermal cycles inherent to selective laser melting significantly affect dimensional accuracy, fatigue life, and susceptibility to cracking in as-built metal components. This paper develops a layer-by-layer finite element thermal-mechanical simulation framework capable of predicting residual stress distributions in SLM-fabricated parts without requiring per-scan resolution, thereby achieving a practical balance between accuracy and computational cost. The model employs an equivalent heat source calibrated against melt pool geometry measurements and incorporates temperature-dependent material properties for 316L stainless steel. A thermo-elasto-plastic constitutive model accounts for phase transformation effects. Simulation predictions of residual stress magnitudes and distributions are validated against neutron diffraction measurements performed on benchmark geometries. The framework is then applied to investigate the influence of substrate preheating temperatures ranging from 20°C to 300°C on residual stress reduction. Results show that preheating at 200°C reduces peak tensile residual stresses by approximately 40%, with diminishing returns at higher temperatures. The model is further used to evaluate the effect of part orientation and scanning strategy rotation angle. This work provides a validated numerical tool for guiding process planning decisions aimed at minimizing distortion and residual stress in SLM production.

title: Support structure optimization for overhanging features in metal powder-bed fusion: a review and comparative assessment
abstract: Support structures are indispensable in metal powder-bed fusion processes yet represent a significant source of material waste, build time, and post-processing effort. This book chapter provides a comprehensive review of support structure optimization strategies developed over the past decade, encompassing geometric design, topology-based approaches, and machine learning-assisted generation methods. The review is organized around three primary objectives: minimizing support volume, ensuring thermal management and part anchoring during the build, and facilitating clean removal without surface damage. Particular attention is given to lattice and fractal support architectures, breakaway interface designs, and integrated topology optimization frameworks that produce self-supporting geometries. Comparative assessment criteria are defined across printability, mechanical adequacy, removability, and computational cost. The chapter also identifies open research challenges, including the lack of standardized benchmarks for support performance evaluation and the limited integration of residual stress considerations into support optimization workflows. Case studies in stainless steel and titanium alloys are used throughout to illustrate the comparative performance of selected methods. The chapter concludes with a roadmap for future development, highlighting the potential of combined build-orientation and support co-optimization strategies to substantially reduce support dependency in industrial metal additive manufacturing practice.

title: Pore morphology classification in SLM-printed metals using convolutional neural networks applied to micro-CT images
abstract: Accurate classification of pore morphology in selectively laser melted components is critical for diagnosing process defects and guiding parameter correction. This study presents a deep learning pipeline based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained on micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) image stacks to automatically classify pores into keyhole, lack-of-fusion, and gas pore categories. A labeled dataset of 4,200 individual pore instances was constructed from 316L stainless steel specimens manufactured under deliberately varied process parameters to induce each defect type. Three-dimensional pore features including sphericity, elongation ratio, nearest-neighbor distance, and orientation relative to build direction were extracted and used as auxiliary inputs alongside raw image patches in a hybrid CNN-feature fusion architecture. The model achieves a classification accuracy of 94.3% on a held-out test set, outperforming prior morphology threshold-based classifiers by a margin of 11%. Grad-CAM visualization confirms that the network focuses on physically meaningful geometric features. The pipeline is integrated into a semi-automated quality assessment workflow that produces per-specimen defect maps linked to local process parameter deviations. This tool enables rapid, objective defect characterization that can inform closed-loop process control strategies in industrial SLM environments, reducing reliance on manual metallographic inspection.

title: Multi-objective topology optimization balancing stiffness, thermal conductivity, and printability for SLM components
abstract: Engineering components produced by selective laser melting increasingly serve multi-physical functions, requiring simultaneous optimization of structural stiffness and thermal performance. This paper formulates and solves a multi-objective topology optimization problem targeting concurrent maximization of structural stiffness and effective thermal conductivity while enforcing a self-supporting printability constraint. The problem is cast as a weighted-sum Pareto optimization within a density-based SIMP framework extended with anisotropic thermal conductivity interpolation. The printability constraint is implemented as a cumulative overhang measure that penalizes designs containing angles below 45° relative to the build platform. A sensitivity filtering scheme adapted for multi-physics problems prevents checkerboard instabilities. Pareto fronts are computed for a range of weighting coefficients and analyzed to identify compromise designs. Selected Pareto-optimal geometries are fabricated in 316L stainless steel and evaluated through mechanical testing and thermographic imaging under controlled heat flux boundary conditions. Experimental results confirm that the multi-objective optimization framework produces physically valid designs that satisfy both performance objectives with deviations of less than 10% from predicted values. The framework is demonstrated on a heat exchanger bracket application, showing meaningful improvements over single-objective benchmarks. This contribution addresses a growing need for integrated design tools in multi-functional metal additive manufacturing.

title: Benchmarking powder flowability and layer uniformity for stainless steel powders used in selective laser melting
abstract: Powder quality is a fundamental determinant of part integrity in selective laser melting, yet standardized characterization protocols for correlating powder properties to as-built density and surface quality remain underdeveloped for industrial practice. This study benchmarks five commercially sourced 316L stainless steel powder batches using a comprehensive suite of flowability and morphology metrics: Hall flow rate, Carr index, Hausner ratio, angle of repose, laser diffraction particle size distribution, and scanning electron microscopy morphology assessment. Powder spreading experiments on a laboratory-scale recoating testbench quantify layer density uniformity and the formation of streaking defects as a function of powder characteristics. Correlation analysis reveals that powder batches with a D50 in the range of 28–35 μm and sphericity above 0.92 consistently produce the most uniform deposited layers. SLM build experiments using identical process parameters across all batches demonstrate that layer uniformity metrics derived from the recoating testbench predict as-built relative density with a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.89. Recycled powder behavior after up to five reuse cycles is also assessed, showing measurable degradation in flowability and a 0.3% average reduction in relative density by the fifth cycle. The study provides practical threshold values for incoming powder quality control applicable to production environments.

title: Sensitivity of fatigue life estimates for welded bridge connections to WIM measurement uncertainty and traffic extrapolation assumptions
abstract: WIM-based fatigue assessments inevitably involve two sources of uncertainty: sensor calibration errors affecting the measured load spectrum and statistical assumptions used to extrapolate short records to the design life. This paper quantifies the sensitivity of fatigue life estimates to both sources for a representative set of welded steel bridge connections. WIM calibration uncertainty was characterised from repeated static weighing trials at a test site, yielding a relative standard deviation of 4.3% for gross vehicle weight. Extrapolation uncertainty was assessed by comparing damage estimates from subsampled records of 3, 6, 12 and 24 months drawn from a 36-month baseline dataset. For FAT 71 and FAT 90 details on a 50 m span bridge, the 90th-percentile error in damage ratio due to calibration error alone was below 9%, while extrapolation from a 3-month record introduced errors up to 31%. Minimum monitoring duration recommendations are derived as a function of heavy vehicle flow rate and acceptable error tolerance.

title: Scalability Analysis of Evolutionary NAS under Strict Latency Budgets on Heterogeneous Embedded Targets
abstract: This paper studies how the difficulty of multi-objective NAS scales with the number of objectives and the strictness of latency constraints when targeting a heterogeneous set of three embedded platforms: an ARM Cortex-M4, a RISC-V MCU, and a low-power DSP. Latency is treated as a separate objective for each target, yielding a five-objective problem when combined with accuracy and model size. Experiments compare NSGA-III and a reference evolutionary strategy across search spaces of increasing depth (4, 8, and 12 cells). Hypervolume scales sub-linearly with the number of cells but degrades faster under tight latency budgets. An analysis of Pareto front collapse—where the feasible set shrinks to near-zero under the tightest constraints—is presented with practical implications for search space design. Results suggest that decoupling the latency constraints into soft penalties rather than hard objectives preserves Pareto front diversity without significant accuracy loss.

title: Heterotrophic plate count versus flow cytometry for monitoring microbial regrowth in treated water: a comparative field study
abstract: Heterotrophic plate count (HPC) on R2A agar and flow cytometry with SYBR Green I staining were applied in parallel to water samples from three waterworks in the Danube–Tisa–Danube canal catchment area over six months. Flow cytometric total cell counts were consistently 10–100-fold higher than HPC values, with the greatest divergence observed after secondary chlorination steps. Intact cell counts correlated positively with dissolved organic carbon levels (Spearman ρ = 0.63) but showed weaker correlation with turbidity. HPC proved insensitive to uncultivable fractions that comprised, on average, 92 % of the cytometrically enumerated population. Regression analysis indicated that neither method alone predicted downstream biofilm accumulation indices adequately; a combined index incorporating both measures performed better (R² = 0.71). Findings support incorporating flow cytometry into routine monitoring alongside HPC for a more complete picture of regrowth potential.

title: Crease-stiffness prediction for recycled cartonboard across a humidity range using near-infrared spectroscopy of incoming reels
abstract: Near-infrared (NIR) spectra were collected from reel samples of recycled grey cartonboard at the rewinder station of a carton-converting plant before conditioning. A partial least squares (PLS) regression model was trained using 210 reel samples with crease stiffness at 50 % and 75 % RH as response variables. Spectral pretreatment used standard normal variate correction and first-derivative transformation. The PLS model for crease stiffness at 75 % RH achieved a cross-validated RMSECV of 0.31 mN·m and an R² of 0.86 on a hold-out test set of 52 samples, enabling prediction before converting. Feature wavelengths identified as most informative (around 1450 and 1940 nm) correspond to OH-stretch overtones associated with fibre bonding and moisture accessibility. The approach was tested in a simulated inline scenario with a 2-second scan time, achieving prediction accuracy within ±7 % for 88 % of samples. The study offers a practical path to real-time sorting of incoming reels by their humidity-conditioned crease behaviour without destructive testing.

title: Does dual-task interference reveal hidden workload in expert operators? An eye-tracking and secondary-task study
abstract: Expert operators often appear to have spare cognitive capacity, but secondary-task methods have produced inconsistent results. This study combined oculomotor measurement with a secondary auditory reaction-time task to probe residual workload in 25 expert switchboard operators and 25 novices. During a primary fault-identification task, experts showed shorter mean fixation durations (196 ms vs. 289 ms) and faster secondary-task reaction times (M = 348 ms vs. 441 ms) than novices, confirming lower primary-task load. However, when task difficulty was increased by adding ambiguous fault signals, expert fixation durations increased by 48 ms and secondary-task RT degraded by 71 ms, indicating that residual capacity was not unlimited. Pupil dilation tracked both manipulations linearly. The combined approach proved more sensitive to graded difficulty changes than either method alone, with effect sizes for the combined index (d = 1.42) exceeding those of oculomotor-only (d = 0.98) or RT-only (d = 0.87) measures.
venue: Applied Cognitive Psychology

title: Eye-tracking patterns during reading of numerical and pictographic risk formats in pharmaceutical package inserts
abstract: Pharmaceutical package inserts routinely present adverse-event frequencies using natural frequencies, percentages, and the EU pictogram system. This study used eye-tracking to compare visual attention patterns during reading of three risk formats in a within-subjects design with 54 healthy adults. Participants read eight matched inserts (two per format, with one hybrid format), and fixation count, total dwell time, and first-pass regression rate were recorded using a Tobii TX300 system. Pictograms attracted significantly more first-pass fixations than numerical formats (F(2,106) = 18.7, p < .001, η² = .26), but comprehension accuracy—assessed by a post-reading forced-choice task—was highest for natural frequency text. Hybrid formats (frequency text accompanied by a simple icon array) produced both high attention and high comprehension scores. Subjective difficulty ratings were lowest for pictograms yet comprehension was lowest for stand-alone pictograms, indicating a fluency illusion. Recommendations for insert redesign are proposed.
venue: Proceedings of the Biennial European Conference on Health Communication

title: A Lumped-Parameter Digital Twin Architecture for Continuous Dielectric Ageing State Estimation in Buried 110 kV Cable Circuits
abstract: This paper proposes a digital twin structure for a 110 kV underground cable circuit composed of modular lumped-parameter elements representing discrete cable sections, joints, and terminations. Each element maintains a state vector encompassing conductor temperature, insulation loss factor, estimated void volume fraction, and a cumulative ageing index derived from an Arrhenius-based thermal ageing model. The twin is updated at 15-minute intervals using SCADA-sourced load current and soil temperature sensor readings from five measurement points distributed over a 4.2 km cable route in northern Serbia. Over a 14-month monitoring period, the predicted cumulative ageing index showed a mean absolute error of 4.1% against offline tan-delta measurements taken at four scheduled outages. Computational runtime per update cycle averaged 0.8 seconds on a standard workstation, making the approach suitable for real-time deployment. The paper also describes the data pipeline, sensor calibration procedure, and a rule-based alarm threshold scheme derived from IEC 60840 service guidelines.
venue: Electric Power Systems Research

title: Ploidy variation and morphological differentiation in the Sesleria caerulea complex along an altitudinal gradient in the Prokletije Mountains
abstract: The Sesleria caerulea species complex (Poaceae) in the Prokletije Mountains spans an altitudinal range from 900 m to 2,430 m a.s.l. and shows considerable morphological variability. We sampled 31 populations across this gradient, measured 14 morphological traits, and estimated ploidy by flow cytometry. Three ploidy levels were detected: diploid (2n = 2x = 26, six populations), tetraploid (2n = 4x = 52, twenty-one populations), and hexaploid (2n = 6x = 78, four populations). Diploids were restricted to low-altitude calcareous grasslands, whereas hexaploids occurred exclusively above 2,100 m. Tetraploids showed the broadest ecological and morphological amplitude. Morphological differentiation between ploidy levels was statistically significant for ligule length, culm width, and spikelet density, but extensive morphological overlap renders ploidy identification by morphology unreliable. Contact zones between diploids and tetraploids were identified at two localities; no mixed-ploidy individuals were detected by flow cytometry.

title: Heterochromatin composition and karyotype asymmetry in tetraploid Onosma species (Boraginaceae) from the Balkan hotspot
abstract: Onosma (Boraginaceae) is one of the most species-rich genera in the Balkans, yet cytogenetic data remain sparse. We present karyotypes, CMA3/DAPI banding, and FISH with 35S and 5S rDNA probes for seven tetraploid Onosma species from Serbia, North Macedonia, and Bulgaria (2n = 4x = 40 throughout). CMA3-positive bands occurred in a consistent pericentromeric pattern in O. visianii and O. pseudoarenaria, while O. javorkae showed additional bright subtelomeric CMA3 signals at two chromosome pairs. FISH revealed two 35S rDNA loci in four species and four loci in three species; 5S rDNA loci numbered two in all taxa. Karyotype asymmetry measured by the MCA index ranged from 0.38 (O. stellulata) to 0.61 (O. thracica), with asymmetry positively correlated with genome size (Spearman ρ = 0.74, p = 0.048). The results support the utility of fluorescent banding and rDNA FISH in discriminating morphologically similar species within this taxonomically difficult genus.

title: Утицај поплавног режима на концентрацију алелохемикала у ризосфери Fallopia japonica у рипаријалним стаништима Тисе
abstract: На три локалитета дуж Тисе (Кањижа, Бечеј, Titel) праћене су концентрације ресвератрола, емодина и феруличне киселине у ризосфери Fallopia japonica у периодима поплаве, оседања воде и суше током 2019–2020. године. Узорковање земљишне воде обављено је лизиметарским цевима на дубини 20 и 40 cm. HPLC-DAD анализа показала је да су концентрације свих три алелохемикала биле значајно ниже за време поплаве него у периоду суше (p < 0,01 за сва три једињења и оба нивоа дубине). Феруличка киселина на 20 cm дубине у периоду суше достигла је 0,34 µg mL⁻¹, насупрот 0,06 µg mL⁻¹ током поплаве. Резултати указују да хидролошки режим у значајној мери модулира биорасположивост алелохемикала у рипаријалним стаништима, са импликацијама за тумачење поплавима условљеног прекида инвазивне супресије домаће вегетације.

title: Two-Year Airborne Pollen Record from a Burkard Trap Station in Central Novi Sad: Taxon Composition and Seasonal Trends
abstract: Continuous volumetric sampling of airborne pollen was conducted at a rooftop Burkard 7-day spore trap station positioned at 12 m height in central Novi Sad from January 2022 through December 2023. Weekly tape sections were prepared by standard glycerine-jelly mounting and counts performed along two longitudinal traverses per day-section at 400× magnification. Over the two-year period, 48 pollen types were identified. Poaceae contributed 31% of total annual pollen load in both years, followed by Corylus (14%), Betula-type (11%), and Artemisia (9%). The main pollen season for grasses began on average on 5 May and lasted 68 days. Correlation with meteorological data from a co-located weather station showed that daily maximum temperature and wind speed from the southwest explained 58% of daily Poaceae pollen variance (multiple regression, R² = 0.58, p < 0.001). Inter-annual differences in Betula-type pollen peak were 12 days, consistent with the warm spring of 2023.
