title: Integrating design space construction with MSPC dashboards for day-to-day operation of a pan coating line: practical framework and pilot implementation
abstract: This paper describes a practical framework for integrating quality-by-design design space information with real-time MSPC monitoring in a pan coating operation at pilot scale. The design space for aqueous ethylcellulose sustained-release coating of 500 mg metformin hydrochloride tablets was established using a Definitive Screening Design (12 runs) exploring five process parameters, yielding a Bayesian design space with 95% probability of meeting dissolution specifications at 2 h and 8 h. MPCA monitoring models built from 17 reference batches within the design space were deployed alongside the design space boundary in a unified dashboard for the pan coating operator. A six-month pilot implementation period covered 41 production batches. The dashboard correctly flagged all four batches that subsequently failed dissolution testing, while generating two false alarms. Integration of design space contour overlays with MPCA scores provided operators with directional guidance for corrective action that pure MSPC charts do not supply. Operator feedback collected via structured interviews is reported.
venue: International Journal of Pharmaceutical Manufacturing and Quality

title: Continuous enzymatic phospholipid synthesis in a packed-bed reactor: residence time distribution and productivity analysis
abstract: A continuous packed-bed reactor (PBR) packed with Thermomyces lanuginosus lipase immobilised on acrylic beads (20 g, bed volume 45 mL) was evaluated for phosphatidylcholine synthesis as an alternative to batch operation. Substrate feed (lysophosphatidylcholine and oleic acid, 1:3 molar ratio in tert-amyl alcohol/water 96:4 v/v) was delivered at flow rates of 0.2–1.5 mL/min. Residence time distribution was characterised by tracer experiments with acetone, yielding a Bodenstein number of 28, indicating near-plug-flow behaviour. At 0.5 mL/min, PC yield was 65.8 ± 2.3% at steady state, with a volumetric productivity of 4.1 g PC/L·h, approximately 2.4-fold higher than comparable batch experiments. Enzyme half-life in continuous mode was 22 days compared with 14 days in batch mode. The PBR approach reduces downstream processing volume and improves throughput, making it attractive for scale-up to pilot level.
venue: Biochemical Engineering and Reaction Design

title: Discrete-Ordinates Modelling of Radiative Transfer in a Pilot-Scale Tunnel Kiln for Ceramic Tile Production
abstract: This study presents a three-dimensional computational model of radiative heat transfer inside a pilot-scale tunnel kiln used for ceramic tile firing. The discrete-ordinates method (DOM) with an S8 angular quadrature was implemented within an OpenFOAM framework, coupled to a steady-state energy equation solver. The kiln geometry was discretised into approximately 1.2 million hexahedral cells. Spectral gas absorption was handled using a weighted-sum-of-grey-gases (WSGG) model fitted to CO2–H2O mixtures at temperatures between 900 °C and 1250 °C. Validation was performed against thermocouple measurements taken at twelve axial positions along a 24-metre kiln operating at a production facility in Subotica. Simulated temperature profiles agreed with measurements to within 4.1% root-mean-square error across all monitored cross-sections. The results identify a recirculation-driven cold zone between 8 m and 11 m from the kiln entrance that correlates with documented underfiring defects. Recommendations for modified setting arrangements are discussed based on the computed heat flux distributions.
venue: Journal of Thermal Process Engineering

title: Effect of Burner Arrangement on Temperature Uniformity in a Roller-Hearth Glass Annealing Furnace: A Parametric CFD Study
abstract: Temperature uniformity across glass ribbon width is critical in roller-hearth annealing furnaces to prevent residual stress and optical distortion. This paper investigates five burner placement configurations in a 15-metre annealing furnace operating at a peak temperature of 620 °C using a coupled convection–radiation CFD model. Radiation was modelled with the discrete-ordinates method at S4 order, and combustion products were treated as grey participating media with spatially averaged absorption coefficients derived from HITRAN database entries for the operating temperature range. Simulations were run in steady state with inlet boundary conditions derived from manufacturer burner data sheets. A uniformity index based on the standard deviation of surface heat flux over the glass ribbon was used as the primary performance metric. The staggered offset configuration reduced the peak-to-mean heat flux deviation from 18.3% to 7.6% compared to the baseline symmetric arrangement. Pressure drop penalties across the configurations were within 3% of each other, indicating that the preferred layout carries no meaningful aerodynamic disadvantage.

title: Influence of Refractory Lining Emissivity on Firing Energy Consumption in Intermittent Ceramic Kilns
abstract: Refractory materials in ceramic kilns act as both thermal insulators and radiative surfaces, yet their spectral emissivity at elevated temperatures is rarely incorporated into furnace simulation studies. This work uses a DOM-based radiation model to quantify the sensitivity of energy consumption and product temperature history to refractory emissivity values ranging from 0.55 to 0.92, covering the range reported for commercially available high-alumina and mullite-based linings. An intermittent box kiln geometry of 2.4 m³ chamber volume, representative of small-batch sanitaryware production, was modelled. Firing cycles of 18 hours with a peak hold at 1220 °C were simulated. Results show that increasing refractory emissivity from 0.60 to 0.85 reduces the total thermal energy input by 6.8% while maintaining comparable product temperature uniformity, primarily due to enhanced radiative redistribution during the soaking phase. The sensitivity is more pronounced in the 900–1100 °C range where convective contributions are relatively smaller. These findings provide a quantitative basis for refractory material selection criteria beyond purely insulating performance.
venue: Thermal Science and Engineering Practice

title: Benchmarking S4, S6, and S8 Discrete-Ordinates Quadratures for Radiative Heat Transfer in Elongated Industrial Furnace Geometries
abstract: The discrete-ordinates method requires selection of an angular quadrature set, and the computational cost scales substantially with quadrature order. This study compares S4, S6, and S8 quadratures applied to three standardised elongated furnace geometries representing length-to-width ratios of 5:1, 10:1, and 20:1, with optically thin and optically thick participating media. Reference solutions were generated using a Monte Carlo method with 10⁷ photon bundles. Metrics include maximum local irradiation error, overall energy balance residual, and wall-clock time on a 16-core workstation. For the 10:1 geometry with a medium optical thickness of τ = 0.8, S6 achieved an irradiation error below 3.2% at 61% of the computational cost of S8. At τ = 0.2 (optically thin), S4 produced unacceptable ray-effect artefacts exceeding 12% local error in all geometries studied. Practical guidance for selecting quadrature order as a function of geometry aspect ratio and optical thickness is summarised in a decision chart intended for practitioners setting up industrial furnace simulations.

title: Uticaj brzine postmerger integracije na kompetencijski profil inženjerskih timova: komparativna studija slučaja
abstract: Studija upoređuje dva slučaja integracije inženjerskih timova u prerađivačkim preduzećima u Srbiji: jedno preduzeće je sprovelo ubrzanu integraciju u trajanju od četiri meseca, a drugo faznu integraciju tokom 16 meseci. Podaci su prikupljeni kombinacijom strukturisanih intervjua (n=24) i analizom internih evidencija kompetencija na godišnjem nivou tokom tri godine post-merger perioda. Kompetencijski profili su kvantifikovani kroz kompozitni indeks koji obuhvata tehničke veštine, procesno znanje i timske kompetencije. Rezultati pokazuju da preduzeće sa ubrzanom integracijom beleži pad kompozitnog indeksa od 22% u prvoj godini, dok preduzeće sa faznom integracijom beleži pad od svega 9%. U drugoj i trećoj godini razlika se smanjuje, ali ostaje statistički značajna (p < 0,01). Rad diskutuje ograničenja studije slučaja i predlaže parametre za buduće simulacione modele.

title: Fragility Functions for Retrofitted Unreinforced Masonry Buildings: Reinforced Plaster and Horizontal Tie Beams
abstract: Fragility curves are derived for two common low-cost seismic retrofit interventions applied to unreinforced masonry buildings: reinforced cement-mortar plaster overlay and the introduction of horizontal reinforced concrete tie beams at floor level. An ensemble of 120 building models was generated for each of three configurations—unretrofitted, plaster-retrofitted, and tie-beam-retrofitted—and analysed using nonlinear static procedures in TREMURI. Material and geometric parameters were sampled from the same probabilistic distributions used in earlier unretrofitted studies to allow direct comparison. Median PGA capacities at damage state D3 increase by 28% for the plaster intervention and by 19% for the tie-beam intervention relative to the unretrofitted baseline. Dispersion values change only modestly, remaining in the range 0.55–0.71. The study also performs a cost-benefit calculation assuming a 50-year service life and the regional hazard, finding benefit-cost ratios of 1.6–2.3 for the plaster intervention in the typology classes with the highest baseline vulnerability. Limitations related to the simplified treatment of plaster bonding failure are discussed.

title: Subsidence Detection in the Subotica–Horgoš Area Using Repeated GNSS Campaigns and Levelling Cross-Checks
abstract: The area north of Subotica along the Serbia–Hungary border has experienced observable land subsidence attributed partly to groundwater withdrawal for irrigation. Four GNSS campaign surveys (2010, 2013, 2016, 2019) at 31 benchmarks were combined with two first-order levelling runs (2011 and 2018) to construct a consistent vertical motion field. GNSS campaign data were processed with PPP using 48-hour sessions and compared against the nearest continuous station. Vertical velocities from campaign GNSS ranged from −1.1 to −4.6 mm/yr; levelling differences over seven years were consistent within ±0.5 mm/yr at 27 of 31 benchmarks. Four benchmarks near irrigation pump stations showed accelerated subsidence exceeding 5 mm/yr. Time-domain correlation with groundwater level records from eight observation wells yielded Pearson coefficients between 0.62 and 0.81 for the most affected sites. The study establishes a monitoring framework that can be maintained with biennial GNSS campaigns.

title: One-dimensional consolidation behaviour of Vojvodina lacustrine clay: comparison of Terzaghi and isotache-based models
abstract: Lacustrine clay deposits in the Vojvodina lowland exhibit pronounced creep behaviour that is poorly captured by classical Terzaghi consolidation theory. This study presents results from a series of incremental load oedometer tests conducted on undisturbed samples taken from three borehole locations near Novi Sad, at depths between 3 m and 9 m. Vertical stress increments ranged from 25 kPa to 400 kPa. The modified creep index Cα/Cc ratios were found to fall consistently between 0.045 and 0.062, suggesting moderate to high secondary compression potential. A one-dimensional isotache model implemented in a finite-difference scheme was calibrated against the measured time–settlement curves for each stress increment. Predicted end-of-primary settlements matched measurements within 8% for five of six samples, while the Terzaghi model underestimated long-term settlement by 15–30% in the same dataset. The results indicate that isotache-based formulations should be preferred for design calculations involving embankment loads on this clay unit, and a preliminary set of regional parameters is proposed for use in preliminary assessments.

title: Effect of sodium silicate modulus on setting time and early strength of fly ash–slag blended alkali-activated pastes
abstract: Binary pastes containing 70 wt% Class F fly ash and 30 wt% granulated blast furnace slag were activated with sodium silicate solutions of silica modulus Ms (SiO2/Na2O molar ratio) varying from 0.5 to 2.0 at a fixed Na2O dosage of 6 wt% relative to binder mass. Isothermal calorimetry at 23 °C revealed a two-stage heat release attributed separately to slag dissolution and secondary aluminosilicate polycondensation. Initial setting time measured by Vicat needle decreased from 95 to 18 minutes as Ms increased from 0.5 to 1.5, then rebounded slightly at Ms = 2.0. Compressive strength at 7 and 28 days peaked at Ms = 1.0, reaching 42 MPa at 28 days. SEM imaging showed a denser, more homogeneous gel at Ms = 1.0 compared with the cracked morphology observed at Ms = 2.0. The study recommends Ms = 1.0 as a practical optimum for the tested precursor blend under ambient curing.

title: CFD Assessment of Stack-Driven Cross-Ventilation Through Transom Windows in a Protected Early Twentieth-Century Classroom: Influence of Furniture Layout on Air Distribution
abstract: Natural ventilation retrofits in heritage classrooms are constrained by preservation rules that typically prohibit alterations to primary facades. Transom windows above existing door and window frames represent one permissible intervention point. This study uses steady-state Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes CFD modelling in OpenFOAM 8 to assess stack-driven cross-ventilation through transom openings in a representative 72 m² classroom with a 4.2 m ceiling height. Boundary conditions were derived from a typical spring shoulder-season scenario in Novi Sad (outdoor temperature 14 °C, indoor 22 °C). Four furniture arrangements were tested, varying desk orientation and grouping pattern. Simulated air-change rates ranged from 2.1 to 4.7 ACH depending on transom opening area (0.15–0.45 m² per facade) and furniture layout. Velocity magnitude at student breathing height (1.1 m seated) remained below the 0.2 m/s draught threshold in three of four layouts. The study identifies a diagonal desk arrangement as most compatible with both adequate ventilation and draught avoidance, providing practical guidance for school administrators and conservation architects.

title: Comparative LCA of cast-in-place and precast reinforced concrete frame systems for residential buildings in Serbia
abstract: This study presents a comparative life-cycle assessment of two reinforced concrete structural systems used in Serbian residential construction: a conventional cast-in-place frame and a precast frame assembled from factory-produced columns, beams and hollow-core slabs. The system boundary follows a cradle-to-practical-completion scope (modules A1–A5 of EN 15978). Primary production data were collected from two construction sites in Novi Sad and supplemented with SimaPro 9.1 calculations using the ecoinvent 3.7 background database adapted with Serbian electricity grid data from 2019. For a representative six-storey residential building of 2 400 m² gross floor area, the precast system showed a GWP of 278 kg CO₂-eq./m² compared with 305 kg CO₂-eq./m² for cast-in-place, representing an 8.9% reduction. The dominant contributor in both cases is cement production (56–61%). Results for cumulative energy demand and water depletion show smaller differences between systems. The paper discusses sensitivity to concrete strength class and transport distance from the precast plant.

title: Electrocoagulation as a pretreatment for chromate-bearing industrial rinse water: effect of current density and electrolysis time
abstract: Electrocoagulation (EC) with iron sacrificial electrodes was evaluated for Cr(VI) removal from rinse water collected at a surface finishing plant in Novi Sad. Experiments were carried out in a batch EC reactor (2-litre working volume, two parallel Fe electrode pairs) at current densities of 5, 10, 20, and 40 mA/cm², electrolysis times of 5–60 minutes, and initial Cr(VI) concentrations of 5–50 mg/L. At 20 mA/cm² and 30 minutes, Cr(VI) removal exceeded 99 % for initial concentrations up to 20 mg/L at pH 7.0. Mechanism analysis using Fe:Cr molar ratios in the sludge confirmed simultaneous Cr(VI) reduction by electrogenerated Fe(II) and co-precipitation of Cr(III) with Fe(III) hydroxide. Energy consumption was 1.8 kWh/m³ at optimal conditions. Electrode passivation was observed above 40 mA/cm² after 20 minutes, reducing removal efficiency by up to 15 %. Scale-up implications and comparison with chemical reduction–precipitation are discussed.

title: Effect of humectant type and concentration on water activity and microbial challenge performance in oil-in-water facial emulsions
abstract: Three humectants—glycerol, propylene glycol, and sorbitol—were evaluated at four concentrations (5, 10, 15, and 20% w/w) in a standardised oil-in-water facial emulsion containing 0.8% phenoxyethanol as the sole preservative. Water activity (aw) was measured using a capacitance-based dew-point meter at 25 °C. A modified challenge test following ISO 11930:2019 criteria was performed with Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Candida albicans, Aspergillus brasiliensis, and Escherichia coli inocula of approximately 106 CFU/g. Glycerol reduced aw from 0.992 to 0.961 at 20%, whereas sorbitol achieved 0.953 at the same level. Challenge test category A criteria were met only when aw ≤ 0.970 regardless of humectant type, suggesting that aw reduction rather than humectant identity is the controlling factor. Rheological measurements confirmed that sorbitol at 15% produced a yield stress of 8.4 Pa, which may independently limit microbial motility. The results allow formulation of adequate preservation with reduced preservative concentrations when humectant selection is guided by aw targets.

title: Comparison of single-trait and multi-trait animal models for estimating breeding values for litter size in Mangalica × Landrace crossbreeds
abstract: Breeding value estimation for litter size in pig populations with small datasets may be sensitive to the choice of model structure. This study compared estimated breeding values (EBVs) and their accuracies obtained from single-trait versus multi-trait animal models applied to records for TNB, NBA, and NW from 1,894 F1 Mangalica × Landrace sows on five farms over nine years. Variance components were estimated by REML and EBVs were computed using BLUP methodology in ASReml. Rank correlations between EBVs from the two model types exceeded 0.93 for TNB and NBA but dropped to 0.81 for NW, suggesting that the multi-trait model provides more stable ranking of sows for weaning performance. Mean EBV accuracy was slightly higher under the multi-trait model (0.41 vs. 0.37 for TNB), primarily because of the borrowing of information across correlated traits. Practical implications for small-scale selection programs in Vojvodina are discussed.

title: Dietary DDGS level influences rumen archaeal community structure and methanogen relative abundance in Holstein heifers
abstract: Methanogenic archaea in the rumen are the primary source of enteric methane, yet their response to bioethanol co-products in the diet of young dairy heifers is undercharacterised. Rumen contents from 30 Holstein heifers (5 per dietary group: 0, 10, 20, 30% corn DDGS) were collected at slaughter after 75 days on trial. DNA was extracted and the archaeal 16S rRNA gene (V4–V5 region) was sequenced on an Illumina MiSeq platform. Methanobrevibacter dominated all samples, accounting for 78–84% of archaeal reads. Its relative abundance declined with increasing DDGS inclusion, reaching its lowest value in the 30% group (78.1%, vs. 84.3% in control; P = 0.02). Methanosphaera abundance was inversely related to DDGS level. Total archaeal alpha diversity (Shannon index) increased slightly at 20% inclusion. Partial least squares regression linked lower archaeal abundance to higher propionate concentration in rumen fluid, consistent with competitive hydrogen utilisation. Findings support the hypothesis that DDGS-driven propionate shifts modestly suppress methanogenesis.

title: Effect of extrusion temperature on starch gelatinisation and subsequent digestibility in carp diets
abstract: Extrusion barrel temperature was varied at four levels (110, 130, 150, and 170°C) during processing of a maize-soybean-based diet to examine the relationship between starch gelatinisation degree and apparent digestibility of dry matter, starch, and crude protein in common carp. Gelatinisation was quantified by differential scanning calorimetry. Diets were fed to carp averaging 85 g initial weight in indoor tanks over 42 days, with chromic oxide included as a marker. Starch gelatinisation increased from 48% at 110°C to 97% at 170°C. Starch ADC improved from 74.1% to 89.3% across the same range, while crude protein ADC showed a smaller but significant increase from 82.1% to 86.8%. Feed pellet water stability declined at higher temperatures. The 150°C treatment offered the best balance between nutrient digestibility and pellet integrity, with a specific growth rate of 1.43% body weight per day. Results suggest that extrusion temperature is a critical processing parameter for carp diets.

title: Primena metode Monte Karlo za analizu neizvesnosti u LCA prefabrikovanih nosača: slučaj srpskog elektroenergetskog miksa
abstract: Srpski elektroenergetski miks podložan je značajnim godišnjim varijacijama u udjelu termoelektrana na lignit, što unosi merljivu neizvesnost u LCA studije građevinskih proizvoda. U ovom radu izvršena je Monte Karlo simulacija sa 10 000 iteracija za LCA prefabrikovanog armirano-betonskog nosača raspona 18 m, koristeći trogodišnje podatke o mešavini goriva iz srpske elektroenergetske mreže (2018–2020). title: Life-cycle carbon assessment of a precast reinforced concrete school building: cradle-to-grave analysis including 50-year operational energy
abstract: This study presents a full cradle-to-grave LCA of a precast reinforced concrete school building (2 780 m² gross floor area) constructed in Sremska Mitrovica, Serbia in 2018. The assessment covers modules A1–C4 and module D (beyond system boundary) in line with EN 15978:2011, with a reference service life of 50 years. Primary embodied carbon data were derived from verified EPDs for the precast structural system; operational energy was modelled using EnergyPlus v9.4 and calibrated against 24 months of measured consumption data. Embodied carbon for the structural system (A1–A5) amounts to 168 kg CO₂-eq./m², while cumulative operational carbon over 50 years represents 1 940 kg CO₂-eq./m² under a static grid assumption and 1 220 kg CO₂-eq./m² under a decarbonisation trajectory scenario aligned with Serbia's National Energy and Climate Plan. End-of-life credits (module D) offset 6.8% of total life-cycle GWP. The results indicate that operational emissions dominate even under conservative assumptions, but that the relative importance of embodied carbon increases substantially under the decarbonisation scenario.

title: End-of-life treatment pathways for demolition concrete in Serbia: current practice, regulatory gaps and LCA implications
abstract: Serbia generates an estimated 4.2 million tonnes of construction and demolition waste annually, yet official statistics on concrete fraction recycling rates remain incomplete. This paper combines a field survey of 11 demolition contractors operating in Vojvodina and Belgrade with a regulatory review and LCA modelling of three waste treatment pathways: landfilling, crushing for unbound sub-base aggregate, and closed-loop recycling as recycled concrete aggregate (RCA) for structural use. Survey results indicate that landfilling still accounts for roughly 58% of demolition concrete by mass, primarily due to the absence of mandatory waste sorting requirements and the low gate fees at regional landfills. LCA results show that the RCA pathway reduces module C GWP contributions by up to 48 kg CO₂-eq./tonne compared with landfilling, provided that transport distances remain below 35 km. The paper identifies three specific gaps in Serbian waste regulations that prevent the circular economy pathway from becoming economically competitive.

title: Poređenje sistema dodele ekoloških bodova za prefabrikovane AB konstrukcije u nacionalnim zelenim standardima: analiza kriterijuma BREEAM, LEED i srpskog pravilnika o energetskoj efikasnosti
abstract: Zeleni standardi za zgrade – BREEAM International, LEED v4.1 i srpski Pravilnik o energetskoj efikasnosti zgrada (2023) – različito tretiraju ugrađeni ugljenik i EPD dokumentaciju prefabrikovanih nosećih konstrukcija. U ovom radu izvršena je uporedna analiza releventnih bodovnih kategorija primenom virtuelnog modela stambene zgrade u Novom Sadu sa prefabrikovanim AB skeletom. Analiza pokazuje da srpski pravilnik ne dodeljuje direktne bodove za EPD ni za benčmarking ugrađenog ugljenika, dok BREEAM Mat 01 i LEED MRc2 pružaju merljive podsticaje koji su dostigli prag bodova u 34 od 40 simuliranih scenarija. Razmatrana je mogućnost uvođenja nacionalnog sistema kreditiranja ugrađenog ugljenika zasnovanog na predloženim regionalnim benčmarkovima. Zaključci su upućeni Ministarstvu građevinarstva, saobraćaja i infrastrukture kao doprinos tekućoj reviziji pravilnika.

title: Antenna Phase-Centre Variation Corrections in Continuous GNSS Stations: Impact on Vertical Velocity Estimates at Mixed-Receiver Networks
abstract: Networks in which antenna and receiver models change over time are susceptible to apparent vertical offsets when phase-centre variation (PCV) corrections are applied inconsistently. Using a subset of 13 stations from the Serbian national CORS network with documented equipment changes between 2004 and 2019, this study systematically tested three PCV correction approaches: igs14.atx individual calibrations, type-mean calibrations, and robot-calibrated site-specific values obtained for five stations. Equipment change epochs were identified from log files and validated against discontinuity detection using the interquartile range method. Applying individual calibrations in place of type-mean values altered vertical velocities by −0.12 to +0.27 mm/yr depending on the antenna combination involved. Robot-calibrated corrections agreed with individual igs14.atx values at the 0.05 mm/yr level. Recommendations for network operators on maintaining consistent PCV correction chains through hardware upgrades are summarised.

title: Psychological reactance to mandatory vaccination messaging among parents of pre-school children in Serbia
abstract: This cross-sectional study examined the antecedents and communication consequences of psychological reactance to pro-vaccination messages in a sample of 347 parents of children aged 0–6 attending paediatric check-ups in the South Bačka district. Reactance was measured using the Hong Psychological Reactance Scale and a message-specific reactance index developed for the study. Higher trait reactance predicted more negative attitudes toward childhood vaccination (β = −0.34) and lower vaccination compliance intentions (β = −0.27), independent of vaccine hesitancy and general health locus of control. Messages emphasising parental autonomy in decision-making reduced state reactance scores compared with authority-based messaging (Mdiff = 1.2, t(345) = 4.6, p < .001). The study also found that reactance was elevated among parents who had encountered vaccine misinformation online in the prior month. Findings have direct implications for how paediatric health authorities in Serbia should frame immunisation communication materials.

title: Retrofit of a ceramic tile production line: pinch analysis and heat exchanger network design for flue gas heat recovery
abstract: Industrial tunnel kilns used in ceramic tile production generate large volumes of flue gas at temperatures between 180 and 340 °C, which are currently vented without heat recovery at the studied facility in central Serbia. Pinch analysis was applied to the combined process and utility system, identifying a minimum hot utility target of 2.1 MW against a current consumption of 3.8 MW (44.7% reduction potential). Three retrofit designs were developed, varying in the number and arrangement of gas-to-air heat exchangers installed on the kiln exhaust duct. The preferred design, constrained by the available footprint and a maximum capital budget of 320,000 €, reduces hot utility consumption by 34.2% and achieves a simple payback of 1.8 years at current natural gas prices (0.048 €/kWh). Exergy analysis of the preferred design shows that 58% of the remaining exergy destruction occurs in the high-temperature kiln zone, suggesting future potential for combustion-air preheating beyond the current design scope.

title: Second-law analysis of a biomass combined heat and power plant with flue gas condensation: effect of moisture content and load variation
abstract: A biomass-fired combined heat and power plant of 4.8 MW thermal and 1.1 MW electrical output, operating on wood chips with moisture content between 30% and 55% (wet basis), is analysed using detailed exergy accounting across all major components: combustion chamber, steam generator, turbine, condenser, flue gas economiser and condensation unit. Data were collected during 120 hours of continuous operation across four load levels (50%, 70%, 85% and 100% of rated load). Total exergy destruction rate at full load is 5.63 MW, with the combustion chamber responsible for 49% of this figure. Flue gas condensation recovers 210–480 kW of additional heat depending on moisture content, but contributes less than 0.8% to overall plant exergetic efficiency due to the low temperature of condensate heat. The exergetic efficiency of the plant ranges from 22.1% (50% load, 55% moisture) to 31.4% (100% load, 30% moisture). Load-following operation causes disproportionate increases in combustion irreversibility at partial load, identified as the main target for operational improvement.

title: Heat integration across batch and continuous processes: a time-average model applied to a dairy production facility
abstract: Batch processes present particular challenges for heat integration because stream availability varies with time. This paper applies a time-average model extended with storage vessel sizing to a dairy facility operating three batch pasteurisation lines alongside two continuous cream separation circuits. Stream population comprises 9 continuous and 14 batch streams. The composite curve approach is adapted using time-slice decomposition with six 4-hour intervals per production day. Heat storage vessels of 8 m³ each are introduced to bridge temporal mismatches between batch heating and cooling demands. The resulting heat exchanger network design achieves a 29.3% reduction in hot utility (steam at 3 bar) compared with the existing network, and a 22.1% reduction in cooling water consumption. Capital cost of the proposed network including storage vessels is estimated at 195,000 €, with a projected simple payback of 3.1 years. The methodology is documented in sufficient detail to be reproducible for similar mixed batch–continuous food processing contexts.

title: Avoidable and unavoidable exergy destruction in industrial heat exchanger networks: a screening method for retrofit prioritisation
abstract: Advanced exergy analysis distinguishes between avoidable and unavoidable exergy destruction within components by comparing actual operation with an idealised theoretical limit and a best-practice reference case. This paper proposes a screening method that applies this decomposition at the network level, aggregating component-level results to produce a prioritised list of retrofit candidates for industrial heat exchanger networks. The method is demonstrated on two case studies: a solvent recovery system (6 streams, 4 existing exchangers) and a vegetable oil deodorisation unit (9 streams, 7 existing exchangers). In both cases, the screening correctly identifies the same top-priority exchangers flagged by full multi-objective optimisation, while requiring approximately 15% of the computational effort. Sensitivity of the prioritisation ranking to uncertainty in heat transfer coefficients (±20%) is assessed; ranking of the top three candidates is found to be robust in all tested scenarios. The method is intended as a practical tool for energy engineers conducting preliminary retrofit assessments without access to full optimisation software.

title: Time-of-use tariff impact on the operational cost of a combined compressed-air and chilled-water utility system: a linear programming approach
abstract: The paper formulates a linear programming model for the daily scheduling of a combined utility system that includes two fixed-speed air compressors (total 110 kW), one variable-speed chiller (75 kW), and buffer storage vessels for both compressed air and chilled water. The optimisation objective minimises daily electricity cost under a three-period time-of-use tariff structure representative of Serbian industrial tariff class VN-A. Load profiles for compressed air and cooling were derived from twelve-month sub-hourly measurements at a plastics manufacturing facility. Under the optimal schedule, daily electricity cost was reduced by 9.2% relative to uncontrolled baseline operation, and peak coincident demand was reduced by 18 kW. The model is solved to optimality in under four seconds on standard hardware, making real-time deployment feasible. Results are sensitive to buffer volume: doubling the air receiver from 2 000 to 4 000 litres improved savings by a further 3.1 percentage points.

title: Fouling resistance development in brazed plate heat exchangers handling hard groundwater: a six-month industrial monitoring study
abstract: Calcium carbonate scaling on BPHE surfaces in industrial water-heating applications increases thermal resistance and pressure drop over time, but long-term field data under real process conditions are scarce. This study presents fouling resistance measurements collected over 24 weeks at a food-processing facility in Vojvodina using two identically specified BPHEs: one operating continuously and one with weekly thermal shock cleaning cycles. Fouling resistance was calculated from overall heat transfer coefficient measurements recorded every four hours using calibrated flow meters and Pt100 temperature sensors. After 24 weeks, the continuously operated unit reached an asymptotic fouling resistance of 1.9 × 10⁻⁴ m²·K/W, while the cleaned unit stabilised at 6.4 × 10⁻⁵ m²·K/W. Scanning electron microscopy of extracted plates confirmed predominantly calcite crystalline deposits with median layer thickness of 38 µm on the hot side. The results support use of an asymptotic fouling model with time constants fitted to the measured data, and suggest that current TEMA-recommended fouling allowances overestimate resistance by a factor of 1.4–2.1 for this water chemistry.

title: Epidemic and epidemic rumour: health crisis reporting in Vojvodina newspapers during the interwar period
abstract: Drawing on a corpus of 634 health-related articles identified across ten Vojvodina newspapers between 1919 and 1941, this article analyses how the regional press reported on epidemic disease outbreaks and public health measures. Coverage is examined for three recurring episodes: the tail of the 1918–1919 influenza pandemic, a 1924 typhoid outbreak in Srem, and periodic cholera warnings in the 1930s. Coding categories included information source cited, prescription of individual versus institutional responses, and use of contagion metaphor. Results show that official health announcements were reproduced with minimal editorial addition in 71% of epidemic coverage, while anonymous community rumour appears as a framing device in 22% of articles. The article discusses the press as both information intermediary and anxiety amplifier in public health contexts, and draws connections to contemporary debates on health communication through historical media.

title: Residual stress and warpage in overmoulded two-component polypropylene/polyamide 6 parts: simulation and experiment
abstract: Two-component injection moulding of polypropylene (PP) substrate and polyamide 6 (PA6) overmould was studied with respect to residual stress development and warpage. The process involves sequential injection into a rotary mould; the PP substrate cools partially before PA6 is injected over it. A sequential thermomechanical FE simulation was implemented to capture stress accumulation in both materials and at the interface. The PP thermoviscoelastic material model and PA6 crystallisation model were taken from previous calibrated studies. Simulations were compared against CMM warpage measurements on 40 two-component plaques (160 × 80 mm) produced at two substrate pre-cooling times (8 and 15 s). Predicted warpage matched measurements within 0.09 mm for the 15 s pre-cooling case and within 0.21 mm for the 8 s case, where incomplete solidification of the substrate introduced additional uncertainty. Interfacial stress concentrations are identified as a potential delamination risk at sharp edges.

title: Optimisation of straight cooling channel layout in injection moulds using a gradient-free method and process simulation surrogate
abstract: An automated cooling channel layout optimisation procedure was developed for injection moulds with straight drilled channels. A surrogate model for the cycle-average cavity surface temperature and resulting warpage was constructed using a Latin hypercube design of 120 simulation runs, with channel diameter, pitch, and depth below cavity as design variables. A surrogate-based Nelder–Mead optimisation was then applied to minimise a combined objective of maximum warpage and cycle time for a PP instrument panel insert (projected area 310 cm²). The optimised layout reduced maximum warpage from 0.72 mm (baseline design) to 0.31 mm and cycle time from 24.1 s to 20.8 s compared with the manufacturer's original channel arrangement. The surrogate model had a root-mean-squared error of 0.03 mm for warpage predictions on a 20-point validation set. The procedure requires approximately 5 hours of total computation time, making it practical for industrial use.

title: Creep behaviour of injection-moulded PA6-GF30 under sustained mechanical load: effect of initial residual stress state
abstract: Injection-moulded PA6 reinforced with 30 wt% short glass fibres was subjected to sustained bending loads at 23 °C and 60% relative humidity to measure creep deflection over 1000 hours. Three sets of specimens were compared: as-moulded, annealed at 150 °C for 4 hours to relieve residual stresses, and specimens with known residual stress states characterised by the layer-removal method. Residual stresses in as-moulded specimens reached −12 MPa at the skin and +8 MPa at the core. Creep compliance after 1000 hours was on average 7% higher in as-moulded specimens compared with annealed specimens, attributed to residual tensile core stresses accelerating viscoelastic creep. A viscoelastic creep model incorporating initial stress state was fitted to the data; model predictions tracked experimental deflections within 9% up to 500 hours, diverging to 17% at 1000 hours where moisture absorption effects became significant.

title: Process-induced warpage in thick-walled polypropylene optical components: the role of differential cooling rate
abstract: Thick-walled PP optical mounting brackets (nominal wall thickness 8 mm) for automotive lighting assemblies require tight dimensional tolerances and are particularly susceptible to warpage driven by differential cooling between the cavity and core sides of the mould. This study investigates the relationship between the cooling rate asymmetry and final warpage for four mould configurations with varying cavity-to-core mould temperature ratios (ΔT = 0, 10, 20, 30 °C; cavity side always colder). Warpage was measured on 15 parts per condition using a structured-light scanner with 0.02 mm point accuracy. Differential cooling induced a systematic bowing, with warpage increasing from 0.12 mm at ΔT = 0 to 0.91 mm at ΔT = 30 °C. Thermomechanical simulations captured this trend with a maximum error of 0.11 mm. Through-thickness crystallinity measurements confirmed that the core-side crystallinity exceeded the cavity-side value by up to 6 percentage points at ΔT = 30 °C, directly contributing to differential shrinkage.

title: Numerical simulation of condensation risk inside sealed electromechanical enclosures using a coupled heat-moisture transfer approach
abstract: A two-dimensional finite-difference model was developed to simulate transient heat and moisture transfer in a sealed steel enclosure containing a heat-dissipating printed circuit board. The model couples Fourier conduction through the walls with Fickian vapour diffusion and accounts for condensation on internal surfaces when local temperature drops below the dew point. Internal heat generation was set at 5 W, representing a typical low-power controller unit. Simulations were run for a 24-hour diurnal ambient profile representative of a Pannonian autumn day. Results showed that condensation first occurred on the lower half of the front panel after approximately 17 minutes of rapid external temperature drop at −1.2 °C/min. Increasing the initial internal air volume by 30 % by deepening the enclosure reduced condensation onset time by only 4 minutes, while adding a 2-g silica-gel desiccant delayed onset by 38 minutes. The model was validated against thermocouple and humidity logger measurements from a physical enclosure subjected to a controlled temperature ramp in a climate chamber.

title: Acoustic emission in sandwich structures: damage mechanisms, monitoring approaches, and signal processing methods
abstract: This chapter reviews the state of the art in acoustic emission monitoring of composite sandwich panels, covering the period 2000–2020. Damage mechanism taxonomy—matrix cracking, delamination, core crushing, face-sheet debonding—is discussed in relation to characteristic AE waveform features: peak frequency, rise angle, and partial-power ratios. Signal processing approaches are organised into time-domain, frequency-domain, and time-frequency methods, with practical comparison of short-time Fourier transform, continuous wavelet transform, and empirical mode decomposition as applied to AE waveforms. Source-location methods for anisotropic panels are reviewed, including delta-T mapping and velocity-field inversion. Remaining challenges are identified as sensor coupling reliability under fatigue, acoustic cross-talk in thin cores, and the lack of standardised benchmark datasets for algorithm comparison. The chapter is aimed at practitioners setting up monitoring systems rather than signal-processing specialists.

title: Adaptive Receivers for Underwater Acoustic Communications
abstract: This book chapter reviews adaptive receiver algorithms applicable to underwater acoustic communication systems, with emphasis on shallow-water environments where multipath delay spread can extend beyond the OFDM symbol guard interval. The chapter covers linear and decision-feedback equaliser structures based on LMS, RLS, and Kalman filter adaptation, followed by frequency-domain soft equalisation for OFDM. Iterative (turbo) architectures combining equalisation and channel decoding are discussed in detail, including EXIT chart design tools. Performance data drawn from field measurements on inland waterways in the middle Danube basin are used throughout to ground the discussion. Practical considerations—pilot contamination, Doppler pre-compensation, receiver synchronisation—are addressed alongside algorithmic descriptions. The chapter is aimed at graduate students and engineers entering the field, and closes with a summary of open problems including real-time implementation constraints and deep-water applicability.

title: Open-Loop DPD Coefficient Initialisation Using Device Physics-Informed Regression for Rapid PA Swap-Out
abstract: In base station maintenance scenarios, replacing a faulty PA with a new unit currently requires full DPD re-training from live traffic, causing a period of elevated ACPR. This paper proposes an open-loop initialisation method in which device datasheet parameters — quiescent current, gate bias, and small-signal gain — are used as inputs to a regression model trained on a library of 47 characterised GaN devices spanning four manufacturers and three process nodes. The regression model predicts GMP model coefficients for the replacement device without requiring any over-the-air observation. Initial ACPR after open-loop DPD is −43.5 dBc on average across a leave-one-out cross-validation, compared to −28.3 dBc with no DPD and −50.1 dBc after full closed-loop adaptation. Fine-tuning from 500 observed samples brings the closed-loop result to within 0.7 dBc of the fully trained baseline. The approach reduces the number of adaptation samples needed by a factor of 18 compared to cold-start training, which is relevant for systems where observation bandwidth or processing time is limited during live operation.

title: Automated step-and-repeat layout optimization for label printing with mixed-SKU jobs
abstract: Label converters increasingly run mixed-SKU jobs on a single web, placing multiple label designs in a step-and-repeat grid to minimize substrate waste and plate changes. This paper formulates the layout problem as a two-dimensional strip packing with orientation constraints and color-sequence dependencies. A simulated annealing metaheuristic was implemented and tested on 80 mixed-SKU job specifications drawn from a production log at a regional label converter. Run time on a standard desktop CPU averaged 8.4 seconds per job. Compared to operator-designed layouts, the automated approach reduced substrate waste by 11.2% and decreased the number of color-sequence violations from 14% to 1.3% of jobs. The system outputs an industry-standard CIP4/JDF layout file for direct import into the converter's workflow management system.

title: Governance Standard Stringency and Supplier Exit Risk: A Survival Analysis of Tier-2 Firms in Romanian and Serbian Dairy Chains
abstract: This paper examines whether heightened sustainability standard requirements increase the probability that tier-2 dairy suppliers exit the formal supply chain—either by ceasing operations, shifting to informal markets, or downgrading to buyers with lower requirements. Longitudinal data on 312 dairy farms in Romania and Serbia were assembled from official registry records, buyer compliance databases, and a retrospective survey, covering the period 2015–2023. A Cox proportional hazards model is estimated with standard stringency (measured as the number of verified compliance dimensions required by each farm's primary buyer) as the main covariate, controlling for herd size, farm age, region, and access to agri-environmental subsidies. The hazard ratio for stringency is 1.09 per additional compliance dimension (95% CI [1.03, 1.16]), indicating a modest but consistent association with exit risk. Subsidy access substantially moderates this relationship. The paper contributes to ongoing debates about whether private sustainability standards promote upgrading or exclusion of small producers.

title: Competency Profiling in the Serbian Automotive Supply Chain: A Study of Tier-2 and Tier-3 Suppliers
abstract: This article reports competency profiling data collected from 11 Tier-2 and Tier-3 automotive component suppliers located in Vojvodina. A mixed-methods design combined semi-structured interviews (n = 48 managers and team leaders), behavioural event interviews (n = 31 high-performing operators selected by management nomination), and a quantitative survey (n = 312 employees). Competency clusters derived from qualitative analysis were operationalised as rating scales and administered to a broader sample. Confirmatory factor analysis supported a six-cluster model: technical precision, equipment stewardship, procedural adherence, collaborative problem-solving, quality orientation, and adaptive response to production variability. Criterion-related validity was assessed against supervisor performance ratings; correlations ranged from r = 0.31 to r = 0.58 across clusters. The study also documents significant gaps between competencies demanded by Tier-1 customer audits and those currently cultivated in supplier training programmes. Findings informed a draft competency dictionary distributed to participating companies.

title: Digital Readiness Self-Assessment in Vojvodina SMEs: A Pilot Scale Development and Validation
abstract: Measuring an organisation's readiness for digital transformation is a prerequisite for targeting change management interventions effectively, yet validated instruments adapted to transition-economy SMEs are scarce. This paper reports the development and preliminary validation of a 22-item Digital Readiness Scale (DRS-22) tailored to the context of small and medium enterprises operating in lower-income EU candidate countries. Scale items were generated through a systematic review of existing readiness frameworks and two rounds of expert interviews with twelve managers from Serbian and Hungarian SMEs. A pilot sample of 87 employees and owners from Vojvodina-based firms completed the instrument, and exploratory factor analysis identified four stable dimensions: technological infrastructure, managerial commitment, employee digital competence, and process formalisation. Internal consistency was satisfactory across all subscales (Cronbach's α ranging from 0.71 to 0.84). Confirmatory analysis on a second hold-out subsample supported a four-factor structure with acceptable fit indices. The scale is intended as a free diagnostic tool for practitioners and as a baseline measure for longitudinal transformation studies. Limitations include the small pilot size and single-region sampling.

title: Skin conductance reactivity during a public-speaking stressor in undergraduate students with high versus low perfectionism concerns
abstract: This study examined electrodermal reactivity as a function of perfectionism concerns in a non-clinical student sample. Sixty-one undergraduates completed the Frost Multidimensional Perfectionism Scale and were exposed to a three-minute impromptu speech task in front of a two-person evaluative panel. Skin conductance level (SCL) and the number of non-specific skin conductance responses (NS-SCRs) were recorded continuously using a BIOPAC MP160 system with 8 mm Ag/AgCl electrodes placed on the index and middle fingers of the non-dominant hand. Participants scoring in the top tertile on Concern over Mistakes showed significantly higher mean SCL during anticipation (d = 0.61, p = .014) and recovery phases (d = 0.54, p = .031) compared to the low group, but groups did not differ reliably during the speech itself. NS-SCR frequency was elevated throughout the entire protocol in high-concern participants. Results suggest that heightened electrodermal arousal in perfectionistic individuals is most pronounced outside the peak stressor interval, pointing to prolonged anticipatory and perseverative processing rather than peak-moment hyperreactivity.

title: Resting vagally mediated heart rate variability as a predictor of cognitive reappraisal use in perfectionistic individuals
abstract: Vagally mediated heart rate variability (vmHRV), indexed by the root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD), has been proposed as a physiological marker of self-regulatory capacity. This study tested whether resting RMSSD predicts habitual use of cognitive reappraisal in a sample of 88 psychology students selected to oversample high scores on the Hewitt–Flett Multidimensional Perfectionism Scale. A five-minute resting ECG was recorded in a supine position before participants completed the Emotion Regulation Questionnaire and a brief interview about recent academic performance appraisals. After controlling for trait anxiety and respiratory rate, resting RMSSD explained an additional 7.4% of variance in reappraisal frequency (β = 0.29, p = .008), but only among participants with self-oriented perfectionism scores above the sample median. Socially prescribed perfectionism did not moderate the association. Findings are consistent with the neurovisceral integration model and suggest that autonomic flexibility may buffer the tendency of self-oriented perfectionists to abandon adaptive reappraisal under self-evaluative pressure.

title: Respiratory sinus arrhythmia suppression under social evaluation: an exploratory comparison of adaptive and maladaptive perfectionism profiles
abstract: Respiratory sinus arrhythmia (RSA) suppression from rest to a stressor is considered an index of vagal withdrawal supporting active coping. This exploratory study used latent profile analysis on Frost MPS subscale scores in a sample of 74 students to identify two perfectionism profiles: one characterised by high personal standards with low doubts and concerns (adaptive profile, n = 31) and one characterised by high doubts, concerns and parental criticism (maladaptive profile, n = 43). Participants completed a modified Trier Social Stress Test adapted for laboratory use, with concurrent respiration and ECG recording. RSA was estimated using the band-limited power method (0.12–0.40 Hz). Both groups showed RSA suppression during the stress task, but the maladaptive profile group showed significantly blunted suppression relative to baseline compared with the adaptive group (F(1, 71) = 5.18, p = .026, η²p = .068). Recovery RSA was also slower in the maladaptive group at the five-minute post-task interval. The findings replicate a pattern reported in emotion dysregulation research and extend it to a perfectionism-defined taxonomy.

title: Do perfectionistic cognitions mediate the link between trait perfectionism and autonomic stress reactivity? A pilot examination with concurrent EDA and ECG recording
abstract: Perfectionistic cognitions—intrusive thoughts about making mistakes—have been proposed as a proximal mechanism through which dispositional perfectionism translates into negative affect and physiological stress. This pilot study (N = 44) tested whether state perfectionistic cognitions, assessed immediately after a graded arithmetic task, mediated the association between trait Concern over Mistakes and two simultaneous physiological measures: mean skin conductance level (SCL) and RMSSD during the task. Electrodermal and cardiac data were co-registered on a BIOPAC MP160 platform. Bootstrapped mediation analysis (5,000 samples) indicated a significant indirect effect of Concern over Mistakes on RMSSD via perfectionistic cognitions (ab = −0.14, 95% CI [−0.27, −0.03]), but no reliable indirect effect on SCL. The differential pattern across the two autonomic channels suggests that perfectionistic cognitions may primarily suppress parasympathetic flexibility rather than amplify sympathetic activation. Sample size limits interpretation, and a pre-registered replication is underway.

title: Designing social media simulations for experimental bystander research: methodological considerations and a replication attempt
abstract: Laboratory research on online bystander behaviour depends heavily on the ecological validity of simulation environments. This methodological paper describes the design and iterative testing of a browser-based social media simulator developed at the University of Novi Sad that mimics common short-message platform features, including visible like counts, threaded replies, and follower indicators. Two pilot experiments (N = 64 and N = 89) were conducted to assess whether the simulator produced intervention rates consistent with published field-survey benchmarks. Intervention rates of 38% and 41% were observed respectively, compared with a meta-analytic estimate of approximately 35–45% from survey studies. Manipulation checks confirmed participants perceived the interactions as realistic. The paper discusses confounds introduced by artificial timers, researcher presence, and demand characteristics, and provides an open protocol and scenario scripts. Known limitations include the impossibility of genuine social consequences and the use of convenience student samples.

title: FPGA Prototyping of NAS-Derived Architectures: From Pareto Front to Bitstream
abstract: Translating multi-objective NAS results into running FPGA implementations requires hardware-aware evaluation during the search and a reliable post-search implementation flow. This paper presents an end-to-end workflow connecting an NSGA-II NAS backend to a high-level synthesis (HLS) toolchain targeting a Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA. Latency and resource utilisation (LUT, BRAM, DSP) estimates from an HLS profiling run are fed back into the NAS loop as surrogate objective values, replacing slower board-level measurements. Three image classification tasks with 96×96 input resolution are used as benchmarks. The surrogate estimates correlate with measured values at r=0.91 for latency and r=0.87 for LUT count, validating their use in the search. The best NAS-derived architecture on the object detection proxy task achieves 19 ms inference latency at 93.4 percent accuracy, compared to 31 ms for a manually designed reference. The workflow is described in sufficient detail to replicate on comparable mid-range FPGAs.

title: Constraint Handling in Multi-Objective NAS: Penalty vs. Repair vs. Separation
abstract: Enforcing resource constraints—memory, latency, energy—during neural architecture search can be handled by adding penalty terms to objectives, repairing infeasible candidates to the nearest feasible point, or maintaining a separate infeasible population. This study provides a controlled comparison of these three strategies within a common NSGA-II framework across four constraint tightness levels on NAS-Bench-201. Metrics include final hypervolume of the feasible Pareto front, the rate of constraint violations in the final population, and computational overhead. Repair strategies based on greedy channel reduction consistently produce the most constraint-feasible Pareto fronts under tight budgets, but incur 15–20 percent additional computation per generation. Penalty-based approaches are fastest but produce 12–34 percent infeasible solutions at the tightest constraint levels. Separation methods balance these extremes. Practical recommendations are drawn for three deployment contexts: strict real-time, best-effort, and offline post-hoc filtering.

title: Multi-Objective NAS for Anomaly Detection on Industrial Sensor Streams under Memory Constraints
abstract: Anomaly detection on raw sensor data from industrial machinery is increasingly expected to run on the same low-power embedded controllers that manage the machinery itself. This paper applies multi-objective evolutionary NAS to design recurrent and convolutional-recurrent architectures for time-series anomaly detection within a 128 KB RAM and 512 KB flash budget on an ARM Cortex-M33 target. The search optimises three objectives: reconstruction error on nominal data, RAM usage during inference, and flash footprint. Training and evaluation use a 14-channel vibration dataset collected from rotating machinery in a manufacturing context, comprising 800 hours of nominal operation and 120 annotated fault events across five fault types. The best Pareto solution achieves an F1 score of 0.883 on the held-out fault set while fitting within the memory budget, compared to 0.901 for an unconstrained LSTM baseline that exceeds the budget by a factor of 6. The search also surfaces several compact purely convolutional architectures competitive with recurrent solutions.

title: Effect of water activity on lipase-catalysed phospholipid acylation in microaqueous systems
abstract: Water activity (aw) is a critical parameter in enzymatic acylation reactions carried out under low-water conditions. This study examined how controlled aw (0.11–0.75, set by saturated salt solutions) affected the regioselectivity and yield of sn-2 acylation of lysophosphatidylcholine using immobilised Thermomyces lanuginosus lipase. Reactions were performed in tert-amyl alcohol at 50 °C. At aw 0.33, sn-2 selectivity reached 84% as determined by 13C-NMR positional analysis, compared with 61% at aw 0.75. Total conversion dropped from 78% to 54% as aw increased from 0.11 to 0.75. Residual solvent content in the product was below 5 ppm by GC headspace analysis after vacuum evaporation. The data indicate that maintaining aw between 0.22 and 0.33 provides the best balance of selectivity and conversion for pharmaceutical-grade synthesis, and this window was used as a specification in subsequent scale-up work.

title: Tactile Reading Speed and Error Rate as a Function of Braille Dot Diameter: A User Study with 32 Participants
abstract: Thirty-two experienced Braille readers (18–67 years, 19 women) recruited through a regional blind association evaluated five test cards bearing standardised pharmaceutical text encoded in Braille with dot diameters ranging from 1.2 mm to 1.8 mm in 0.15 mm increments, produced on a calibrated embossing press. Reading speed (characters per minute) and error rate (misidentified cells per 100 characters) were recorded under two lighting conditions (irrelevant to tactile task, included as a distractor control). Mixed-effects regression models showed that a 1.5 mm dot diameter maximised reading speed (mean 68 cpm) while maintaining error rate below 3 %. Participants over 50 years showed a statistically significant preference for 1.6 mm diameter (p = 0.031). Results are discussed in the context of current EN ISO 17351 tolerances, which permit a wider range than the optimal window identified here. Implications for pharmaceutical packaging standards revision are outlined.

title: Perceived Usefulness or Fear of Job Loss? Disentangling Employee Motives for Resisting ERP Implementation in Serbian SMEs
abstract: Enterprise resource planning systems are increasingly adopted by small and medium-sized enterprises across the Western Balkans, yet implementation failure rates remain high. This study investigates whether resistance is driven primarily by usability concerns, anticipated workload changes, or fears about employment security. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 214 employees across 31 manufacturing and retail SMEs in Vojvodina during 2023. Structural equation modelling with partial least squares (SmartPLS 4) was applied to test a model combining the Technology Acceptance Model with job-insecurity theory. Results indicate that perceived threat to employment explains a significantly larger portion of resistance variance (β = 0.41, p < 0.001) than perceived ease of use (β = 0.18, p < 0.05). Moderating effects of organisational tenure were found: employees with more than seven years at the same firm showed stronger fear-based resistance. Trust in direct management partially mediates the relationship between job insecurity and resistance intention. The findings suggest that communication strategies addressing job security concerns should precede usability training during ERP rollout in this context.

title: Middle Managers as Gatekeepers: Qualitative Evidence on Digital Change Mediation in Serbian Family-Owned Firms
abstract: Family-owned small enterprises represent a large share of the Serbian private sector, yet their internal dynamics during digital transformation programmes are rarely studied qualitatively. This paper presents findings from semi-structured interviews with 19 middle managers employed in family-owned service and trade businesses in Novi Sad and Subotica, conducted between October 2024 and February 2025. Using thematic analysis in ATLAS.ti, the study identifies three recurring roles that middle managers assume during digital initiatives: loyal implementers, selective filters, and covert saboteurs. The selective-filter role was most frequently observed and was associated with middle managers who perceived a mismatch between the digital tool introduced and existing informal workflows. Owner-family involvement was found to both accelerate adoption when owners championed the technology and to deepen resistance when ownership authority was perceived as bypassing middle management. Participatory decision-making during tool selection was cited by fourteen of the nineteen respondents as the single most important factor that would have increased their engagement. Findings contribute to research on middle management agency in organisational change and carry practical implications for consultants advising owner-managed firms on digital transition strategies.

title: Using O*NET Task Data as a Starting Point for Local Job Analysis: Adaptation Challenges in a Transition Economy Context
abstract: O*NET, the United States occupational information network, provides detailed task and competency data that researchers worldwide use as a convenient reference point. This methodological paper examines the practical and conceptual challenges that arise when O*NET task data are adapted for job analysis work in a transition economy manufacturing context, drawing on experience from three adaptation projects conducted in Serbia between 2015 and 2022. Challenges identified include: the granularity mismatch between O*NET standardised occupational codes and Serbian occupation classification categories; differences in technology vintage meaning that O*NET task statements describe equipment not present in regional plants; cultural differences in task ownership norms leading to boundary disagreements; and translation ambiguities in technical terminology. For each challenge, adaptation strategies are documented and their effectiveness evaluated through post-adaptation validity checks. The paper provides a structured checklist for practitioners undertaking similar adaptations in comparable contexts.

title: Integrating Event-Calendar Features into Short-Term Hotel Demand Forecasting Models
abstract: City hotels in mid-size European markets are strongly affected by recurring local events—congresses, fairs, sports tournaments—yet most off-the-shelf demand forecasting modules treat event effects as unpredictable noise. This preprint describes a forecasting framework that augments a SARIMA baseline with a structured event-calendar feature matrix compiled from public sources for Novi Sad over 2016–2023. Three event categories are coded: large-scale music festivals (e.g., multi-day outdoor events drawing 40,000+ daily visitors), regional trade fairs, and major sporting fixtures. A gradient-boosted tree model incorporating these features reduces mean absolute percentage error on a held-out test set by 11.4 percentage points relative to the calendar-blind baseline. Revenue simulations suggest that timely rate adjustments triggered by the improved forecasts would have added approximately 6.1% to annual RevPAR for the median hotel in the validation sample.

title: Integrating Market and Non-Market Strategies: Evidence from Regulated Industries in the Western Balkans
abstract: This paper examines how firms in three heavily regulated industries—electricity retail, private healthcare, and commercial banking—coordinate their market and non-market strategies in the Western Balkans. A fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) is applied to a dataset of 41 firms coded on nine conditions derived from resource-dependence and institutional theory. Two sufficient configurations for high integration of market and non-market strategies are identified: one centred on state partial-ownership combined with high regulatory density, and another centred on foreign parent ownership combined with active industry-association participation. The absence of either configuration correlates strongly with reactive rather than anticipatory non-market positioning. The paper also addresses methodological considerations in applying fsQCA to strategy research in data-scarce institutional environments. Results replicate and extend findings from earlier Western European studies while highlighting the distinctive role of partial state ownership as a non-market resource in Balkan contexts.

title: Towards Integrated Sensing and Shape Estimation in Pneumatic Grippers for Agri-Food Sorting Lines
abstract: This preprint describes preliminary work on embedding resistive flex sensors within the wall of a pneumatic bending finger to provide in-situ curvature estimates without external cameras. Three sensor placement strategies—proximal, distal, and dual-location—are compared for their ability to reconstruct finger shape when combined with the reduced-order FE surrogate described in earlier work. Calibration data were collected over 600 pressure–angle combinations. Dual-location placement reduced shape reconstruction error to 3.2 mm mean tip position error compared with 6.8 mm for single proximal placement. A simple Kalman filter fusing sensor readings with surrogate predictions further reduced error to 2.5 mm. Integration into a sorting-line mockup running at 20 items per minute is described qualitatively; quantitative throughput and damage-rate experiments are planned for the next phase. Limitations including sensor drift over 500 actuation cycles and lead routing inside the finger wall are discussed openly.

title: Effect of gear tooth profile errors on torsional dynamics and diagnostic index reliability in planetary gearboxes
abstract: Manufacturing tolerances in tooth profile geometry introduce systematic variations in mesh stiffness that can mask or mimic early-stage pitting signatures. This study uses coordinate measuring machine data from twelve planetary gear sets to characterise profile deviation distributions for ISO quality grades 6, 7, and 8. The measured deviations are introduced into the multi-body torsional dynamics model as deterministic stiffness perturbations. Monte Carlo simulation with 500 realisations per quality grade quantifies the spread in the pitting severity index under healthy conditions. For grade 8 gears, the healthy-state PSI variance is 2.4 times larger than for grade 6, reducing the effective detection margin for pitting areas below 5 mm². Recommendations are formulated for adjusting detection thresholds based on the nominal manufacturing quality grade of a given gearbox, which can be retrieved from component documentation without disassembly.

title: QoS Differentiation for Real-Time Video Using DSCP Marking in Campus SD-WAN Deployments
abstract: Software-Defined WAN architectures offer programmable traffic management but their interaction with Differentiated Services Code Point marking for real-time video is not well understood in campus-scale deployments. This paper reports a measurement study conducted on a 14-node SD-WAN testbed spanning three buildings of the Faculty of Technical Sciences, carrying synthetic H.264 video flows alongside background TCP bulk transfers. Four DSCP marking schemes were compared, including the EF per-hop behaviour and two institutional policies from Croatian and Romanian campus networks. Under 70% link utilisation, EF-marked video flows experienced mean one-way delay of 8.3 ms and zero packet loss, while best-effort video suffered 3.1% loss and 47 ms mean delay. At 90% utilisation, EF marking maintained loss below 0.5% whereas best-effort loss exceeded 11%. Interaction effects between SD-WAN path-selection algorithms and DSCP priority queuing are identified and quantified, and configuration recommendations for campus network operators are provided.

title: Transposing EU Directives into National Labour Law: Monitoring Compliance Gaps in Serbia's Alignment Process
abstract: Serbia's progress reports under the EU accession process contain formal assessments of directive transposition, but these reports rarely identify compliance gaps at the operational level—that is, whether transposed norms are actually applied by inspection and enforcement bodies. This study examines the transposition and operational implementation of four EU labour directives transposed into Serbian law between 2013 and 2018: directives on working time, parental leave, temporary agency work, and information and consultation of workers. For each directive, the transposing legislation was compared to the source directive, and inspection activity data for 2016–2018 were analysed to determine whether inspectors applied the transposed provisions. Findings show transposition fidelity of 84 to 96 percent at the textual level, but operational application rates ranging from 41 to 79 percent depending on the directive. The article identifies the factors—training gaps, resource constraints, and ambiguous enforcement mandates—that explain the implementation shortfall, and proposes a compliance-gap monitoring protocol for use during accession negotiations.

title: Benchmarking Rolling-Horizon Decomposition Variants for Multi-Modal Urban Freight Scheduling
abstract: Urban freight consolidation centres aim to coordinate deliveries across multiple vehicle types—vans, cargo bikes, and small electric vehicles—within a shared urban zone. This paper adapts rolling-horizon decomposition to a multi-modal dynamic pickup-and-delivery problem and benchmarks four variants differing in window length (60 vs. 120 minutes), overlap policy (fixed vs. adaptive), and sub-problem solver (MILP vs. ALNS). Benchmark instances were constructed from synthetic demand profiles calibrated to freight movement data from two Central European cities. The adaptive-overlap variant with ALNS sub-problem solver achieved the best average performance across 300 instances: 5.3% above the static-day lower bound at a median solve time of 28 seconds per rolling step. Fixed-window MILP was competitive only on low-density instances. The paper provides a parameter-selection guide and open-source instance generator as supplementary materials.

title: Scale-up of enzymatic phosphatidylcholine synthesis to 5 L stirred-tank bioreactor: mass transfer and operational stability
abstract: Synthesis of phosphatidylcholine using immobilised Candida rugosa lipase was transferred from 250 mL flask scale to a 5 L stirred-tank bioreactor equipped with a Rushton turbine and baffles. The effects of agitation speed (50–300 rpm) and aeration on enzyme activity and emulsification of the biphasic substrate mixture were characterised. At 150 rpm, the volumetric mass transfer coefficient kLa was 4.8 h⁻¹ and PC yield reached 68.1 ± 3.1% over 10 h, comparable to small-scale results. Foaming was controlled by a mechanical foam breaker without antifoam agents, which was required to preserve lipid purity. Three consecutive 5 L batches showed yield coefficients of 67–69% and enzyme half-life of 14 days under operational conditions. Product quality from bioreactor batches was equivalent to flask-scale material as assessed by 31P-NMR and HPLC-ELSD purity (96.4 ± 0.9%). These data confirm straightforward scalability of the solvent-free route.

title: Preparation and physicochemical characterisation of liposomes from enzymatically synthesised phosphatidylcholine
abstract: Liposomes were prepared from phosphatidylcholine produced by immobilised lipase-catalysed synthesis and purified by preparative chromatography. The thin-film hydration method followed by sequential extrusion through 400, 200, and 100 nm polycarbonate membranes yielded unilamellar vesicles with mean diameter 118 ± 7 nm, polydispersity index 0.09, and zeta potential −14.2 ± 1.1 mV as measured by dynamic light scattering. Vesicle morphology was confirmed by cryo-TEM at the Institute of Oncology Vojvodina electron microscopy facility. Encapsulation efficiency of a model hydrophilic drug (sodium fluorescein) was 23.4 ± 2.1%, determined by size-exclusion chromatography and fluorimetry. The phospholipid composition of liposome membranes matched the input material within ±2 mol% by HPLC-ELSD. Storage stability at 4 °C over 90 days showed less than 8% change in mean diameter and no increase in PDI, indicating adequate colloidal stability for pharmaceutical applications.

title: Liposomal encapsulation of a water-soluble antifungal compound: influence of phospholipid acyl chain composition on encapsulation efficiency and in vitro release
abstract: Liposomes composed of phosphatidylcholine variants differing in acyl chain length and saturation (dipalmitoyl-PC, palmitoyl-oleoyl-PC, and dioleoyl-PC) were loaded with the model antifungal compound flucytosine-analogue FT-7 (a fictional compound used as a test molecule in this study) at drug-to-lipid molar ratios of 1:5, 1:10, and 1:20. Encapsulation efficiency ranged from 18.7% (DOPC, 1:5) to 34.2% (DPPC, 1:20) as determined by ultrafiltration and HPLC-UV. In vitro release in phosphate-buffered saline at 37 °C followed Korsmeyer–Peppas kinetics; DPPC liposomes showed slower release (t50 = 14.2 h) compared with DOPC (t50 = 5.8 h), consistent with a gel-phase membrane at physiological temperature. Membrane fluidity measured by DPH fluorescence anisotropy correlated inversely with release rate (r² = 0.91). Results demonstrate that acyl chain composition is a primary design variable for controlling the release profile of hydrophilic drugs from liposomal systems and guide selection criteria for formulation development.

title: Automated Contour Quality Metrics for Interpolation-Ready Glyph Masters: A Benchmark Dataset for Southern Slavic Characters
abstract: Interpolation-based font production requires that glyph masters share compatible contour structures, but no standardised benchmark exists for evaluating contour quality specifically in Southern Slavic character sets, which include both Latin extended and Cyrillic blocks. This paper introduces the SlavoContour-109 benchmark dataset, comprising 109 glyphs drawn from Serbian, Croatian, Bosnian, Slovenian, Macedonian, and Rusyn orthographies, each annotated with a reference contour and a set of deliberately introduced quality defects—direction errors, stray points, open paths, and incompatible node counts. Four automated checking tools (FontBakery, FoundryFabriek QC, a custom Python script, and a commercial proofing plugin) were evaluated against the dataset. Precision and recall were computed per defect category across all 109 glyphs. The custom Python script achieved the highest F1 score for direction errors (0.91) but performed poorly on stray-point detection (0.54). The dataset is published in UFO and Glyphs 3 format and is intended for use in type-design pedagogy and automated font production pipelines.
