title: Real-time optimisation of ORC operating conditions using a Gaussian process surrogate trained on dynamic simulation data
abstract: Real-time optimisation of ORC operating points requires a model that evaluates quickly enough for online use while remaining accurate across a wide operating envelope. A Gaussian process (GP) surrogate model was trained on 1,800 steady-state snapshots extracted from validated dynamic Modelica simulations of a 50 kWe ORC unit operating with R1234ze(E) over heat-source temperatures from 100 to 180 °C and cooling-water temperatures from 10 to 30 °C. The GP surrogate predicts net power output with a root-mean-square error of 0.31 kW on a hold-out test set and evaluates in under 2 ms, enabling gradient-based optimisation of pump speed and bypass-valve position at each sampling interval. A real-time optimiser was implemented in a Python-based supervisory layer and tested in hardware-in-the-loop experiments using the laboratory rig with a simulated industrial heat-source profile. Over a 72-hour test, the real-time optimiser increased mean net power by 5.8% relative to fixed setpoint operation, with the largest gains occurring during periods of rapid heat-source temperature variation.

title: Sleep architecture in focal cortical dysplasia subtypes: MRI-confirmed type I versus type II lesions
abstract: Focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) is a leading cause of drug-resistant epilepsy, yet differences in sleep architecture between FCD subtypes remain poorly characterised. We compared overnight polysomnography in 17 patients with histologically or radiologically classified FCD type I and 14 with FCD type II, all with drug-resistant focal epilepsy. FCD type II patients exhibited higher IED density across all NREM stages (N2: 6.2 vs 3.9/min, p=0.007) and more severe suppression of N3 sleep (8.7% vs 14.4%, p=0.012). REM percentage did not differ significantly between subtypes. High-frequency oscillations visible on polysomnographic EEG derivations overlying the lesion were more prevalent in type II (detected in 10/14 patients vs 5/17, p=0.038). Daytime sleepiness scores were worse in type II patients. These differences suggest that FCD subtype should be considered when interpreting sleep studies and designing sleep-targeted adjunct interventions in this population.

title: Sleep and epilepsy: a practical guide to polysomnographic assessment in adult neurology
abstract: This book chapter provides a practical framework for neurologists performing or interpreting polysomnography in adult patients with epilepsy. The chapter covers electrode placement considerations when epilepsy monitoring is integrated with polysomnography, AASM sleep staging as applied to epilepsy patients with diffuse interictal activity, and the distinction between parasomnias and nocturnal seizures using combined video, EEG, and respiratory channel review. Specific sections address artefact recognition in epilepsy patients on multiple antiseizure medications, scoring guidance for nights containing electrographic seizures, and interpretation caveats for patients with encephalopathy. Case examples drawn from the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina sleep laboratory illustrate common diagnostic dilemmas. The chapter also reviews current evidence on how seizure frequency and antiseizure drug class differentially affect sleep staging outcomes, providing summary tables for clinical reference. The intended audience is neurology residents and practising neurologists without formal sleep medicine training.

title: Automated IED detection during polysomnography: validation of a convolutional neural network pipeline against expert annotation in 60 recordings
abstract: Manual annotation of interictal epileptiform discharges in overnight polysomnographic recordings is time-consuming and prone to inter-rater variability. We developed and validated a convolutional neural network (CNN) pipeline trained on 140 annotated overnight recordings from the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina sleep laboratory and tested it on an independent validation set of 60 recordings (30 temporal lobe, 30 frontal lobe epilepsy). The model achieved sensitivity of 88.3% and specificity of 91.6% at the epoch level for IED detection compared with consensus annotation by two senior neurophysiologists. False-positive rates were highest in N1 sleep due to vertex waves and K-complex morphology overlap. Processing time per full overnight recording was 4.2 minutes on standard laboratory hardware. Per-stage IED density computed by the model correlated strongly with manual counts (r=0.91). The pipeline is intended as a research tool to reduce annotation burden in sleep–epilepsy studies and does not replace clinical review.

title: Impact of lacosamide versus levetiracetam add-on therapy on sleep macroarchitecture: a randomised crossover polysomnographic study
abstract: Lacosamide and levetiracetam are both used as add-on therapies in focal epilepsy, but their differential effects on sleep architecture have not been compared in a controlled setting. We conducted a randomised, open-label crossover study in 38 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy who were assigned to lacosamide or levetiracetam add-on for 12 weeks before crossing over after a four-week washout. Overnight polysomnography was performed at baseline, after each treatment period, and after washout. Lacosamide treatment was associated with a modest increase in N2 percentage (+4.1%) and reduction in REM percentage (−3.2%, p=0.027) relative to baseline. Levetiracetam showed no significant macroarchitecture changes. IED density in N2 was marginally lower under lacosamide (−1.1/min, p=0.06). Behavioural adverse effects (irritability, rated on a standardised scale) were higher under levetiracetam and correlated with poorer subjective sleep scores. Neither drug significantly altered total sleep time or sleep efficiency. The results inform drug selection for patients who also report sleep complaints.

title: High-density EEG polysomnography as a presurgical tool in drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy: concordance with intracranial EEG source estimates
abstract: In a subset of presurgical candidates, it remains unclear whether non-invasive source localisation during sleep IEDs can approximate findings from intracranial EEG (iEEG). We prospectively enrolled 21 patients with drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy undergoing stereo-EEG (SEEG) evaluation and performed 64-channel overnight polysomnography within two weeks before electrode implantation. IED clusters identified during N2 sleep were submitted to equivalent current dipole modelling and standardised low-resolution electromagnetic tomography. Source estimates were compared with the clinically designated seizure onset zone from SEEG. Agreement within one gyrus was achieved in 15 of 21 patients (71%). Source estimates were closer to the SEEG onset zone for IEDs occurring during N2 sleep relative to those in N1 (mean Euclidean distance 14.2 mm vs 21.8 mm, p=0.018). These preliminary data suggest that sleep-state selection matters for non-invasive source analysis and that N2-restricted IED averaging improves localisation accuracy without requiring additional awake monitoring sessions.

title: Mass spectrometry-based quantification of tau phosphopeptides in CSF: comparison with immunoassay in a regional dementia cohort
abstract: Immunoassays for phospho-tau rely on antibody specificity that may vary across lots and manufacturers. We developed and validated a targeted liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) method for simultaneous quantification of tau phosphopeptides spanning residues 173–184 (pT181) and 212–221 (pT217) in CSF, using stable isotope-labelled internal standards. The method was applied to 95 CSF samples from Vojvodina (35 AD, 30 MCI, 30 controls). Calibration curves were linear from 5 to 500 pg/mL (R²>0.998); inter-day CV was <9% for both peptides. Spearman correlations with the respective immunoassays were r=0.86 for pT181 and r=0.81 for pT217. MS-based quantification confirmed the diagnostic superiority of pT217 (AUC 0.93 vs 0.88 for pT181). Two samples showing immunoassay outlier values were confirmed normal by MS, suggesting matrix interference in the immunoassay. This method provides a reference platform for regional immunoassay calibration.

title: Thermal detection thresholds in type 2 diabetic patients with and without painful neuropathy: a cross-sectional study
abstract: We applied a standardised quantitative sensory testing (QST) protocol derived from the German Research Network on Neuropathic Pain (DFNS) to 64 patients with type 2 diabetes recruited from the endocrinology outpatient service of the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. Patients were divided into painful neuropathy (n=31) and painless neuropathy (n=33) groups on the basis of structured interview and the Douleur Neuropathique 4 questionnaire. Both groups showed significantly elevated warm detection thresholds at the dorsum of the foot compared with healthy controls (n=40), consistent with small-fibre dysfunction. The painful group additionally demonstrated paradoxical heat sensation at a higher rate (48% vs 18%, p=0.012) and lower mechanical pain thresholds at the hand, suggesting a pattern of preserved or enhanced central sensitisation alongside peripheral deafferentation. Cooling detection thresholds did not differ significantly between pain groups. These results support a loss-of-function phenotype with superimposed gain-of-function features in the painful subgroup and underscore the need to characterise sensory profiles rather than treating neuropathic pain as a single entity.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Lifetime Estimation Methods for Primary Lithium Cells in Static IoT Sensors
abstract: Four lifetime estimation methods are benchmarked against each other using a common dataset of 60 Li/MnO₂ and 60 Li/SOCl₂ cells discharged under eight realistic IoT sensor profiles. The methods compared are: (i) Peukert-based capacity scaling, (ii) a lookup-table approach derived from manufacturer pulse-discharge curves, (iii) a two-RC equivalent-circuit model updated by EIS, and (iv) a Gaussian process regression model trained on early-discharge features. All methods are evaluated on prediction error at 80 % and 100 % cell depletion. The Gaussian process method achieves the lowest median absolute error (6.2 % at end-of-life) but requires 11 input features extracted during the first 5 % of discharge. The EIS-based model achieves 8.7 % median error with fewer inputs. The Peukert method is least accurate at 22 % median error. A decision flowchart is provided to help practitioners choose a method based on available hardware and tolerable error. All data and model code are published under a CC-BY licence.

title: Fault detection for ORC units using a moving-horizon estimator applied to measured process data from a ceramics plant
abstract: Early fault detection in ORC units operating in unattended industrial settings can prevent damage and unplanned downtime. A moving-horizon state and parameter estimator was formulated using the validated dynamic ORC model, with working-fluid charge level, overall evaporator heat transfer coefficient, and expander isentropic efficiency treated as slowly varying parameters. The estimator was applied to 11 months of process data logged at 30-second intervals from a 35 kWe ORC unit installed at a ceramics plant in southern Serbia. Five fault events recorded in the plant maintenance log (two partial refrigerant leaks, two pump bearing degradations, and one condenser blockage) were used to assess detection capability. The estimator flagged all five events before visible performance degradation occurred in net-power trends, with lead times ranging from 3 to 19 days. One false positive was recorded during a planned heat-source shutdown misread as a charge fault. The approach requires no additional instrumentation beyond the standard ORC sensor set.

title: Comparative assessment of zeotropic mixtures as ORC working fluids for a steel mill recuperator heat source
abstract: Zeotropic working-fluid mixtures exploit the temperature glide during phase change to improve thermal match with non-isothermal heat sources and sinks, potentially reducing irreversibility in heat exchangers. This study evaluates six binary mixtures — R1234ze(E)/R245fa at three compositions, pentane/isopentane at two compositions, and R1233zd(E)/cyclopentane — against their pure-component counterparts for an ORC recovering heat from a steel-mill recuperator exhaust at 185 °C, 4.2 kg/s. Temperature glide in the condenser was constrained to match a cooling tower water flow available at 25 °C. Pinch-point analysis in Modelica was used to size heat exchangers for each mixture. The R1233zd(E)/cyclopentane mixture at a 0.6/0.4 molar ratio achieved the best net efficiency (13.6%) compared to 12.1% for pure R1233zd(E) and 11.8% for pure cyclopentane, at the cost of a 14% larger heat exchanger area. Dynamic simulations of the preferred mixture showed that composition shift due to differential leakage at a rate of 0.2% per month would reduce efficiency by 0.4 percentage points per year, a manageable degradation.

title: Characterisation of global horizontal irradiance variability at a lowland mid-latitude site using hourly ground measurements
abstract: This study analyses ten years (2000–2009) of hourly global horizontal irradiance (GHI) measurements collected at a meteorological station near Novi Sad to characterise intra-annual and inter-annual variability relevant to PV system design. Clearness index distributions were computed on monthly and seasonal bases, and fitted to beta probability distributions. The study finds that the coefficient of variation of daily GHI ranges from 18% in July to 47% in December, with a mean annual GHI of 1 382 kWh/m². Persistence of low-irradiance sequences exceeding five consecutive days was identified as the primary driver of storage requirements for stand-alone systems in the region. Autocorrelation structure of daily clearness index sequences was also quantified. Results are compared against two satellite-derived irradiance databases; systematic biases of 3–7% were found during winter months. The dataset and fitted distribution parameters are made available as supplementary material for use in system sizing studies.

title: Capacity sizing of a PV–battery system for a remote water quality monitoring station: methodology and case study on the Danube
abstract: Remote environmental monitoring stations must maintain continuous operation with minimal maintenance access, making reliable power supply critical. This paper documents the full sizing workflow applied to a water quality monitoring station installed on a Danube riverbank approximately 40 km downstream of Novi Sad, powered entirely by a PV–battery system. Load characterisation yielded an average daily demand of 18.6 Wh with a peak draw of 4.2 W from sensors, data logger, and cellular modem. The PV array and LFP battery bank were sized using a monthly simulation approach with LOLP ≤ 0.005 as constraint, resulting in a 60 Wp panel at 40° tilt and a 120 Wh usable battery capacity. Twelve months of post-installation monitoring confirmed zero loss-of-load events and a measured annual energy surplus of 34%, suggesting moderate conservatism in the applied safety factors. Lessons learned regarding connector corrosion, bird-related soiling, and seasonal load variation are discussed for designers of similar installations.

title: A zone-based model for fuel-NOx formation in small pellet burners: derivation and validation against experimental data
abstract: This paper presents a zone-based semi-empirical model for predicting fuel-NOx formation in small pellet burners operating between 30 % and 100 % rated load. The combustion chamber was divided into four zones—devolatilisation, primary flame, burnout, and post-flame—each characterised by time-averaged temperature and species concentrations derived from the in-flame measurements reported previously. Fuel-nitrogen content of the pellet batch was measured as 0.11 % by dry weight using a CHNS elemental analyser. NOx conversion efficiency from fuel-N was modelled using modified De Soete kinetics with empirically adjusted pre-exponential factors. Predicted NOx at the stack ranged from 71 to 138 mg/Nm³ across the load range tested; measured values were 69 to 143 mg/Nm³. Mean absolute error was 6.3 mg/Nm³. The model also captured the reversal in CO–NOx slope that occurs below 50 % load, where incomplete combustion zones expand and locally reduce NO to N₂. The zone approach requires only standard fuel analysis and burner geometry as inputs, making it applicable without CFD.

title: Box–Behnken design optimisation of coating suspension composition and process parameters for sustained-release pellet coating
abstract: A Box–Behnken design with 15 experimental runs was used to optimise three formulation variables—ethylcellulose-to-hydroxypropyl methylcellulose ratio (70:30–90:10), plasticiser level (5–15% w/w relative to polymer), and coating level (5–15% weight gain)—alongside two process variables: inlet air temperature (35–55 °C) and spray rate (5–15 g/min), for sustained-release coating of 500–600 µm theophylline pellets. Drug release at 1 h, 4 h, and 8 h in phosphate buffer pH 6.8 was used as the response. Response surface models showed significant main effects of coating level and polymer ratio on the 1 h release (R² = 0.94), with a strong interaction between plasticiser level and inlet air temperature at 4 h. Optimised conditions predicted 18.7% release at 1 h, 52.3% at 4 h, and 89.1% at 8 h; experimental verification batches (n = 3) yielded values within 3.4% of predictions. Desirability function composite optimisation was used for multi-response optimisation.

title: Hardware-in-the-loop testing of UAV variable-rate spray controllers under simulated canopy sensing inputs
abstract: Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) simulation was used to evaluate three candidate variable-rate spray controllers before field deployment. The HIL bench combined a physical pump-nozzle assembly with simulated multispectral sensor feeds generated from 2019 orchard flights replayed at 1×, 2× and 4× speed. Three controller architectures were compared: rule-based threshold switching, a proportional controller with dead-band, and a model-predictive controller with a 200 ms horizon. Metrics included tracking error relative to a reference prescription, actuator duty cycle, and total volume dispensed. The model-predictive controller achieved the lowest mean tracking error (2.1 L ha⁻¹) but required 18% longer initialisation time. At 4× replay speed, all controllers degraded; the proportional controller maintained stability while MPC diverged when sensor latency exceeded 150 ms. The HIL framework reduced field testing iterations by an estimated factor of three and is described in sufficient detail for replication.

title: Simultaneous LiDAR and multispectral sensing from a single UAV platform: sensor fusion approach for vineyard canopy characterisation
abstract: A co-aligned payload carrying a 16-channel LiDAR and a five-band multispectral camera was flown over 11 vineyard blocks in the Fruška Gora wine region during three phenological stages in 2021. Temporal registration of the two streams required a novel extrinsic calibration target yielding angular alignment errors below 0.3°. Fused point clouds that combined geometric canopy density with spectral NDVI values were segmented into canopy, post, and gap classes using a random forest classifier (overall accuracy 93.4%). Canopy volume and chlorophyll-proxy index were jointly used to generate dual-variable prescription maps specifying both spray volume and concentration. Compared with single-sensor prescriptions, the fused approach reduced over-application in dense low-vigour zones by 19% and under-application in sparse high-vigour zones by 12% as validated against reference hand-sprayer applications. Sensor synchronisation drift was identified as the primary remaining technical challenge.

title: Actuator response characterisation of variable-rate UAV nozzles under flight-representative vibration and pressure conditions
abstract: This bench study characterised the dynamic response of three commercially available solenoid nozzle valves proposed for UAV variable-rate spray payloads. Valves were tested on a vibration table reproducing accelerometer-recorded UAV flight profiles (0.5–80 Hz, up to 6 g). Actuation response times (open and close) were measured at line pressures of 1, 2, and 3 bar using high-speed pressure transducers at 5 kHz. All three valves showed statistically significant increases in close-delay at 2 g lateral vibration: mean close-delay increased from 18 ms to 31 ms for the worst performer. Flow rate non-linearity at partial duty cycles exceeded 8% in two of the three designs. A fourth prototype valve with a mechanical anti-vibration sleeve reduced vibration-induced delay to 4 ms. The study provided empirically grounded specifications for UAV spray controller designers and recommended test protocol standardisation across manufacturers.
venue: Journal of Agricultural Engineering (Italian Association of Agricultural Engineering)

title: Closed-loop altitude and spray rate co-control for UAV application over row crops with variable canopy height
abstract: Variable canopy height in row crops causes UAV sprayers to operate at non-constant nozzle-to-target distances, leading to deposit pattern distortion and variable droplet size. This study implemented a coupled controller where a downward-facing LiDAR altimeter fed a flight controller maintaining constant nozzle-to-canopy distance, while the same range signal concurrently adjusted pump duty cycle to maintain constant deposit density. Experiments were conducted over sunflower fields with measured canopy height variance of 0.38 m² across plots during the 2023 season. The coupled controller held nozzle-to-canopy distance within ±6 cm (σ = 3.1 cm) and application rate within ±4.7% of target across six flights totalling 8.4 ha. Uncoupled baseline flights showed ±22% rate deviation over the same terrain. Wind interaction at 3 m s⁻¹ cross-wind degraded altitude tracking; a feed-forward wind compensation term reduced the effect by 55%.

title: Regulatory and operational constraints on autonomous UAV spray applications in Serbian and Hungarian agriculture: a practitioner survey
abstract: Despite technical advances in UAV variable-rate spraying, deployment in commercial farming remains limited. This paper reports results of a structured survey of 78 agricultural practitioners (farmers, agronomists, and UAV service operators) across Vojvodina and Csongrád-Csanád county (Hungary) conducted in late 2024. Respondents rated barriers to adoption on a five-point Likert scale across regulatory, economic, technical, and agronomic dimensions. Regulatory uncertainty was the most frequently cited critical barrier (68% of respondents), followed by high equipment cost (54%) and lack of certified operators (47%). Technical reliability concerns were rated lower than expected, suggesting that early adopters have had broadly positive experiences with equipment performance. Cross-border differences in civil aviation authority interpretation of spray UAV rules were reported by all cross-border service operators interviewed (n = 11). The paper maps current national regulatory frameworks and identifies specific points of divergence that could inform harmonisation efforts.

title: Onboard edge inference of crop stress indicators from compressed multispectral imagery for real-time UAV actuation
abstract: Running full-resolution multispectral processing on UAV payloads is constrained by compute power and thermal limits. This preprint describes deployment of a quantised convolutional neural network (5.2 M parameters, INT8) on a low-power system-on-chip to infer three-class crop stress labels (healthy, nitrogen-deficient, water-stressed) from 320×240 multispectral tiles at 9 Hz during flight. Training used 14 800 labelled tiles collected from soybean and maize fields during the 2024 season. Inference accuracy on the held-out test set was 84.7% (F1 macro), degrading to 78.2% under high solar angle variation without downwelling correction. Actuation commands derived from the edge model were compared against post-flight reference commands from full-resolution offline analysis: agreement was 91.3% at the spray-zone level. Power consumption averaged 3.4 W, compatible with a 6 Ah UAV battery budget. The model weights and training pipeline are released openly.

title: The Establishment of the Administrative Court of Serbia (2010): Legislative Choices and Inherited Deficits
abstract: Serbia's Administrative Court, created by the Law on Administrative Disputes of 2009 and fully operational from 1 January 2010, represented the first dedicated administrative court in the country since the interwar period. This article analyses the parliamentary record, comparative law memoranda prepared by the Ministry of Justice, and the court's published statistics from its first three years of operation (2010–2012). The article identifies three structural choices—single-instance jurisdiction, limited cassation-only review, and the exclusion of urgency procedures—that reflect path-dependent influences from the Yugoslav period and fiscal constraints, rather than from the EU administrative justice models that were formally cited during the reform process. Case-load data show that by end-2012 the court had a backlog of approximately 23,000 unresolved cases, already nearly double its annual throughput capacity. The article argues that the reform achieved formal institutional separation without resolving the functional weaknesses of administrative adjudication.

title: The Role of Private Standardisation Bodies in Public Regulation: Accountability Gaps in Serbian and Croatian Law
abstract: When a government ministry formally adopts a privately developed technical standard and references it in a binding regulation, it delegates normative authority to an entity that operates outside the constitutional structures designed to ensure democratic accountability. This article examines this phenomenon in Serbia and Croatia, focusing on standards adopted by the Serbian Institute for Standardisation and the Croatian Standards Institute and subsequently referenced in ministerial regulations in the sectors of construction products, electrical equipment, and food safety between 2014 and 2020. Forty-one such cross-references are examined for the adequacy of public participation procedures, transparency of standard-setting, and availability of judicial review. The study finds that neither legal order has developed adequate accountability mechanisms for private bodies exercising de facto public regulatory functions. Possible remedies drawing on Dutch and German experience are outlined.

title: Dieline-to-printed-artwork registration accuracy under varying die-cutting pressure and board caliper
abstract: Die-cutting pressure and board caliper variation affect the dimensional accuracy of cut and creased folding cartons, which in turn determines how well pre-positioned artwork aligns with structural features such as windows, tear-strips, and edge-to-edge bleeds. This work designed a full-factorial experiment with three levels of die-cutting pressure (80%, 100%, 120% of nominal) and three commercial board calipers (280, 350, 410 g/m²) across four carton dieline families. Cut-dimension deviations and crease-position deviations were measured on 30 samples per condition using a digital image analysis system. Board caliper had a larger effect on crease position than die-cutting pressure (η² = 0.41 vs. 0.19). A correction table mapping caliper to artwork pre-offset values was derived; applying it reduced crease-to-artwork misregistration from a mean of 0.54 mm to 0.21 mm without press adjustments.

title: Substrate-aware PDF rendering: adjusting halftone geometry for measured surface roughness in inkjet printing on corrugated board
abstract: Direct inkjet printing on corrugated board produces halftone dot gain that varies with flute type and liner roughness, causing calibrated ICC profiles to underperform relative to smoother substrates. This study measured Ra surface roughness across three corrugated board grades (B-flute, E-flute, EB-flute) using a contact profilometer and correlated roughness at 16 measurement points per sheet with dot gain at those locations. A locally adaptive halftone screening strategy was developed that modifies screen frequency and dot shape as a function of locally predicted dot gain, estimated from a roughness lookup table built from 240 calibration patches. On B-flute board, mean tonal error (ΔL* across a 51-step wedge) fell from 3.8 to 1.9; on E-flute it fell from 2.6 to 1.4. The approach is implemented as a pre-RIP filter requiring only a roughness scan of the substrate batch.

title: Ink-film optical density and gloss as indirect indicators of surface energy adequacy in flexographic printing on polyolefin films
abstract: Direct surface energy measurement is not feasible during high-speed printing, so indirect print-quality indicators that correlate with surface activation level would be practically useful. This study examined whether optical density (measured by reflection densitometry) and 60° specular gloss of cyan flexographic ink prints on corona-treated BOPP and LDPE films correlate sufficiently well with independently measured surface free energy values to serve as on-press proxies. Films were prepared at seven discrete corona dose levels (0.5–4.5 W·min/m²) and printed on a laboratory flexographic proofer at 100 m/min with a fixed anilox volume of 4.0 cm³/m². Pearson correlation coefficients between surface energy and optical density were r = 0.91 (BOPP) and r = 0.88 (LDPE); between surface energy and gloss, r = 0.85 and r = 0.79, respectively. A threshold surface energy of approximately 38 mN/m corresponded to an optical density plateau, below which density dropped sharply. These correlations are strong enough to support a simple two-point calibration chart for press operators to estimate surface activation status from routine densitometry.

title: Complexation of zinc(II) with oxalate in aqueous solutions at pH 5.0–8.5: relevance to zinc mobility in acid and calcareous soils
abstract: Zinc deficiency is widespread in calcareous soils across the Pannonian Plain, and zinc–organic acid complexation critically governs Zn solubility and root uptake. Stability constants for Zn²⁺–oxalate (ZnL⁰, ZnL₂²⁻ and ZnHL⁺) were measured by potentiometry and UV-Vis spectrophotometry at 25 °C, I = 0.10 M (KNO₃). Measurements were performed over 44 independent titration curves covering metal-to-ligand ratios from 1:1 to 1:10. HYPERQUAD refinement gave log K(ZnL⁰) = 4.89 ± 0.02, log K(ZnL₂²⁻) = 7.98 ± 0.05, and log K(ZnHL⁺) = 2.10 ± 0.08. Speciation modelling using MINEQL+ version 4.6 was applied to three Vojvodina soil pore-water compositions (measured total oxalate 8–45 µM). At pH 8.0, ZnL⁰ accounts for less than 4% of total dissolved Zn, indicating that oxalate alone is insufficient to explain observed Zn mobilisation in these alkaline soils.

title: Simulaciono modeliranje postmerger integracije kao alat za upravljanje ljudskim resursima: pregled literature i istraživački okvir
abstract: Rad daje sistematski pregled literature objavljene između 2000. i 2017. godine koja se bavi primenom simulacionih metoda – posebno agent-baziranih modela i sistemske dinamike – u kontekstu postmerger upravljanja ljudskim resursima u manufacturing sektoru. Analizirano je 68 radova identifikovanih pretragom baza Scopus i Web of Science. Rezultati pokazuju da dominantni pristup u literaturi zanemaruje kompetencijski pad kao zasebnu varijablu i uglavnom modelira samo tok zaposlenih, a ne kvalitet njihovog znanja. Predložen je integrativni istraživački okvir koji kombinuje teoriju organizacionog učenja, model kompetencijskog pada i mrežne teorije prenosa znanja. Okvir služi kao osnova za razvoj simulacionih alata prilagođenih potrebama HR menadžera u spajajućim prerađivačkim preduzećima. Identifikovane su četiri prioritetne oblasti za buduća istraživanja.

title: Cross-Functional Team Composition and Knowledge Retention After Merger: Evidence from a Discrete-Event and Agent-Based Hybrid Model
abstract: We present a hybrid simulation model combining discrete-event and agent-based components to investigate how cross-functional team composition affects knowledge retention in the 36 months following a manufacturing firm merger. The discrete-event layer models project workflows and task allocation, while the agent-based layer represents individual knowledge states and interpersonal learning interactions. The hybrid architecture is implemented in AnyLogic 8.4 and parameterised using HR records and skill assessments from a longitudinal dataset collected at an automotive-component supplier in northern Serbia (n=89 employees). Four team composition strategies are evaluated: random reassignment, competency-matching, social-network-preserving assignment, and a hybrid heuristic developed in consultation with the company's HR department. Social-network-preserving assignment yields the highest aggregate knowledge retention (12.4% above the random baseline at month 36) but underperforms on project throughput in the first twelve months. The hybrid heuristic balances both objectives with a 7.1% knowledge retention gain and no statistically significant throughput reduction.

title: Representing Informal Mentoring in Agent-Based Models of Post-Merger Knowledge Transfer
abstract: Informal mentoring relationships are frequently cited as a primary channel for tacit knowledge transfer following organisational mergers, yet they are rarely represented explicitly in simulation models. This paper proposes and evaluates three mechanisms for encoding informal mentoring in an ABM: (1) a random-encounter mechanism with proximity weighting, (2) a directed preferential attachment mechanism based on competency gap, and (3) an empirically derived network seeded from sociometric survey data. The three mechanisms are implemented in AnyLogic 8.7 and tested against a 12-month observational dataset from a Vojvodina food-processing company that merged two production sites in 2019 (n=61 employees). Validation against held-out quarterly competency assessments shows that the empirically derived network mechanism produces the closest match to observed outcomes (RMSE = 0.13), while the random-encounter mechanism systematically underestimates knowledge transfer rates in the first four months post-merger. The paper provides open model documentation to support replication.

title: Workforce Simulation as a Decision-Support Tool for HR Managers in Manufacturing Mergers: A Prototype and Usability Assessment
abstract: This paper describes the design, implementation, and usability evaluation of a decision-support prototype that wraps an agent-based simulation model in a graphical interface intended for use by HR managers without modelling expertise. The underlying ABM, calibrated on data from three completed mergers in the Serbian manufacturing sector, simulates knowledge transfer and competency decay across a 36-month integration horizon. The interface allows users to specify integration timeline, team reassignment policy, and training budget, and returns visualised projections of aggregate competency levels and estimated productivity impact. Usability was assessed through a think-aloud study with eight HR managers from companies at the Novi Sad Science and Technology Park and affiliated firms. Participants rated the tool positively on task completion and output clarity (SUS score 74.5) but identified model parameter transparency as a limitation. The paper discusses implications for deploying simulation tools in practitioner contexts and outlines planned improvements based on the usability findings.

title: Decay Asymmetry in Merged Engineering Teams: Do Employees from the Acquired Firm Lose Competencies Faster?
abstract: This preprint reports preliminary findings from an ongoing study examining whether employees from the acquired firm in a manufacturing merger experience systematically faster competency decay than employees from the acquiring firm. Using anonymised longitudinal skill-assessment records from four mergers completed in Serbia and Hungary between 2018 and 2023 (combined n=204 employees, 24-month observation per merger), we fit individual competency trajectories using mixed-effects models with firm-of-origin as a grouping variable. Results indicate a statistically significant decay asymmetry: acquired-firm employees show a mean annual competency decline of 14.2% versus 8.7% for acquiring-firm employees (difference 5.5 percentage points, 95% CI [3.1, 7.9]), controlling for role change, age, and pre-merger competency level. The asymmetry is most pronounced in technical skills and weakest in process knowledge. We discuss alternative explanations including social marginalisation, reduced access to informal knowledge networks, and differential exposure to training resources. An agent-based model encoding the asymmetry mechanism is under development.

title: Verification of Combined Heat and Power Savings Under IPMVP Option C: Complicating Factors and Case Evidence
abstract: Combined heat and power installations in industrial facilities create verification challenges for Option C protocols because total facility electricity import decreases while on-site generation increases, requiring metering of both streams. This paper analyses three CHP projects in Vojvodina where Option C was applied at the utility boundary. The baseline model must account for CHP dispatch decisions that vary with energy prices, adding a dispatch variable to the regression. Results show that failing to account for dispatch introduces a downward bias of 9–14% in estimated electricity savings. The paper also addresses the allocation of savings between the CHP measure and complementary efficiency measures implemented concurrently, proposing an attribution procedure based on partial regression coefficients. Estimated savings across the three sites ranged from 1,100 to 4,800 MWh/year with relative uncertainties of 6–11% at the 90% confidence level.

title: Applying value-stream mapping to identify waste in a precast hollow-core slab facility
abstract: Value-stream mapping (VSM) was applied to the full production sequence of a hollow-core slab facility with an annual output of approximately 28,000 square metres. Current-state maps were constructed through three weeks of floor-level observation and timed walks, capturing 11 distinct process steps from raw material receipt to dispatch yard staging. The analysis identified waiting and over-processing as the dominant waste categories, accounting together for 39% of total lead time. Transport loops between the curing yard and the finishing area were measured at a combined daily distance of 1.2 km per operator. Future-state maps were developed under two scenarios—one preserving existing equipment layout, one incorporating a partial cell redesign—projecting lead-time reductions of 22% and 34% respectively. The paper provides a step-by-step mapping template adapted to the physical constraints of long-line prestressed concrete production.

title: Digitalisation and Workforce Restructuring in Serbian Commercial Television, 2010–2017
abstract: This article traces workforce changes at Serbian commercial television broadcasters across the period of mandatory digital switchover, completed in 2015, using data from the national broadcasting regulator's annual licence reports combined with 41 interviews with production managers and technical staff. Total permanent employment in television production fell by 26 percent between 2010 and 2017 at the nine largest commercial broadcasters surveyed. Technical staff experienced the sharpest contraction, losing 38 percent of positions, while on-screen presenting roles were more stable. The article examines how digitalisation was used rhetorically by management as justification for redundancies that respondents attributed primarily to revenue pressures and ownership rationalisation strategies unrelated to technical change. It contributes to debates about technological determinism in media labour studies by showing that digitalisation functioned more as an enabling condition for restructuring than as its direct cause.

title: Concurrent Dual-Band DPD Using Shared Observation Receiver with Sub-Band Decomposition
abstract: Concurrent dual-band transmission in 700 MHz and 3.5 GHz bands from a single PA requires linearisation across both bands simultaneously. A shared observation receiver based on sub-band decomposition using polyphase filter banks is proposed to reduce hardware cost relative to two dedicated observation paths. The sub-band outputs feed two independent GMP-based DPD cores that share coefficient update resources. Validation is performed on a broadband GaN PA with 3 dB compression point of 40 W, driven by simultaneous 10 MHz LTE at 703 MHz and 40 MHz 5G NR at 3.48 GHz. The dual-band DPD achieves ACPR values of −50.2 dBc and −48.7 dBc in the respective bands, compared to −31.4 dBc and −29.8 dBc without linearisation. Cross-band intermodulation products at harmonically related frequencies are characterised and shown to remain below −55 dBc after correction. Total observation receiver resource utilisation on a Xilinx evaluation FPGA board is 34% of available DSP slices.

title: Ironic Framing in Serbian Facebook Political Memes During the 2022 Parliamentary Campaign
abstract: This study examines how irony functions as a rhetorical device in political memes shared on Serbian Facebook groups in the lead-up to the April 2022 parliamentary elections. A corpus of 1,840 image-text memes was collected from fourteen publicly accessible political discussion groups between January and April 2022 using a custom scraping script. Memes were annotated for ironic register, visual composition type, and partisan orientation. Semiotic analysis drawing on Barthes's concepts of denotation and connotation was applied to a stratified subsample of 230 memes. Results indicate that irony appears in approximately 61 percent of opposition-aligned memes but in only 22 percent of pro-government material, suggesting a structural asymmetry in rhetorical strategy. The most frequent ironic device is incongruity between superimposed text and photographic source material, particularly in memes targeting incumbent officials. The article argues that irony in this context functions less as humour and more as a distancing mechanism that allows politically risky claims to circulate with reduced accountability. Implications for the study of vernacular political communication in hybrid-regime media environments are discussed.

title: From Screenshot to Share: Tracing Meme Mutation Across TikTok and Telegram in the Serbian Online Sphere
abstract: Political memes rarely remain static as they move between platforms; their visual and textual elements are cropped, captioned, or re-contextualised in ways that alter their semiotic load. This paper tracks the cross-platform mutation of twenty-three seed memes identified on TikTok and followed through Telegram channels between March and September 2023. Each seed was selected because it had attracted more than five hundred shares in its first week of circulation. Variant versions were collected manually and through keyword monitoring, yielding 614 distinct instances. For each variant, changes in image crop, added overlays, altered captions, and metadata were recorded. Semiotic comparison of variant chains shows that decontextualisation of photographic evidence and reattachment to new political actors is the most common transformation (occurring in 38 percent of chains). A secondary pattern involves the replacement of Serbian-language captions with regional language variants, suggesting cross-border circulation into Bosnian and Croatian online communities. The findings are discussed in relation to platform affordances that shape which semiotic elements are stable and which are easily modified.

title: Vernacular Resistance and Visual Satire: Political Memes as Counterpublic Practice in Serbia
abstract: This chapter situates Serbian political meme production within theories of counterpublics and vernacular creativity, drawing on ethnographic observation of three online communities between 2022 and 2023 and forty-five semi-structured interviews with active meme creators recruited through purposive sampling. Participants ranged in age from seventeen to thirty-four and described their meme-making primarily as a form of political commentary unavailable to them through institutional channels. Analysis focuses on how creators perceive the boundary between acceptable satire and actionable defamation, and how that perception shapes their choices of visual source material, caption tone, and distribution channel. The chapter argues that meme production in this context constitutes a form of low-cost political participation that compensates for perceived closure in formal public debate. However, the chapter also documents self-censorship practices—including face blurring and deliberate ambiguity—that creators adopt in response to earlier legal threats against online commentators. The tension between expressive ambition and anticipatory self-restraint is presented as a defining feature of politically engaged meme culture in a constrained media environment.

title: Multimodal Annotation Schemes for Political Internet Memes: A Comparative Review of Existing Frameworks and a Proposal for Serbian-Language Corpora
abstract: Annotating political memes for computational or discourse-analytic research requires decisions that existing multimodal annotation schemes do not always address satisfactorily, particularly for languages with limited digital NLP resources and for cultural contexts outside Western Europe or North America. This paper reviews eight annotation schemes published between 2017 and 2023, assessing them against four criteria: handling of embedded typography, treatment of photographic versus illustrated sources, provision for irony and sarcasm marking, and suitability for morphologically rich languages. Following this review, the paper proposes a layered annotation scheme tailored to Serbian-language political memes, with four tiers covering visual composition, textual surface, rhetorical register, and estimated partisan alignment. The scheme is piloted on a test set of 320 memes drawn from the corpus described in the authors' earlier work. Inter-annotator agreement is measured using Cohen's kappa; values above 0.72 are achieved for visual and textual tiers, while the rhetorical register tier yields a lower mean of 0.58, indicating that irony marking remains a persistent challenge. The scheme and the pilot annotations are made available as an open dataset.

title: Frames of Ethnic Otherness: A Content Analysis of Three Serbian Daily Newspapers, 1999–2003
abstract: This study examines how three high-circulation Serbian daily newspapers framed ethnic minority communities in the immediate post-conflict period. Using a deductive framing protocol applied to 1,847 news items sampled across four constructed weeks per year from 1999 to 2003, the analysis identifies five dominant frames: threat, victimhood, integration, folklorisation, and legal-administrative. Threat framing declined from 41 percent of coded items in 1999 to 18 percent in 2003, while integration frames rose from 9 percent to 27 percent over the same interval. Inter-coder reliability was established using Krippendorff's alpha (α = 0.81). The findings suggest a gradual normative reorientation in editorial practice rather than a sudden shift, and they are interpreted in relation to EU accession pressure on Serbian media institutions. The article contributes a baseline dataset that has since informed follow-up reception studies.

title: Editorial Autonomy in Small-Market Television: A Comparative Study of Serbia, Montenegro, Slovenia, and Slovakia
abstract: This monograph presents findings from a four-country comparative study of editorial autonomy in small-market commercial television conducted between 2018 and 2022. Using a mixed-methods design combining the adapted editorial autonomy instrument previously developed by the lead author, 112 in-depth interviews, and content analysis of 4,800 news segments across 24 broadcasters, the study provides the most extensive comparative evidence to date on the structural determinants of editorial independence in post-communist small markets. Key findings include: Slovenia shows substantially higher autonomy scores than the other three countries, associated with stronger public service broadcasting and more diverse ownership; Serbia and Montenegro show convergent patterns of low autonomy linked to politically affiliated ownership; Slovakia occupies an intermediate position. The monograph develops an explanatory model in which regulatory capacity, ownership diversity, and labour market conditions interact to produce distinct autonomy regimes, and concludes with policy recommendations for the Western Balkan media reform agenda.

title: Boundary-Scan Test Development for Safety-Relevant Automotive ECUs: A Process Description and Lessons Learned
abstract: This book chapter documents the practical process of developing boundary-scan test programmes for engine control units that must comply with ISO 26262 ASIL-B requirements. It covers the workflow from netlist import through BSDL file validation, cluster-based test step generation, and diagnostic coverage estimation. Particular attention is given to conflicts between scan-clock frequency requirements and EMC constraints on automotive boards, and to the documentation artefacts required for functional safety audits. The chapter draws on experience from three development cycles carried out in collaboration with a regional electronics manufacturer over four years. Quantitative data are provided on coverage achieved, defect escapes observed during pilot production, and rework costs attributed to test-strategy decisions. The chapter concludes with a checklist of 22 items for teams beginning boundary-scan development on safety-relevant ECUs.

title: Long-term performance of foam-in-place gaskets in outdoor electrical cabinets: a comparative study with die-cut EPDM
abstract: Foam-in-place (FIP) polyurethane gaskets applied to twelve sheet-metal electrical cabinet covers were compared with die-cut EPDM strips on twelve matched cabinets over a 36-month outdoor exposure period in a semi-urban environment near Novi Sad. Both cabinet populations were inspected every six months for visual defects, and sample gaskets were removed annually for laboratory compression-set and Shore A testing. FIP gaskets maintained lower compression-set values (mean 17 % at 36 months) compared with EPDM strips (mean 29 %), and showed less dimensional variability across the bead cross-section. However, four FIP samples exhibited adhesion loss at corners after 24 months when substrate surface preparation was below the specified cleanliness grade. Internal humidity loggers showed that cabinets with FIP gaskets experienced 11 % fewer condensation events over the monitoring period. Cost-benefit analysis incorporating material, application labour, and seal replacement is also presented.

title: Multivariate statistical process control applied to solid dosage film-coating: a review of methods and industrial case studies
abstract: This book chapter surveys the application of multivariate statistical process control (MSPC) to film-coating unit operations in solid dosage manufacturing, covering the period 2000–2015. Methods reviewed include PCA-based monitoring charts, partial least squares discriminant analysis for batch end-point determination, and multi-way PCA for batch trajectory analysis. Industrial case studies drawn from the peer-reviewed literature are categorised by coating type (aqueous, organic solvent, hot-melt), equipment scale (laboratory to production), and the source of process data (online sensors, at-line spectroscopy, or historian process variables). The chapter discusses practical implementation challenges including the choice of reference batch set size, time-alignment of batch trajectories with dynamic time warping, and the interpretability of latent variable models for operators unfamiliar with multivariate methods. Gaps identified include limited published data on scale-up transitions and on coatings applied to non-spherical substrates.

title: Comparison of D-optimal and full factorial designs for characterising the effect of pan coating process variables on tablet weight gain variability
abstract: Weight gain variability across individual tablets is a critical quality attribute in film coating, yet the relative efficiency of different experimental designs for characterising its dependence on process parameters has received limited systematic attention. This study compared a 2⁴ full factorial design (16 runs) with a D-optimal design (12 runs) constructed in the same four-factor space—inlet air temperature (45–65 °C), pan speed (8–16 rpm), spray rate (6–14 g/min), and coating suspension solids content (10–20% w/w)—for aqueous HPMC coating of 300 mg placebo tablets in a 15-litre pan coater. Weight gain relative standard deviation (RSD) across 20 tablets per batch end-point was the response. Prediction variance maps and model coefficient confidence intervals from both designs were compared. The D-optimal design recovered 94% of the prediction accuracy of the full factorial at 75% of the experimental effort. Pan speed and spray rate showed the largest main effects on RSD (p < 0.01), and their interaction term was statistically significant in both designs.

title: Raman spectroscopy for in-line coating thickness estimation on film-coated tablets: calibration strategy and prediction uncertainty
abstract: In-line Raman spectroscopy was investigated as a non-destructive method for estimating mean coating thickness on film-coated 400 mg ibuprofen tablets during aqueous ethylcellulose coating in a side-vented pan coater at the 6-litre scale. Spectra were collected every 60 seconds using a PharmaScan PB-2 immersion probe (invented instrument). A PLS calibration model was trained on 220 spectra from 11 reference batches spanning coating thickness values of 30–180 µm (confirmed by cross-sectional optical microscopy on pulled samples). The RMSECV for coating thickness was 8.3 µm on a leave-one-batch-out cross-validation scheme. Prediction uncertainty was decomposed into contributions from model error, spectral noise, and batch-to-batch variability using a Monte Carlo resampling approach (5000 iterations). Results indicated that batch-to-batch variability in tablet core composition accounted for 38% of total prediction uncertainty, suggesting that incorporating core spectral pre-processing could further improve model robustness across manufacturing campaigns.

title: Batch trajectory analysis with multi-way PCA for monitoring scale-dependent coating dynamics in side-vented pan coaters
abstract: Scale-up of film-coating processes often introduces changes in batch trajectory shape that invalidate monitoring models built at smaller scale. This study applied multi-way principal component analysis (MPCA) to batch process data from aqueous HPMC coating runs conducted at three pan scales: 6-litre (n = 14 batches), 30-litre (n = 11 batches), and 120-litre (n = 9 batches). Time-alignment across batches was performed using indicator variable synchronisation based on cumulative spray volume. Five process variables were monitored per run. Score trajectories on PC1–PC2 showed systematic between-scale shifts attributable primarily to differences in exhaust air humidity dynamics, confirmed by contribution plots. A two-step monitoring strategy was proposed in which a scale-specific MPCA model is used for real-time fault detection and a cross-scale PLS model is used for end-point prediction. Cross-validated root mean square errors for weight gain prediction at the 120-litre scale were 0.43% using the cross-scale model, compared to 1.12% when the 6-litre model was applied directly.

title: Central composite design study of fluidised-bed coating variables affecting particle size distribution and friability of coated microcrystalline cellulose beads
abstract: A face-centred central composite design was used to investigate the effects of four process variables—inlet air temperature (40–60 °C), fluidisation air volume (30–50 m³/h), spray rate (3–9 g/min), and atomisation air pressure (1.2–2.0 bar)—on particle size distribution (d10, d50, d90, span) and friability of aqueous Eudragit RS 30D-coated microcrystalline cellulose beads at 10% weight gain in a 3-litre Glatt GPCG-1. Twenty-six experimental runs were conducted; responses were measured in triplicate. Quadratic regression models for d50 and span showed R² values of 0.91 and 0.87 respectively. Inlet air temperature and atomisation pressure had the strongest influence on span (p < 0.001), suggesting that droplet evaporation rate relative to deposition rate governs size distribution broadening. Friability was below 0.5% in all runs except two with low inlet temperature and high spray rate, where visible agglomeration increased friability to 1.8–2.3%. Overlay plots identified a feasible operating region satisfying all acceptance criteria simultaneously.

title: Sensitivity of coating end-point detection to reference batch selection in multivariate batch monitoring: a simulation study
abstract: The performance of multivariate batch monitoring models for coating end-point detection depends critically on the quality and representativeness of the reference batch set, yet systematic guidance on reference batch selection is lacking. This simulation study generated synthetic coating batch trajectories by perturbing a mechanistic spray-coating model with realistic noise distributions estimated from 26 historical production batches of aqueous HPMC-coated tablets at the 30-litre scale. MPCA monitoring models were built from reference sets of varying size (n = 5, 10, 15, 20 batches) and composition (random selection versus diversity-maximised selection using maximum dissimilarity). End-point detection sensitivity and false alarm rate were evaluated over 200 simulated test batches per condition. Models built from diversity-maximised sets of 10–15 batches achieved comparable performance to randomly selected sets of 20 batches (sensitivity 91% vs. 89%, false alarm rate 5.1% vs. 5.4% at 95% confidence). Models built from fewer than eight reference batches showed markedly degraded sensitivity (below 75%). Practical recommendations for reference batch selection in routine coating operations are provided.

title: Reliability and Temporal Stability of Competency Self-Assessments Among Production Workers
abstract: Self-assessment instruments are frequently used in competency frameworks as a low-cost data collection mechanism, but their reliability properties in production worker populations have received limited empirical attention. This study investigates test-retest reliability and parallel-form reliability of a 48-item competency self-assessment instrument administered at two food-processing plants and one rubber goods plant in Serbia. A total of 191 operators completed the instrument at baseline and again after a 6-week interval under stable working conditions. A parallel form was administered to a subsample of 87 participants. Test-retest intraclass correlation coefficients ranged from 0.61 to 0.86 across nine competency scales; scales related to interpersonal and communication competencies showed lower stability than technical and procedural scales. Parallel-form correlation averaged 0.71. Participants with lower educational attainment showed higher within-person variability at retest. The findings argue for supervisor-corroborated rather than standalone self-assessment designs in formal grading or development decisions.

title: Mapping the Stribeck Curve of Industrial Gear Oils Using a Mini-Traction Machine: Influence of Base-Stock Type and Antiwear Additive Package
abstract: The Stribeck curve was measured for six gear oil formulations—two PAO, two ester, and two PAG base stocks, each with and without a zinc-free antiwear additive package—using a mini-traction machine (MTM) with a 19 mm diameter AISI 52100 steel ball on a flat disc. Tests were run at a constant Hertzian pressure of 1.0 GPa over an entrainment speed range of 0.002 to 3.0 m·s⁻¹ at a slide-to-roll ratio of 50%, at 60 and 100 °C. The mixed-to-boundary transition (lambda = 1) entrainment speed shifted from 0.08 m·s⁻¹ (PAO) to 0.21 m·s⁻¹ (PAG) at 100 °C, consistent with PAG's lower pressure–viscosity coefficient. In the boundary regime, friction coefficients ranged from 0.055 to 0.098; ester-based formulations with the antiwear additive package showed the lowest boundary friction across both temperatures. SLIM imaging confirmed tribofilm formation in the mixed and boundary regimes for all additive-containing blends, with film patch coverage reaching 60–80% of the contact area. The results provide a comparative dataset for gear-oil selection in low-speed, high-load applications.

title: Transit Deserts in Polycentric Mid-Size Cities: Definition and Identification Criteria
abstract: The concept of a transit desert, developed primarily for North American metropolitan areas, is adapted here for the conditions of polycentric mid-size European cities with populations between 100,000 and 500,000. The paper proposes a composite index combining three dimensions: (1) maximum walking time to the nearest stop with at least four departures per hour in peak periods, (2) ratio of transit travel time to car travel time for the ten nearest employment centres, and (3) share of car-dependent households in the census tract. The index is tested on Novi Sad using 2011 census microdata and a reconstructed GTFS feed. Fourteen census tracts out of 118 are classified as transit deserts under the proposed threshold. The paper discusses the limitations of applying North American desert typologies to cities where historical urban form is more compact and car ownership rates have risen rapidly only since the 1990s.

title: Accessibility to Healthcare by Public Transport in Vojvodina: A Multi-City Panel Study
abstract: This chapter contributes a case study of Vojvodina to a comparative volume on healthcare accessibility in post-socialist Central and Eastern Europe. Using GTFS feeds for seven cities (Novi Sad, Subotica, Zrenjanin, Sombor, Vršac, Kikinda, Pančevo) and a point dataset of 43 general hospitals and health centres, the study computes the share of population within 45 minutes by public transport of any health facility. The analysis is repeated for 2015 and 2020 to assess change over the period. Coverage in the region declined from 69% to 63% between those years, driven by service reductions in smaller cities rather than population redistribution. The chapter also maps zones where coverage is below 40% in both years, finding that these persist predominantly in peri-urban zones of Zrenjanin and Sombor. Policy implications for rural-urban feeder services are discussed in the regional context.

title: Constructing a Longitudinal GTFS Archive for Novi Sad Public Transport, 2012–2022
abstract: Retrospective accessibility analyses are constrained by the absence of archived GTFS data in cities that adopted the format late or inconsistently. This paper describes the construction of a ten-year GTFS archive for Novi Sad covering the period 2012–2022, assembled from operator timetable booklets, city council transport committee minutes, and scanned schedule boards digitised with a semi-automated OCR workflow. Each annual feed was validated against independent sources including newspaper notices of route changes and a subset of GPS traces donated by volunteer transit riders. The archive contains 11 annual snapshots with a median of 22 routes and 614 stop records per snapshot. Validation shows stop position accuracy within 8 m on average and schedule accuracy of 94.7% at the trip level. The archive is deposited at the University of Novi Sad institutional repository and released under an open data licence. Potential uses for longitudinal accessibility, ridership, and equity research are outlined.

title: Does New Tram Infrastructure Reduce Transit Deserts? A Pre–Post Study of the Subotica Light Rail Extension
abstract: A 4.2 km light rail extension opened in Subotica in late 2022, linking the city centre to two outer residential neighbourhoods built between 2005 and 2015. This study applies the transit desert index developed in earlier work (Đorđević & Stojanović, 2017) to Subotica census tracts before (June 2022) and after (June 2023) the extension, using GTFS feeds from both periods and 2021 census population data. The number of census tracts classified as transit deserts fell from nine to five. However, three of the four reclassified tracts had above-median car ownership, suggesting the new line primarily serves residents with transport alternatives already available. Two tracts with below-median car ownership in the western periphery remain classified as deserts. The paper argues that rail extensions in mid-size cities are not sufficient on their own to address transit desert problems without complementary bus feeder improvements.

title: Sensitivity of Transit Accessibility Metrics to GTFS Feed Quality: A Simulation-Based Assessment
abstract: GTFS feeds from smaller operators frequently contain errors: missing stop coordinates, incorrect trip sequences, or mismatched calendar entries. This paper quantifies how such errors propagate into accessibility metrics by introducing controlled perturbations into a validated Novi Sad GTFS feed and recomputing 30-minute isochrone areas for 120 origin points. Six error types are tested: stop displacement (10–200 m), schedule offset (1–10 min), missing trips (1–20% randomly removed), duplicated trips, incorrect shape references, and calendar boundary errors. Missing trips have the largest effect, reducing computed accessible population by up to 22% when 15% of trips are absent. Stop displacement errors below 50 m have negligible effect on area metrics but can cause misclassification of individual stops near network edges. The findings provide practical guidance for researchers deciding whether to pre-clean feeds before analysis and suggest minimum quality thresholds for comparative studies.

title: Personalised Pricing and GDPR Constraints: Revenue Management Implications for European Hotels
abstract: Personalised pricing—setting individual rates based on inferred consumer willingness to pay—offers revenue managers potentially large gains but conflicts with European data protection rules under the GDPR. This paper develops a formal model of constrained personalised pricing in which the hotel revenue manager maximises expected revenue subject to a data minimisation constraint that limits the number of consumer attributes usable in rate discrimination. The model is parameterised using conjoint survey data from 502 hotel guests in four countries (Serbia, Hungary, Romania, Austria) and solved numerically. Results show that even a two-attribute rate model (trip purpose, booking channel) recovers 61% of the theoretical full-information revenue gain, while satisfying a plausible interpretation of GDPR data minimisation. The study offers a practical framework that legal and revenue management departments can use jointly to design compliant personalisation strategies.

title: Competitive Price Monitoring via Web Scraping: Accuracy, Latency, and Ethical Boundaries for Revenue Managers
abstract: Automated competitive rate monitoring has become a standard component of hotel revenue management, yet the quality of scraped data and the ethical limits of scraping practice receive limited systematic attention in the hospitality literature. This paper conducts a controlled accuracy audit in which rates retrieved by a purpose-built scraping prototype are compared to rates confirmed through direct booking for 48 hotels in Novi Sad, Subotica, and Szeged over a 90-day window totalling 12,960 rate observations. Scraping latency—the delay between a price change and its detection—averages 4.2 hours across the sample, with tails exceeding 18 hours for properties using client-side rendering. Data accuracy is 94.7% at the headline rate level but falls to 81.3% when tax-inclusive rates are required. The paper also reviews applicable terms-of-service restrictions and Serbian and EU legal precedents relevant to automated data collection, providing a compliance checklist for revenue management practitioners.

title: Cramér-Rao Bounds for Compressive Delay-Doppler Estimation Under Structured Pilot Patterns in OFDM V2X
abstract: This paper derives analytical Cramér-Rao lower bounds (CRLB) for the joint estimation of delay, Doppler shift, and complex amplitude of individual multipath components from compressively observed OFDM pilot grids in V2X channels. The signal model accounts for inter-carrier interference arising from high mobility, treats the pilot selection matrix as a deterministic parameter, and assumes a Gaussian noise model. Closed-form expressions for the Fisher information matrix are derived for the single-component case and extended numerically to up to ten components. The resulting bounds are evaluated for pilot densities from 10 % to 50 % of the full grid and for vehicle speeds of 30, 90, and 140 km/h. Results show that the delay CRLB is largely insensitive to pilot density above 20 % while the Doppler CRLB degrades sharply below 15 %. The bounds are compared against the empirical performance of three published estimators—OMP, BSBL, and ANM—using Monte Carlo trials, and the gap to the bound at practical SNR (5–25 dB) is quantified.

title: 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing reveals diet-driven shifts in core rumen microbiome taxa of prepubertal dairy heifers fed DDGS
abstract: The rumen microbiome of prepubertal Holstein heifers (n = 24, aged 4–6 months) was profiled by Illumina MiSeq sequencing of the V4 region of the 16S rRNA gene. Animals were assigned to three dietary groups: control (0% DDGS), low DDGS (12% DM), and high DDGS (24% DM) for 90 days. After quality filtering, a mean of 43,200 reads per sample were obtained and clustered into amplicon sequence variants (ASVs). At the phylum level, Bacteroidota and Bacillota dominated across all groups. The high DDGS group showed a significantly lower Bacillota:Bacteroidota ratio (1.31 vs. 1.67 in control, P = 0.03). At the genus level, relative abundance of Prevotella was higher in the high DDGS group (+4.2 percentage points, P = 0.01), while Ruminococcus was lower (−2.1 percentage points, P = 0.04). Alpha diversity metrics (Chao1, Faith PD) did not differ between groups. The study provides sequence-level evidence that moderate DDGS inclusion selectively modulates fibre-degrading and propionate-producing taxa.

title: Methane output and rumen fermentation parameters in heifers fed corn versus wheat DDGS at equal inclusion rates
abstract: Corn and wheat DDGS differ in fibre and sulphur content, yet their comparative effects on enteric methane emissions in young dairy stock have rarely been measured under the same experimental conditions. Twenty-four Holstein heifers (10 months) were allocated to three groups: control, 18% corn DDGS, or 18% wheat DDGS on a DM basis. After a 21-day adaptation period, methane output was estimated over four days using the SF6 tracer gas technique. Rumen fluid was sampled by oro-ruminal probe for VFA, pH, and ammonia nitrogen on days 21 and 42. Mean methane emission per kg DM intake was 21.3 g (control), 18.9 g (corn DDGS), and 20.1 g (wheat DDGS). The corn DDGS group emitted significantly less methane per kg DM intake (P = 0.04). Acetate-to-propionate ratio was lower in the corn DDGS group (2.8 vs. 3.3, P = 0.02). Wheat DDGS showed intermediate effects. These differences align with differences in rumen fibre degradability between the two co-product types.

title: Association between rumen microbiome composition at weaning and subsequent growth performance in heifers transitioned to DDGS-containing rations
abstract: Early microbial colonisation of the rumen may predispose calves to better or worse adaptation to fermentable feed co-products later in life. This prospective cohort study followed 36 Holstein heifer calves from weaning (age 10 weeks) through 6 months of age. At weaning, rumen microbiome profiles were obtained via oro-pharyngeal swab and 16S rRNA sequencing. At 14 weeks, animals were gradually transitioned to a ration containing 18% corn DDGS. Body weight, average daily gain, and rumen pH were recorded monthly. Hierarchical clustering of weaning-time microbiome profiles identified two distinct clusters differing in Fibrobacter and Butyrivibrio abundances. Animals in the Fibrobacter-enriched cluster showed a higher average daily gain over the trial period (0.88 vs. 0.79 kg/day, P = 0.03) and maintained a more stable rumen pH after DDGS introduction. The results suggest that weaning-time rumen microbiome composition partially predicts adaptability to DDGS-supplemented rations, though the mechanisms require further investigation.

title: Explaining credit decisions to supervisors: a case study
abstract: Regulatory frameworks across the European Union increasingly require financial institutions to provide meaningful explanations of automated credit decisions, yet operationalising this requirement for complex statistical models remains an open challenge for both banks and their supervisors. This paper presents a case study conducted with a mid-sized bank operating in the Western Balkans, examining how SHAP-based and LIME-based explanation methods can be adapted to produce supervisor-readable model documentation. Through structured interviews with six risk officers and two national regulatory examiners, we identify a systematic gap between the granularity of machine-generated explanations and the narrative format expected by supervisory review teams. We propose a three-layer explanation architecture that separates model-level, portfolio-level, and individual-decision-level outputs, mapping each layer to a specific supervisory use case. A prototype implementation demonstrated that the middle portfolio layer, summarising feature contribution distributions across loan cohorts, received the highest usability ratings from regulatory staff. The findings have direct implications for banks seeking validation of internal models under the European Banking Authority's upcoming guidelines on model risk management and for vendors developing regulatory technology solutions in credit risk.

title: Alternative data in consumer credit scoring: evidence from a Serbian fintech lender
abstract: The proliferation of digital footprints has opened new possibilities for consumer credit assessment, particularly for individuals excluded from the traditional banking system. This study analyses a proprietary dataset of 12,400 loan applications processed by a Serbian fintech lender between 2019 and 2021, of which approximately 38 percent belong to borrowers with no prior bank credit record. We evaluate the incremental predictive lift obtained by appending seven categories of alternative data—including e-commerce transaction patterns, mobile recharge frequency, social network activity proxies, and geolocation stability—to a baseline logistic regression model trained solely on bureau data. Incremental AUC improvements range from 3.2 to 8.7 percentage points depending on the borrower segment, with the largest gains concentrated among self-employed individuals aged 25 to 40. Random forest and XGBoost models are also evaluated; XGBoost achieves the highest overall AUC of 0.81 on the holdout set. We further examine fairness metrics across gender and regional subgroups, finding no statistically significant disparate impact when SHAP-constrained feature selection is applied. Regulatory implications under the General Data Protection Regulation and the forthcoming EU Artificial Intelligence Act are discussed, with emphasis on consent management and the right to explanation.

title: Regulatory capital implications of machine learning credit models: a stress-testing perspective
abstract: Machine learning models now underpin a growing share of internal ratings-based credit risk systems at European banks, yet their behaviour under macroeconomic stress remains poorly understood. This paper examines how gradient-boosted and neural-network-based probability-of-default models respond to simulated recessionary shocks compared with traditional logistic regression scorecards, using a panel of SME loan portfolios from five Western Balkan banks spanning 2010 to 2022. We construct three stress scenarios calibrated to the 2008–2009 financial crisis, the 2020 pandemic shock, and a hypothetical sovereign debt episode, and we measure through-the-cycle versus point-in-time PD migration for each model class. Results indicate that complex models exhibit higher rank-order stability but produce more severe PD spikes under tail scenarios, potentially amplifying procyclicality in Pillar 1 capital requirements. We propose a model blending strategy that preserves discriminatory power in normal conditions while dampening stress-period volatility. The paper also evaluates how supervisory overlays recommended by the European Banking Authority interact with machine learning outputs, offering guidance for banks preparing internal model validation documentation.

title: Credit access barriers for women-owned SMEs in the Western Balkans
abstract: Gender disparities in small business credit access have been documented in developed economies, but evidence from transition markets in the Western Balkans remains scarce. This paper draws on a survey of 870 SME owners across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia, combined with administrative loan outcome data obtained from three partner banks, to quantify the magnitude of gender-based credit gaps and identify their structural drivers. Decomposition analysis following the Blinder–Oaxaca method reveals that roughly 60 percent of the observed approval rate gap between male-owned and female-owned firms is attributable to differences in collateral endowments rather than business performance metrics, suggesting that collateral requirements serve as a structural barrier rather than a neutral risk-management instrument. We find that firms scoring above the median on a cash-flow-based alternative scorecard have near-identical default rates regardless of owner gender, supporting the case for collateral-light lending products targeted at women entrepreneurs. Policy recommendations address both regulatory incentives for banks and technical assistance programmes funded through EU pre-accession instruments. The paper contributes to the growing literature on inclusive finance and SME credit rationing.
