title: Explainability requirements under the EU AI Act: implications for credit scoring vendors
abstract: The EU Artificial Intelligence Act classifies credit scoring systems as high-risk AI applications, imposing stringent transparency and human oversight obligations on both developers and deployers. This paper systematically maps those obligations onto the technical architecture of contemporary scoring platforms, focusing on three widely adopted model families: gradient-boosted trees, neural networks, and scorecard ensembles. We identify eight distinct explainability requirements arising from the Act's Articles 13 and 14 and evaluate the degree to which current post-hoc explanation libraries—SHAP, LIME, DiCE, and Anchors—satisfy each requirement as interpreted by draft guidance from the European AI Office. Our analysis finds that no single library fully addresses all eight requirements and that the most underserved dimension is contrastive explanation for portfolio-level supervisory reporting. We propose a modular explanation stack architecture for credit vendors that combines global surrogate models, individual SHAP waterfalls, and counterfactual generators within a unified audit trail. Case studies drawn from two anonymised Serbian fintech deployments illustrate the practical implementation challenges. The paper has implications for regulatory technology firms developing compliance tooling and for banks seeking to achieve AI Act conformity assessments before the 2026 deadline.

title: Incorporating cash-flow volatility into SME credit scoring: a machine learning approach
abstract: Traditional SME credit scoring models rely heavily on balance-sheet snapshots that fail to capture the temporal dynamics of business cash flows. This paper proposes a scoring methodology that extracts volatility and trend features from monthly bank transaction records spanning at least twelve months, feeding these time-series features into a stacked ensemble model alongside conventional financial ratios and owner characteristics. The dataset comprises transaction histories and twelve-month loan outcomes for 6,200 Serbian SMEs obtained from a commercial bank under a data-sharing agreement. Feature engineering steps include rolling standard deviation of net cash flow, seasonal decomposition residuals, and autocorrelation-based regularity scores. The stacked ensemble combines a long short-term memory network for sequence features with gradient-boosted trees for tabular features, achieving an AUC of 0.83 on the holdout set compared with 0.74 for a bureau-only logistic regression baseline. SHAP values confirm that cash-flow regularity score and the ratio of peak-to-trough monthly receipts are among the top five predictors. The paper also discusses data governance considerations, including minimum transaction history requirements and the treatment of COVID-19 payment moratoria as structural breaks in the time series.

title: Open banking data for thin-file borrower assessment: opportunities and regulatory constraints
abstract: Open banking frameworks established under the revised Payment Services Directive have created legal pathways for lenders to access enriched transaction data with borrower consent, offering a potential solution to the thin-file problem that affects an estimated 30 percent of adult borrowers in Serbia and neighbouring markets. This book chapter reviews the current state of open banking adoption in the Western Balkans, evaluates the credit information value of Payment Initiation Service Provider and Account Information Service Provider data streams, and discusses the regulatory constraints that limit their use in automated scoring. Drawing on pilot studies conducted with two regional banks and one licensed fintech lender, we present empirical evidence that open banking features improve AUC by 6 to 11 percentage points for borrowers with fewer than two years of credit bureau history. The chapter also examines tensions between the General Data Protection Regulation's data minimisation principle and the feature richness required for accurate thin-file scoring, proposing a privacy-preserving feature aggregation protocol as a practical reconciliation. The chapter concludes with a framework for national regulators considering mandatory open banking data standards as a tool for financial inclusion.

title: Benchmarking scorecard interpretability metrics in credit risk practice
abstract: The credit risk literature has converged on SHAP values as the dominant post-hoc explanation tool, yet practitioners frequently report difficulty translating SHAP outputs into actionable underwriting narratives for loan officers and borrowers. This preprint introduces a benchmarking protocol for scorecard interpretability that evaluates five dimensions: local fidelity, global coherence, counterfactual proximity, regulatory legibility, and borrower comprehensibility. We apply the protocol to six model types—logistic regression scorecard, decision tree, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and a shallow neural network—using a unified dataset of 8,500 Serbian consumer and micro-business loan applications. Logistic regression scorecards dominate on regulatory legibility and borrower comprehensibility but lag on predictive performance, confirming the classic accuracy-interpretability trade-off. XGBoost with SHAP explanation achieves the best composite interpretability-performance score under our weighting scheme, which assigns equal weight to all five dimensions. We also show that LIME explanations exhibit lower cross-run stability than SHAP for tree-based models, raising concerns about their suitability for audit documentation. The benchmarking protocol is released as an open-source Python toolkit to support reproducibility and adoption by practitioners preparing model validation dossiers under Basel IV and the EU AI Act.

title: Energy Budget Analysis for LoRaWAN End-Nodes Powered by Single Primary Cells: Field Measurements from a Flood-Warning Network
abstract: This paper reports measured energy consumption data from 18 LoRaWAN end-nodes deployed along the Tisa river basin for flood-level monitoring over a 20-month period. Each node is powered by a single AA-size Li/MnO₂ cell. Current waveforms were logged at 1 ms resolution using a shunt-based data logger co-located on the PCB. The study decomposes total energy into four phases: sensor acquisition (7 %), radio transmission (61 %), idle sleep (29 %), and microcontroller housekeeping (3 %). Radio transmission current peaks ranged from 38 mA to 124 mA depending on spreading factor. An empirical energy model calibrated on the first six months of data predicted total charge drawn over the remaining 14 months with a 4.1 % root-mean-square error. Cells in nodes with high spreading factors (SF12) showed 28 % lower delivered capacity than those using SF7, attributable to larger pulse amplitude stressing the passivation layer. These findings suggest that adaptive data-rate policies can meaningfully extend primary-cell lifetime in flood-monitoring deployments.

title: Effect of Duty Cycle and Inter-Pulse Interval on Voltage Recovery in Li/SOCl₂ Cells: Systematic Bench Tests
abstract: Voltage recovery after a current pulse is critical for reliable data transmission in intermittent wireless devices. This work examines how duty cycle (1 %–20 %) and inter-pulse interval (0.5 s–60 s) affect voltage recovery time and recovered terminal voltage in Li/SOCl₂ cells at three states of discharge (fresh, 50 % depleted, 80 % depleted). Tests were conducted on 45 cells across five lots from three manufacturers. Voltage recovery curves were fitted with a biexponential function; time constants τ₁ (fast, 0.1–0.9 s) and τ₂ (slow, 4–35 s) were extracted. τ₂ increases by a factor of 3.1 between fresh and 80 %-depleted states. At 20 % duty cycle and 0.5 s inter-pulse interval, recovered voltage at 80 % depletion falls 140 mV below the fresh-cell baseline—sufficient to cause transmission failure on 3.0 V-threshold radio modules. A simple lookup table parametrised on state-of-discharge and inter-pulse interval is proposed as a lightweight pre-transmission voltage check implementable on a Cortex-M0.

title: Low-Power Embedded Energy Meters for In-Situ Primary Cell Characterisation on Deployed Sensor Nodes
abstract: Characterising primary cells in situ on deployed sensor nodes is difficult because measurement hardware must not significantly perturb node energy consumption. This paper describes the design and validation of an embedded energy meter that draws under 9 µA average current from the measured cell and logs voltage, temperature, and accumulated charge to on-board flash at configurable intervals down to 100 ms. The meter uses a 24-bit sigma-delta ADC, a precision 10 mΩ current-sense resistor, and a Cortex-M0+ microcontroller in deep-sleep mode between samples. Calibration against a laboratory Keithley 2450 source-measure unit shows a current measurement error below 0.4 % over 0.1 mA–200 mA. The meter was validated on 12 nodes installed in a grain-silo humidity monitoring network. In-situ capacity estimates derived from logged data agreed with post-deployment laboratory capacity tests to within 3.8 % RMS. Board gerbers and firmware are published in an open repository.

title: Temperature-Dependent Capacity Loss in Primary Lithium Cells: Separating Passivation and Electrolyte Conductivity Contributions via Frequency-Resolved Impedance
abstract: At sub-zero temperatures, primary lithium cells lose usable capacity through two overlapping mechanisms: increased passivation-layer resistance and reduced electrolyte ionic conductivity. Disentangling these contributions is necessary for accurate cold-temperature lifetime models. This study applies distribution-of-relaxation-times (DRT) analysis to impedance spectra collected at nine temperatures between −20 °C and +45 °C on 36 Li/SOCl₂ cells at four states of discharge. DRT peaks are assigned to passivation, charge-transfer, and electrolyte processes using supporting DC polarisation data. The passivation contribution dominates the impedance increase below −5 °C, accounting for 68 % of total resistance rise at −20 °C, while the electrolyte contribution is dominant above +10 °C. An additive model combining both temperature functions fits the measured capacity-delivered data with an adjusted R² of 0.94 across all conditions. Implications for sensor-node deployment in unheated outdoor enclosures are discussed with reference to three case-study climatic zones in the western Balkans.

title: Integrating Real-Time Traffic Data into Rolling-Horizon Bus Scheduling: A Case Study from Novi Sad
abstract: Planned bus schedules assume fixed travel times that diverge from reality during peak hours and incidents. This paper describes a system that feeds real-time GPS and loop-detector traffic data into a rolling-horizon scheduler operating on a 20-minute receding horizon, re-solving sub-problems every 5 minutes. The system was piloted on four bus lines in Novi Sad over a 6-week period in 2022 using historical data replay. Updated travel time estimates were obtained from a gradient-boosted regression model trained on 11 months of GPS traces. Compared to a static daily schedule, the rolling-horizon system reduced total accumulated delay by 18% and reduced the number of trips arriving more than 3 minutes late by 22%. Practical challenges encountered during deployment—data latency, GPS dropouts, and dispatcher override frequency—are documented. The paper concludes with a discussion of the gap between research prototype and operational deployment.

title: Comparison of D-type and Gradient-Descent ILC Algorithms on a Flexible-Transmission Gantry with Varying Friction
abstract: Friction in linear guideways of Cartesian gantry systems is not constant: it varies with velocity, temperature, and lubrication state over a working shift. This study compares the sensitivity of derivative-type (D-type) and gradient-descent ILC to such friction variations. A horizontal single-axis gantry was operated over a four-hour session during which guideway friction torque was estimated online using a disturbance observer. Friction varied between 1.8 N and 4.4 N over the session. D-type ILC showed steady-state RMS errors that increased from 0.027 mm at the start to 0.061 mm after two hours before a re-initialisation was needed. The gradient-descent variant, which re-estimates the system Markov parameters every 20 trials, maintained errors below 0.033 mm throughout. Computational overhead of the online identification step was 1.4 ms per sample on a 1 kHz control loop, compatible with real-time implementation on the dSPACE DS1007 target used in the experiment.

title: Transferability of thermal error models between kinematically identical robots in the same production cell
abstract: Industrial production cells often contain multiple copies of the same robot model. Identifying a full thermal error model for each unit is time-consuming. This study investigates how much of the thermal error model identified on a source robot can be transferred to a target robot of the same model without re-identification. Four nominally identical six-axis robots from the same manufacturing batch were instrumented and characterised individually. The source model, transferred without modification, achieved an RMS TCP error of 0.19 mm on the three target robots, compared with 0.09 mm for individually identified models. A lightweight adaptation procedure requiring only 60 measurement epochs per robot reduced the transferred model error to 0.11 mm, retaining 78% of the accuracy benefit of full identification at roughly 10% of the measurement effort. The adaptation exploits the fact that inter-unit geometric variation is small while thermal expansion coefficients differ by up to 8% due to manufacturing tolerances in harmonic drive assemblies. The method is directly applicable to multi-robot welding and assembly lines.

title: Combining structured-light scanning and kinematic recalibration for volumetric accuracy verification of robot-based machining cells
abstract: Robot-based machining relies on positional accuracy exceeding what standard factory calibration provides, particularly for aluminium aerospace components where dimensional tolerances are below 0.2 mm. This preprint presents a workflow in which a structured-light scanner mounted on an external tripod measures the workpiece after each machining pass and feeds dimensional deviations back to the recalibration module to update joint offset corrections before the next pass. The scanner, a Fotomess SL-300 with a stated point accuracy of 0.05 mm, was used on aluminium test pieces with pocket features milled by a six-axis robot. Over 20 parts, the mean dimensional deviation from nominal was reduced from 0.31 mm with static calibration to 0.12 mm with closed-loop recalibration. Cycle time overhead introduced by the scanning step averaged 47 seconds per pass for the test geometry. The paper discusses conditions under which the overhead is acceptable and identifies fixture drift as the remaining dominant error source at 0.06 mm.

title: Identification of Nonlinear Rope-Tension Characteristics in Bridge Cranes Using Stepped-Sine Excitation
abstract: Rope tension in bridge cranes exhibits amplitude-dependent stiffness due to wire lay geometry and inter-strand friction. This paper applies a stepped-sine excitation protocol to characterise this nonlinearity on a full-scale 5-tonne bridge crane at a metal fabrication facility. Excitation frequencies are swept from 0.2 Hz to 4 Hz in 0.05 Hz steps at three payload levels (500 kg, 1 500 kg, and 3 000 kg). Tension is measured by a calibrated shackle-type load cell with 0.1% full-scale accuracy. Backbone curves extracted from the frequency responses show effective stiffness varying by 18% between low-amplitude (below 5 mm rope displacement) and high-amplitude (above 20 mm) regimes. A Duffing-type single-degree-of-freedom model is fitted via nonlinear least squares, achieving a relative fit error below 4% across all load levels. The identified parameters provide a physically interpretable basis for model updating in digital twin frameworks.

title: Pouzdanost strukturisane psihodinamske formulacije kod adolescenata: primena PKODNI na uzorku adolescentnih pacijenata psihijatrijske dnevne bolnice
abstract: Studija je ispitivala da li je Priručnik za kodiranje odbrambenih mehanizama u narativnim intervjuima (PKODNI), razvijen prvobitno za odraslu populaciju, pouzdan i validan pri primeni na adolescentnom kliničkom uzorku. Uzorkom je obuhvaćeno 56 adolescenata (uzrast 14–18 godina) koji su bili na tretmanu u dnevnoj bolnici psihijatrije Kliničkog centra Vojvodine. Dva procenjivača kodirala su polustrukturisane intervjue uz korekciju priručnika za razvojne norme. Inter-rater agreement merena ICC-om iznosila je prosečno 0.63 (raspon 0.47–0.76), što je neznatno niže nego u odraslim uzorcima. Najniža saglasnost utvrđena je za kodiranje sublimacije i humor odbrana, što autori dovode u vezu sa razvojno uslovljenom nejasnošću ekspresije ovih mehanizama u adolescenciji. Predlažu se modifikacije kodnog priručnika prilagođene razvojnom kontekstu.

title: Automated Text-Based Pre-Coding of Defence Mechanisms: Testing a Dictionary Approach Against Human Raters
abstract: This study tested whether a rule-based dictionary approach to automatic text coding could approximate human rater judgements of defence mechanism use in clinical interview transcripts. A lexical dictionary was constructed from the Psychodynamic Defence Coding Manual (PDCM), covering 22 defence mechanisms with associated linguistic markers. The dictionary was applied to 112 interview transcripts previously coded by trained human raters. Agreement between automated and human coding was evaluated using percentage agreement, Cohen's kappa, and Krippendorff's alpha. Automated coding achieved acceptable agreement for mature defences such as humour (κ = 0.61) and intellectualisation (κ = 0.58), but showed poor agreement for primitive defences such as splitting (κ = 0.27) and projective identification (κ = 0.19), which rely heavily on contextual and relational inference beyond the reach of dictionary methods. The findings delineate the boundary conditions of text-automated approaches and suggest that hybrid human-automated pipelines should focus automation on the more linguistically transparent defence categories.

title: A Rolling-Horizon Framework for Electric Bus Scheduling with Charging Constraints
abstract: Introducing electric buses into an existing fleet imposes charging constraints that couple vehicle scheduling decisions across time in a way that classical vehicle scheduling models do not capture. This paper extends the rolling-horizon decomposition framework to handle state-of-charge dynamics, modelling each sub-problem as a mixed-integer linear program with battery level as a side constraint. The framework was applied to a hypothetical electrification scenario for a city with 14 bus lines, constructed from publicly available timetable data, and tested for fleet sizes between 20 and 80 electric vehicles with three charging infrastructure configurations. Results show that a 120-minute window with 45-minute overlap balances solution quality and tractability; average deviation from a full-day MILP optimum is 3.8% with a maximum of 7.1%. The paper also quantifies the trade-off between number of installed fast chargers and deadhead mileage.

title: Sensitivity of Metaheuristic Performance to Disruption Frequency in Dynamic Vehicle Scheduling
abstract: Most computational studies of dynamic vehicle scheduling evaluate algorithms at a single disruption rate chosen for convenience. This paper systematically varies disruption frequency—measured as expected incidents per operating hour—from 0.05 to 2.0 across 480 randomly generated instances and measures the performance of three metaheuristics: reactive tabu search, ALNS, and iterated local search. Performance is evaluated on solution cost, number of unserviced trips, and computation time. The experiments show that ALNS maintains the lowest cost across the full frequency range, but its advantage over reactive tabu search diminishes above 1.2 incidents per hour, where rapid reheating in tabu search compensates for less structured neighbourhood selection. Iterated local search degrades sharply above 0.8 incidents per hour due to insufficient time for perturbation. The paper proposes a simple classifier, trained on instance features, that predicts which algorithm to deploy given an estimated disruption rate.

title: Bolt pattern and preload distribution effects on contact-pressure uniformity in rectangular enclosure covers
abstract: Six bolt-pattern configurations for a 400 mm × 300 mm rectangular polycarbonate lid with a continuous groove-mounted O-ring were analysed using finite-element analysis in a general-purpose structural solver. Lid thickness was varied at 4, 6, and 8 mm. Contact-pressure distributions along the gasket groove centreline were extracted for each configuration. Four-bolt corner patterns produced contact-pressure variation coefficients of 38–52 %, while eight-bolt perimeter patterns reduced this to 11–18 %. A lid thickness of 6 mm was found to be the best compromise: further thickening beyond 8 mm provided less than 3 % additional uniformity improvement. Physical validation used pressure-sensitive film inserted between the lid gasket and the flange on a prototype enclosure; measured pressure distributions agreed with FEA predictions within 15 % at all measurement points. Recommendations for minimum bolt count as a function of lid aspect ratio and flexural stiffness are derived.

title: Characterisation of water absorption and swelling in compressed NBR gaskets immersed in dew-cycle condensate
abstract: NBR gaskets of two hardness grades (50 and 70 Shore A) were subjected to repeated immersion in distilled water at 25 °C for 8 hours followed by drying at 60 °C for 16 hours, simulating dew-cycle condensation, for up to 90 cycles. Mass uptake, dimensional change in thickness, and compression-set were tracked after every 15 cycles. The softer 50 Shore A grade reached a water uptake plateau of 4.8 % by mass after 45 cycles, accompanied by a 1.7 % thickness increase. The 70 Shore A grade showed 2.9 % uptake and 0.9 % thickness increase. Compressive stress relaxation tests after the final cycle showed that both grades lost 22–27 % of initial contact-force capacity. Hardness measurements after cycling indicated slight softening (−3 to −5 Shore A units) for both grades. The data suggest that groove-depth tolerances should be re-evaluated when NBR seals are used in condensation-prone environments.

title: Seal groove geometry optimisation for reduced stress concentration in polymer enclosure lids under thermal expansion mismatch
abstract: The thermal expansion mismatch between glass-fibre-reinforced polyester lids and aluminium frames in outdoor enclosures was investigated using parametric FEA. Groove cross-sections of rectangular, trapezoidal, and semicircular profiles were modelled with an O-ring compressed to 15, 20, and 25 % of its free-diameter height. Temperature ranges from −30 °C to +80 °C representative of Central European outdoor conditions were applied. Maximum principal stress in the lid material at the groove root was taken as the key output. Trapezoidal grooves with 7° side-wall draft angles reduced stress concentration factors by 18–24 % relative to rectangular grooves at all compression levels. O-ring compression of 20 % was identified as optimal: the 25 % compression case produced lid-corner stresses exceeding the material fatigue limit under 10 000 thermal cycles. Guidelines for groove geometry as a function of lid material stiffness and operational temperature range are tabulated.

title: Accelerated ageing test protocol for gaskets in outdoor electromechanical enclosures: correlation with field performance data
abstract: A laboratory accelerated-ageing protocol was developed by combining UV exposure, thermal cycling, and intermittent condensation. Fourteen gasket specimens from five material families were aged under the protocol at acceleration factors estimated from Arrhenius and UV-dose equivalence principles. After 600, 1200, and 2000 protocol hours, compression-set, tensile retention, and leak-rate measurements were taken. Correlation with field data collected from 34 enclosures in service for 1–8 years showed that the protocol at 1200 h corresponded to approximately 5 field-years (R² = 0.81 for compression-set correlation, n = 34). EPDM and fluorosilicone showed the best retention of sealing performance. The protocol is structured around commercially available climate chamber equipment requiring no specialised modifications and is proposed as a candidate for inclusion in national testing guidelines for outdoor enclosure seals. Uncertainty analysis and repeatability data from three independent test runs are included.

title: Regulatory Impact Assessment as a Constraint on Agency Discretion: Evidence from Serbian Technical Rulemaking 2015–2022
abstract: Serbia introduced a formal regulatory impact assessment (RIA) obligation for sub-legislative acts in 2013, subsequently reinforced by the 2018 Public Administration Reform Strategy. This article investigates whether RIA procedures have in practice constrained the discretion of five Serbian regulatory agencies—covering energy, electronic communications, civil aviation, food safety, and environmental protection—when those agencies issue technical rules. Using a dataset of 204 technical rulebooks published between 2015 and 2022, together with the accompanying impact assessment documents where available, the study measures compliance rates, depth of quantitative analysis, and responsiveness to public consultation inputs. RIA documents were absent in 31 percent of cases and substantively thin in a further 44 percent. Agencies with more developed internal legal departments produced qualitatively better RIA documents, but no agency systematically connected impact findings to the scope of the rule ultimately adopted. The article discusses implications for constitutional oversight.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Automated Standard-Setting: Constitutional Questions for Serbian Administrative Law
abstract: Several Serbian regulatory agencies have begun using algorithmic tools to calibrate technical parameters embedded in binding rulebooks, particularly in the domains of network tariffs, emission thresholds, and product safety coefficients. This preprint explores the constitutional questions that arise when normative choices with binding legal effect are, in whole or in part, the output of automated systems rather than human deliberation. Drawing on the Serbian constitutional framework and on administrative law scholarship from Austria, the Netherlands, and the EU level, the paper identifies three distinct scenarios: fully automated parameter-setting, human-confirmed algorithmic outputs, and algorithm-informed expert discretion. It argues that the first scenario is constitutionally impermissible under the current Serbian constitutional order and that the second requires legislative authorisation specifying criteria the algorithm must apply. A preliminary doctrinal framework is offered for each scenario.

title: Temperature abuse during transport: a sensor study of fruit exports
abstract: Temperature deviations during postharvest transport — commonly termed temperature abuse — are a leading driver of premature spoilage and economic loss in the fresh fruit export sector. This study employed a network of miniaturized wireless temperature and relative humidity data loggers deployed across 18 commercial refrigerated truck consignments of Serbian berries (raspberry, blueberry, strawberry) destined for markets in Germany, Austria, and Slovenia. Sensor placement covered pallet core, pallet surface, and truck door-proximal positions to capture spatial heterogeneity. Results revealed that door-proximal positions experienced mean temperature elevations of 3.8 °C above target during loading and unloading events, with cumulative abuse time averaging 4.2 hours per journey. Principal component analysis of sensor profiles identified loading sequence and pre-cooling status as the two strongest predictors of abuse severity. Correlation analysis linked abuse incidents with elevated Botrytis incidence and firmness loss quantified at destination. The study provides a field-validated evidence base for the adoption of stricter pre-cooling protocols and improved door-management procedures, and introduces a temperature abuse index (TAI) metric applicable to cold-chain audit frameworks. Recommendations for future sensor infrastructure investment by exporters are presented.

title: Active packaging with natural antimicrobial sachets for blueberry shelf-life extension
abstract: Active packaging systems incorporating volatile antimicrobial agents derived from plant extracts represent a promising complement to conventional modified atmosphere packaging (MAP) for fresh blueberries. This study assessed the efficacy of sachets containing encapsulated thymol and carvacrol — sourced from wild thyme and oregano — integrated into clamshell packaging under a 5% O₂/15% CO₂ atmosphere at 2 °C. Blueberry quality was monitored over 18 days for firmness, total anthocyanin content, weight loss, and microbiological load (total aerobic count and Botrytis incidence). Active MAP sachets reduced total aerobic counts by 1.8 log CFU/g relative to passive MAP controls at day 12 and delayed visible mold onset by four days. Anthocyanin retention was significantly higher in active MAP treatments (p < 0.05), suggesting a secondary antioxidant protective effect. Consumer acceptability scores obtained through a 40-member sensory panel confirmed marketable quality at day 14 for saline-active MAP versus day 10 for passive MAP controls. Migration testing confirmed that thymol and carvacrol residues in fruit tissue remained below European regulatory thresholds. This work demonstrates the practical feasibility of combining MAP gas composition with natural antimicrobial active elements for export-grade blueberry packaging.

title: Integrating predictive microbiology into cold-chain digital twins for berry logistics
abstract: Digital twin frameworks — virtual replicas of physical supply chains updated by real-time sensor data — offer a new paradigm for proactive spoilage management in perishable food logistics. This paper describes the integration of validated predictive microbial growth models for Botrytis cinerea and total aerobic bacteria into a digital twin architecture developed for Serbian berry cold-chain operations. The system ingests temperature and relative humidity streams from IoT sensors placed within refrigerated transport units and storage rooms, feeding real-time inputs into a model library calibrated for raspberry, blueberry, and strawberry substrates. A graphical dashboard presents logistics managers with dynamically updated remaining shelf-life estimates and spoilage risk scores for each consignment. A 12-month pilot deployment covering four exporting companies and 240 consignments demonstrated that digital twin alerts correctly flagged 88% of consignments subsequently confirmed to exhibit elevated spoilage at destination. False-positive rates were 9%, attributed primarily to anomalous sensor placement near evaporator coils. Integration with enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems for automated re-routing decisions is discussed as a near-term development pathway. The study establishes a reproducible blueprint for deploying predictive microbiology within commercial cold-chain digital twin platforms in the Serbian fruit export sector.

title: Effect of pre-cooling rate on modified atmosphere equilibration and raspberry quality
abstract: Rapid and uniform pre-cooling of freshly harvested raspberries prior to MAP sealing is critical for establishing the target equilibrium atmosphere within packaging. This experimental study examined three pre-cooling protocols — forced-air cooling at 2 m/s, hydrocooling at 1 °C, and room cooling as control — applied to raspberry punnets subsequently sealed under a 5% O₂/15% CO₂ MAP at 2 °C storage. Headspace gas composition was monitored at 0, 6, 12, 24, and 48 hours post-sealing using an inline gas analyzer. Fruit core temperature profiles, firmness, respiration rate (CO₂ evolution), and drip loss were recorded throughout a 10-day storage trial. Forced-air cooling achieved target core temperature in 38 minutes compared to 210 minutes for room cooling, and resulted in target headspace O₂ equilibration 14 hours earlier than the room-cooled control. Faster equilibration was associated with significantly lower Botrytis incidence (p < 0.01) and superior firmness retention at day 8. Hydrocooling achieved comparable equilibration speed but introduced elevated free moisture that promoted calyx decay. The findings quantify the shelf-life benefit of investing in forced-air cooling infrastructure and inform revised pre-cooling standard operating procedures for export packers.

title: Shelf-life prediction for strawberries under fluctuating cold-chain temperatures using a stochastic modelling approach
abstract: Deterministic predictive models assume fixed temperature inputs, which rarely reflect the stochastic nature of real-world cold-chain environments. This study presents a stochastic modelling framework for predicting the remaining shelf life of fresh strawberries under realistic fluctuating temperature conditions. A Monte Carlo simulation approach was applied to propagate uncertainty in temperature distribution parameters — derived from 180 sensor-monitored consignments — through a validated secondary model for total aerobic count growth on strawberry. Output distributions of predicted shelf life were compared against observed microbiological end-point data from the same consignments. The stochastic model significantly outperformed its deterministic equivalent in capturing the spread of observed outcomes, with prediction intervals covering 91% of empirical data points. Sensitivity analysis identified mean transport temperature and frequency of door-opening events as the two variables contributing most to shelf-life variance. A simplified probabilistic shelf-life index (PSI) was derived for use by quality managers without specialist modelling expertise. The framework is applicable to other soft fruits and other pathogen or spoilage organism combinations, provided primary growth data are available. This work advances the practical deployment of quantitative risk-informed decision-making in Serbian berry export supply chains.

title: Packaging material permeability screening for MAP of mixed-berry trays
abstract: Mixed-berry trays combining raspberry, blueberry, and blackberry are commercially attractive but present packaging engineering challenges because each species has a distinct optimal modified atmosphere range and a different respiration rate at equivalent temperatures. This study evaluated 12 commercially available polymeric packaging films differing in oxygen transmission rate (OTR) and carbon dioxide transmission rate (CO₂TR) for their suitability in MAP of mixed-berry trays stored at 2 °C. Headspace equilibrium gas compositions were measured at 24-hour intervals over eight days and compared against species-specific target ranges determined from prior single-species trials. Microbiological and firmness data were collected at four-day intervals. A film with OTR of 3,800 cm³/m²/day and CO₂TR of 18,000 cm³/m²/day delivered headspace conditions within acceptable ranges for all three species simultaneously and reduced mold incidence by 55% relative to a standard polyethylene control. Finite element modelling of gas permeation through the film was used to confirm experimental headspace trends and to predict equilibrium under alternative tray fill-weight scenarios. The results provide film specification guidance for packers handling mixed-berry formats and demonstrate that a single film solution can satisfy the conflicting atmosphere requirements of co-packaged fruit species.

title: Food preservation engineering for horticultural products: packaging and cold-chain perspectives
abstract: This book chapter provides a comprehensive treatment of the engineering principles underpinning postharvest preservation of fresh horticultural products, with emphasis on modified atmosphere packaging and cold-chain management. The chapter opens with a review of the biochemical and microbiological deterioration mechanisms that govern shelf life in soft fruits, including ethylene-mediated ripening, oxidative browning, and fungal pathogen proliferation. It then develops the engineering framework for MAP system design, covering gas mass balance modelling, film permeability selection, and tray geometry effects on headspace equilibration dynamics. Cold-chain management is addressed through the lens of predictive microbiology, explaining how primary and secondary models can be linked to temperature monitoring data to generate real-time shelf-life estimates. A section on supply chain integration discusses how MAP and predictive modelling tools can be embedded in digital logistics systems. Case studies drawn from Serbian berry export operations illustrate the translation of laboratory models into operational practice, including a worked example of a forced-air pre-cooling and MAP line for a mid-sized raspberry exporter. The chapter concludes with a forward-looking discussion of emerging active packaging technologies and AI-assisted cold-chain optimisation. It is intended for graduate students and food industry engineers seeking a practically oriented reference.

title: Sensor-based remaining shelf-life labelling for berry exports: a feasibility study
abstract: Static best-before labelling does not reflect the actual quality state of perishable foods subjected to variable cold-chain conditions. This paper reports a feasibility study for implementing sensor-based dynamic remaining shelf-life (RSL) labelling on raspberry and blueberry consignments exported from Serbia. Time-temperature indicator (TTI) labels from two commercial suppliers were benchmarked against data-logger-calibrated predictive model outputs for Botrytis growth and total aerobic count across 24 simulated and 16 real export consignments. TTI colour-response kinetics were characterised at 0, 4, 8, and 12 °C and integrated into an RSL calculation algorithm using an Arrhenius-based temperature dependence model. Agreement between TTI-derived RSL and model-derived RSL was within ±1.2 days for 79% of consignments, which was deemed commercially acceptable by participating exporters. A cost–benefit analysis estimated that TTI-based RSL labelling could reduce consignment rejection rates at destination by 18–24%, yielding a positive return on investment for exporters operating above 50 tonnes per season. Regulatory and labelling compliance considerations under EU food law are discussed, along with the data requirements for formal TTI validation. The study supports the case for piloting RSL labelling in the Serbian berry export sector as part of a broader cold-chain quality assurance programme.

title: Effect of Graphene Oxide Nanoadditive Concentration on the Tribological Performance of a PAO-Based Wind-Turbine Gear Oil
abstract: Graphene oxide (GO) nanosheets were dispersed in a PAO-6 base oil at concentrations of 0.01, 0.05, 0.10, and 0.25 wt% using a combination of probe sonication and oleylamine surface functionalisation to prevent agglomeration. Dispersion stability was confirmed by dynamic light scattering over 30 days; the 0.05 wt% sample maintained a mean hydrodynamic size of 320 nm without precipitation. Tribological evaluation on a ball-on-disc rig at 1.0 GPa, 0.1 m·s⁻¹, and 60 °C showed that 0.05 wt% GO reduced the friction coefficient from 0.112 (base oil alone) to 0.081 and reduced wear volume by 43%. Concentrations above 0.10 wt% produced increased wear, attributed to agglomerate abrasion confirmed by SEM imaging of wear scars. Raman spectroscopy of the worn contact area revealed characteristic D and G bands of GO, consistent with a protective carbonaceous tribofilm. PDSC testing of the GO-containing blends confirmed no significant change in oxidative induction time relative to the base oil, indicating compatibility with the existing antioxidant package.

title: Thermal Memory Characterisation of RF Power Amplifiers Using Pulsed Measurement Techniques
abstract: Thermal memory effects in RF PAs arise from slow variations in junction temperature caused by envelope fluctuations and constitute a primary source of model inaccuracy for burst-mode and multi-carrier signals. This paper describes a pulsed measurement methodology in which a vector signal generator applies rectangular envelope pulses of 1 µs to 10 ms duration at a carrier of 1.8 GHz to a Si LDMOS device, while a synchronised vector signal analyser captures AM–AM and AM–PM characteristics as a function of pulse width and duty cycle. Thermal resistance and capacitance values extracted from the transient gain compression data match those from a separate electrothermal FEM simulation within 8%. The extracted thermal time constants range from 12 µs to 3.4 ms, confirming that conventional DPD with sample-rate memory depth cannot address the longest thermal lags. A two-path model separating electrical and thermal memory components is proposed and shown to reduce NMSE by 3.1 dB compared to a single-path GMP model at equivalent coefficient count.

title: Machine Learning-Based Behavioural Models for PA Nonlinearity: A Comparison of Feed-Forward Networks and Recurrent Architectures
abstract: This paper systematically compares feed-forward neural network (FFNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM) models as behavioural representations of a 20 W GaN PA at 2.6 GHz, driven by a 200 MHz bandwidth signal derived from aggregated 5G NR carriers. Training data consisting of 80 000 complex IQ sample pairs were collected from a calibrated vector signal analyser testbed. FFNN models with two hidden layers (32 and 16 neurons) and tap-delayed inputs of depth 5 achieved NMSE of −39.4 dB after 500 training epochs. LSTM models with a single hidden layer of 32 units trained over the same data reached −44.1 dB NMSE, at the cost of a four-fold increase in training time and greater sensitivity to learning rate selection. Both models outperform a GMP reference (order 5, depth 3) by at least 4 dB NMSE for this signal bandwidth. When used as the pre-distorter model inside an ILA framework, LSTM-based DPD achieves −49.6 dBc ACPR, 2.3 dB better than the GMP baseline. Inference latency estimates for FPGA deployment favour the FFNN for real-time operation.

title: Crest Factor Reduction Interaction Effects on Digital Pre-Distortion Performance in 5G Base Stations
abstract: Crest factor reduction (CFR) is routinely applied before DPD in 5G base station transmitters to relax PA backoff requirements, but clipping and filtering in the CFR stage alter the statistical properties of the signal and can degrade DPD convergence. This paper presents measurements on a 200 W GaN Doherty PA at 3.6 GHz using three CFR schemes — clipping-and-filtering, peak windowing, and tone reservation — each applied to a 100 MHz 5G NR signal at PAPR targets of 8, 9, and 10 dB. The DPD system uses an LSTM-based pre-distorter trained jointly with CFR parameters. Results show that tone reservation at 10 dB PAPR target preserves DPD ACPR performance within 0.4 dB of the no-CFR baseline, whereas clipping-and-filtering at 8 dB PAPR target causes ACPR degradation of 2.9 dB relative to individually optimised DPD. A joint optimisation procedure converging in fewer than 30 iterations is described, reducing ACPR to −50.1 dBc for all three CFR schemes at the 9 dB PAPR target.
